\## AgentWorkflow class



Base class for Workflows that integrate with Agents.



\### Type parameters



| Parameter | Description |

| - | - |

| `AgentType` | The Agent class type for typed RPC |

| `Params` | Parameters passed to the workflow |

| `ProgressType` | Type for progress reporting (defaults to `DefaultProgress`) |

| `Env` | Environment type (defaults to `Cloudflare.Env`) |



\### Properties



| Property | Type | Description |

| - | - | - |

| `agent` | Stub | Typed stub for calling Agent methods |

| `instanceId` | string | The workflow instance ID |

| `workflowName` | string | The workflow binding name |

| `env` | Env | Environment bindings |



\### Instance methods (non-durable)



These methods may repeat on retry. Use for lightweight, frequent updates.



\#### reportProgress(progress)



Report progress to the Agent. Triggers `onWorkflowProgress` callback.



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; await this.reportProgress({

&nbsp;   step: "processing",

&nbsp;   status: "running",

&nbsp;   percent: 0.5,

&nbsp; });

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; await this.reportProgress({

&nbsp;   step: "processing",

&nbsp;   status: "running",

&nbsp;   percent: 0.5,

&nbsp; });

&nbsp; ```



\#### broadcastToClients(message)



Broadcast a message to all WebSocket clients connected to the Agent.



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; this.broadcastToClients({ type: "update", data: result });

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; this.broadcastToClients({ type: "update", data: result });

&nbsp; ```



\#### waitForApproval(step, options?)



Wait for an approval event. Throws `WorkflowRejectedError` if rejected.



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; const approval = await this.waitForApproval(step, {

&nbsp;   timeout: "7 days",

&nbsp; });

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; const approval = await this.waitForApproval<{ approvedBy: string }>(step, {

&nbsp;   timeout: "7 days",

&nbsp; });

&nbsp; ```



\### Step methods (durable)



These methods are idempotent and will not repeat on retry. Use for state changes that must persist.



| Method | Description |

| - | - |

| `step.reportComplete(result?)` | Report successful completion |

| `step.reportError(error)` | Report an error |

| `step.sendEvent(event)` | Send a custom event to the Agent |

| `step.updateAgentState(state)` | Replace Agent state (broadcasts to clients) |

| `step.mergeAgentState(partial)` | Merge into Agent state (broadcasts to clients) |

| `step.resetAgentState()` | Reset Agent state to initialState |



\### DefaultProgress type



```ts

type DefaultProgress = {

&nbsp; step?: string;

&nbsp; status?: "pending" | "running" | "complete" | "error";

&nbsp; message?: string;

&nbsp; percent?: number;

&nbsp; \[key: string]: unknown;

};

```



\## Agent workflow methods



Methods available on the `Agent` class for Workflow management.



\### runWorkflow(workflowName, params, options?)



Start a workflow instance and track it in the Agent database.



\*\*Parameters:\*\*



| Parameter | Type | Description |

| - | - | - |

| `workflowName` | string | Workflow binding name from `env` |

| `params` | object | Parameters to pass to the workflow |

| `options.id` | string | Custom workflow ID (auto-generated if not provided) |

| `options.metadata` | object | Metadata stored for querying (not passed to workflow) |

| `options.agentBinding` | string | Agent binding name (auto-detected if not provided) |



\*\*Returns:\*\* `Promise<string>` - Workflow instance ID



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; const instanceId = await this.runWorkflow(

&nbsp;   "MY\_WORKFLOW",

&nbsp;   { taskId: "123" },

&nbsp;   {

&nbsp;     metadata: { userId: "user-456", priority: "high" },

&nbsp;   },

&nbsp; );

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; const instanceId = await this.runWorkflow(

&nbsp;   "MY\_WORKFLOW",

&nbsp;   { taskId: "123" },

&nbsp;   {

&nbsp;     metadata: { userId: "user-456", priority: "high" },

&nbsp;   },

&nbsp; );

&nbsp; ```



\### sendWorkflowEvent(workflowName, instanceId, event)



Send an event to a running workflow.



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; await this.sendWorkflowEvent("MY\_WORKFLOW", instanceId, {

&nbsp;   type: "custom-event",

&nbsp;   payload: { action: "proceed" },

&nbsp; });

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; await this.sendWorkflowEvent("MY\_WORKFLOW", instanceId, {

&nbsp;   type: "custom-event",

&nbsp;   payload: { action: "proceed" },

&nbsp; });

&nbsp; ```



\### getWorkflowStatus(workflowName, instanceId)



Get the status of a workflow and update the tracking record.



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; const status = await this.getWorkflowStatus("MY\_WORKFLOW", instanceId);

&nbsp; // { status: 'running', output: null, error: null }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; const status = await this.getWorkflowStatus("MY\_WORKFLOW", instanceId);

&nbsp; // { status: 'running', output: null, error: null }

&nbsp; ```



\### getWorkflow(instanceId)



Get a tracked workflow by ID.



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; const workflow = this.getWorkflow(instanceId);

&nbsp; // { instanceId, workflowName, status, metadata, error, createdAt, ... }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; const workflow = this.getWorkflow(instanceId);

&nbsp; // { instanceId, workflowName, status, metadata, error, createdAt, ... }

&nbsp; ```



\### getWorkflows(criteria?)



Query tracked workflows with cursor-based pagination. Returns a `WorkflowPage` with workflows, total count, and cursor for the next page.



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; // Get running workflows (default limit is 50, max is 100)

&nbsp; const { workflows, total } = this.getWorkflows({ status: "running" });





&nbsp; // Filter by metadata

&nbsp; const { workflows: userWorkflows } = this.getWorkflows({

&nbsp;   metadata: { userId: "user-456" },

&nbsp; });





&nbsp; // Pagination with cursor

&nbsp; const page1 = this.getWorkflows({

&nbsp;   status: \["complete", "errored"],

&nbsp;   limit: 20,

&nbsp;   orderBy: "desc",

&nbsp; });





&nbsp; console.log(`Showing ${page1.workflows.length} of ${page1.total} workflows`);





&nbsp; // Get next page using cursor

&nbsp; if (page1.nextCursor) {

&nbsp;   const page2 = this.getWorkflows({

&nbsp;     status: \["complete", "errored"],

&nbsp;     limit: 20,

&nbsp;     orderBy: "desc",

&nbsp;     cursor: page1.nextCursor,

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; // Get running workflows (default limit is 50, max is 100)

&nbsp; const { workflows, total } = this.getWorkflows({ status: "running" });





&nbsp; // Filter by metadata

&nbsp; const { workflows: userWorkflows } = this.getWorkflows({

&nbsp;   metadata: { userId: "user-456" },

&nbsp; });





&nbsp; // Pagination with cursor

&nbsp; const page1 = this.getWorkflows({

&nbsp;   status: \["complete", "errored"],

&nbsp;   limit: 20,

&nbsp;   orderBy: "desc",

&nbsp; });





&nbsp; console.log(`Showing ${page1.workflows.length} of ${page1.total} workflows`);





&nbsp; // Get next page using cursor

&nbsp; if (page1.nextCursor) {

&nbsp;   const page2 = this.getWorkflows({

&nbsp;     status: \["complete", "errored"],

&nbsp;     limit: 20,

&nbsp;     orderBy: "desc",

&nbsp;     cursor: page1.nextCursor,

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



The `WorkflowPage` type:



```ts

type WorkflowPage = {

&nbsp; workflows: WorkflowInfo\[];

&nbsp; total: number; // Total matching workflows

&nbsp; nextCursor: string | null; // null when no more pages

};

```



\### deleteWorkflow(instanceId)



Delete a single workflow instance tracking record. Returns `true` if deleted, `false` if not found.



\### deleteWorkflows(criteria?)



Delete workflow instance tracking records matching criteria.



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; // Delete completed workflow instances older than 7 days

&nbsp; this.deleteWorkflows({

&nbsp;   status: "complete",

&nbsp;   createdBefore: new Date(Date.now() - 7 \* 24 \* 60 \* 60 \* 1000),

&nbsp; });





&nbsp; // Delete all errored and terminated workflows

&nbsp; this.deleteWorkflows({

&nbsp;   status: \["errored", "terminated"],

&nbsp; });

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; // Delete completed workflow instances older than 7 days

&nbsp; this.deleteWorkflows({

&nbsp;   status: "complete",

&nbsp;   createdBefore: new Date(Date.now() - 7 \* 24 \* 60 \* 60 \* 1000),

&nbsp; });





&nbsp; // Delete all errored and terminated workflows

&nbsp; this.deleteWorkflows({

&nbsp;   status: \["errored", "terminated"],

&nbsp; });

&nbsp; ```



\### terminateWorkflow(instanceId)



Terminate a running workflow immediately. Sets status to `"terminated"`.



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; await this.terminateWorkflow(instanceId);

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; await this.terminateWorkflow(instanceId);

&nbsp; ```



Note



`terminate()` is not yet supported in local development with `wrangler dev`. It works when deployed to Cloudflare.



\### pauseWorkflow(instanceId)



Pause a running workflow. The workflow can be resumed later with `resumeWorkflow()`.



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; await this.pauseWorkflow(instanceId);

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; await this.pauseWorkflow(instanceId);

&nbsp; ```



Note



`pause()` is not yet supported in local development with `wrangler dev`. It works when deployed to Cloudflare.



\### resumeWorkflow(instanceId)



Resume a paused workflow.



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; await this.resumeWorkflow(instanceId);

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; await this.resumeWorkflow(instanceId);

&nbsp; ```



Note



`resume()` is not yet supported in local development with `wrangler dev`. It works when deployed to Cloudflare.



\### restartWorkflow(instanceId, options?)



Restart a workflow instance from the beginning with the same ID.



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; // Reset tracking (default) - clears timestamps and error fields

&nbsp; await this.restartWorkflow(instanceId);





&nbsp; // Preserve original timestamps

&nbsp; await this.restartWorkflow(instanceId, { resetTracking: false });

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; // Reset tracking (default) - clears timestamps and error fields

&nbsp; await this.restartWorkflow(instanceId);





&nbsp; // Preserve original timestamps

&nbsp; await this.restartWorkflow(instanceId, { resetTracking: false });

&nbsp; ```



Note



`restart()` is not yet supported in local development with `wrangler dev`. It works when deployed to Cloudflare.



\### approveWorkflow(instanceId, options?)



Approve a waiting workflow. Use with `waitForApproval()` in the workflow.



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; await this.approveWorkflow(instanceId, {

&nbsp;   reason: "Approved by admin",

&nbsp;   metadata: { approvedBy: userId },

&nbsp; });

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; await this.approveWorkflow(instanceId, {

&nbsp;   reason: "Approved by admin",

&nbsp;   metadata: { approvedBy: userId },

&nbsp; });

&nbsp; ```



\### rejectWorkflow(instanceId, options?)



Reject a waiting workflow. Causes `waitForApproval()` to throw `WorkflowRejectedError`.



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; await this.rejectWorkflow(instanceId, { reason: "Request denied" });

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; await this.rejectWorkflow(instanceId, { reason: "Request denied" });

&nbsp; ```



\### migrateWorkflowBinding(oldName, newName)



Migrate tracked workflows after renaming a workflow binding.



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; class MyAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   async onStart() {

&nbsp;     this.migrateWorkflowBinding("OLD\_WORKFLOW", "NEW\_WORKFLOW");

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; class MyAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   async onStart() {

&nbsp;     this.migrateWorkflowBinding("OLD\_WORKFLOW", "NEW\_WORKFLOW");

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\## Lifecycle callbacks



Override these methods in your Agent to handle workflow events:



| Callback | Parameters | Description |

| - | - | - |

| `onWorkflowProgress` | `workflowName`, `instanceId`, `progress` | Called when workflow reports progress |

| `onWorkflowComplete` | `workflowName`, `instanceId`, `result?` | Called when workflow completes |

| `onWorkflowError` | `workflowName`, `instanceId`, `error` | Called when workflow errors |

| `onWorkflowEvent` | `workflowName`, `instanceId`, `event` | Called when workflow sends an event |

| `onWorkflowCallback` | `callback: WorkflowCallback` | Called for all callback types |



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; class MyAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   async onWorkflowProgress(workflowName, instanceId, progress) {

&nbsp;     this.broadcast(

&nbsp;       JSON.stringify({ type: "progress", workflowName, instanceId, progress }),

&nbsp;     );

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   async onWorkflowComplete(workflowName, instanceId, result) {

&nbsp;     console.log(`${workflowName}/${instanceId} completed`);

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   async onWorkflowError(workflowName, instanceId, error) {

&nbsp;     console.error(`${workflowName}/${instanceId} failed:`, error);

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; class MyAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   async onWorkflowProgress(

&nbsp;     workflowName: string,

&nbsp;     instanceId: string,

&nbsp;     progress: unknown,

&nbsp;   ) {

&nbsp;     this.broadcast(

&nbsp;       JSON.stringify({ type: "progress", workflowName, instanceId, progress }),

&nbsp;     );

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   async onWorkflowComplete(

&nbsp;     workflowName: string,

&nbsp;     instanceId: string,

&nbsp;     result?: unknown,

&nbsp;   ) {

&nbsp;     console.log(`${workflowName}/${instanceId} completed`);

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   async onWorkflowError(

&nbsp;     workflowName: string,

&nbsp;     instanceId: string,

&nbsp;     error: string,

&nbsp;   ) {

&nbsp;     console.error(`${workflowName}/${instanceId} failed:`, error);

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\## Workflow tracking



Workflows started with `runWorkflow()` are automatically tracked in the Agent's internal database. You can query, filter, and manage workflows using the methods described above (`getWorkflow()`, `getWorkflows()`, `deleteWorkflow()`, etc.).



\### Status values



| Status | Description |

| - | - |

| `queued` | Waiting to start |

| `running` | Currently executing |

| `paused` | Paused by user |

| `waiting` | Waiting for event |

| `complete` | Finished successfully |

| `errored` | Failed with error |

| `terminated` | Manually terminated |



Use the `metadata` option in `runWorkflow()` to store queryable information (like user IDs or task types) that you can filter on later with `getWorkflows()`.



\## Examples



\### Human-in-the-loop approval



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; import { AgentWorkflow } from "agents/workflows";

&nbsp; export class ApprovalWorkflow extends AgentWorkflow {

&nbsp;   async run(event, step) {

&nbsp;     const request = await step.do("prepare", async () => {

&nbsp;       return { ...event.payload, preparedAt: Date.now() };

&nbsp;     });





&nbsp;     await this.reportProgress({

&nbsp;       step: "approval",

&nbsp;       status: "pending",

&nbsp;       message: "Awaiting approval",

&nbsp;     });





&nbsp;     // Throws WorkflowRejectedError if rejected

&nbsp;     const approval = await this.waitForApproval(step, {

&nbsp;       timeout: "7 days",

&nbsp;     });





&nbsp;     console.log("Approved by:", approval?.approvedBy);





&nbsp;     const result = await step.do("execute", async () => {

&nbsp;       return executeRequest(request);

&nbsp;     });





&nbsp;     await step.reportComplete(result);

&nbsp;     return result;

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }





&nbsp; class MyAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   async handleApproval(instanceId, userId) {

&nbsp;     await this.approveWorkflow(instanceId, {

&nbsp;       reason: "Approved by admin",

&nbsp;       metadata: { approvedBy: userId },

&nbsp;     });

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   async handleRejection(instanceId, reason) {

&nbsp;     await this.rejectWorkflow(instanceId, { reason });

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; import { AgentWorkflow } from "agents/workflows";

&nbsp; import type { AgentWorkflowEvent, AgentWorkflowStep } from "agents/workflows";





&nbsp; export class ApprovalWorkflow extends AgentWorkflow<MyAgent, RequestParams> {

&nbsp;   async run(event: AgentWorkflowEvent<RequestParams>, step: AgentWorkflowStep) {

&nbsp;     const request = await step.do("prepare", async () => {

&nbsp;       return { ...event.payload, preparedAt: Date.now() };

&nbsp;     });





&nbsp;     await this.reportProgress({

&nbsp;       step: "approval",

&nbsp;       status: "pending",

&nbsp;       message: "Awaiting approval",

&nbsp;     });





&nbsp;     // Throws WorkflowRejectedError if rejected

&nbsp;     const approval = await this.waitForApproval<{ approvedBy: string }>(step, {

&nbsp;       timeout: "7 days",

&nbsp;     });





&nbsp;     console.log("Approved by:", approval?.approvedBy);





&nbsp;     const result = await step.do("execute", async () => {

&nbsp;       return executeRequest(request);

&nbsp;     });





&nbsp;     await step.reportComplete(result);

&nbsp;     return result;

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }





&nbsp; class MyAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   async handleApproval(instanceId: string, userId: string) {

&nbsp;     await this.approveWorkflow(instanceId, {

&nbsp;       reason: "Approved by admin",

&nbsp;       metadata: { approvedBy: userId },

&nbsp;     });

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   async handleRejection(instanceId: string, reason: string) {

&nbsp;     await this.rejectWorkflow(instanceId, { reason });

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\### Retry with backoff



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; import { AgentWorkflow } from "agents/workflows";

&nbsp; export class ResilientWorkflow extends AgentWorkflow {

&nbsp;   async run(event, step) {

&nbsp;     const result = await step.do(

&nbsp;       "call-api",

&nbsp;       {

&nbsp;         retries: { limit: 5, delay: "10 seconds", backoff: "exponential" },

&nbsp;         timeout: "5 minutes",

&nbsp;       },

&nbsp;       async () => {

&nbsp;         const response = await fetch("https://api.example.com/process", {

&nbsp;           method: "POST",

&nbsp;           body: JSON.stringify(event.payload),

&nbsp;         });

&nbsp;         if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`API error: ${response.status}`);

&nbsp;         return response.json();

&nbsp;       },

&nbsp;     );





&nbsp;     await step.reportComplete(result);

&nbsp;     return result;

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; import { AgentWorkflow } from "agents/workflows";

&nbsp; import type { AgentWorkflowEvent, AgentWorkflowStep } from "agents/workflows";





&nbsp; export class ResilientWorkflow extends AgentWorkflow<MyAgent, TaskParams> {

&nbsp;   async run(event: AgentWorkflowEvent<TaskParams>, step: AgentWorkflowStep) {

&nbsp;     const result = await step.do(

&nbsp;       "call-api",

&nbsp;       {

&nbsp;         retries: { limit: 5, delay: "10 seconds", backoff: "exponential" },

&nbsp;         timeout: "5 minutes",

&nbsp;       },

&nbsp;       async () => {

&nbsp;         const response = await fetch("https://api.example.com/process", {

&nbsp;           method: "POST",

&nbsp;           body: JSON.stringify(event.payload),

&nbsp;         });

&nbsp;         if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`API error: ${response.status}`);

&nbsp;         return response.json();

&nbsp;       },

&nbsp;     );





&nbsp;     await step.reportComplete(result);

&nbsp;     return result;

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\### State synchronization



Workflows can update Agent state durably via `step`, which automatically broadcasts to all connected clients:



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; import { AgentWorkflow } from "agents/workflows";

&nbsp; export class StatefulWorkflow extends AgentWorkflow {

&nbsp;   async run(event, step) {

&nbsp;     // Replace entire state (durable, broadcasts to clients)

&nbsp;     await step.updateAgentState({

&nbsp;       currentTask: {

&nbsp;         id: event.payload.taskId,

&nbsp;         status: "processing",

&nbsp;         startedAt: Date.now(),

&nbsp;       },

&nbsp;     });





&nbsp;     const result = await step.do("process", async () =>

&nbsp;       processTask(event.payload),

&nbsp;     );





&nbsp;     // Merge partial state (durable, keeps existing fields)

&nbsp;     await step.mergeAgentState({

&nbsp;       currentTask: { status: "complete", result, completedAt: Date.now() },

&nbsp;     });





&nbsp;     await step.reportComplete(result);

&nbsp;     return result;

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; import { AgentWorkflow } from "agents/workflows";

&nbsp; import type { AgentWorkflowEvent, AgentWorkflowStep } from "agents/workflows";





&nbsp; export class StatefulWorkflow extends AgentWorkflow<MyAgent, TaskParams> {

&nbsp;   async run(event: AgentWorkflowEvent<TaskParams>, step: AgentWorkflowStep) {

&nbsp;     // Replace entire state (durable, broadcasts to clients)

&nbsp;     await step.updateAgentState({

&nbsp;       currentTask: {

&nbsp;         id: event.payload.taskId,

&nbsp;         status: "processing",

&nbsp;         startedAt: Date.now(),

&nbsp;       },

&nbsp;     });





&nbsp;     const result = await step.do("process", async () =>

&nbsp;       processTask(event.payload),

&nbsp;     );





&nbsp;     // Merge partial state (durable, keeps existing fields)

&nbsp;     await step.mergeAgentState({

&nbsp;       currentTask: { status: "complete", result, completedAt: Date.now() },

&nbsp;     });





&nbsp;     await step.reportComplete(result);

&nbsp;     return result;

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\### Custom progress types



Define custom progress types for domain-specific reporting:



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; import { AgentWorkflow } from "agents/workflows";

&nbsp; // Custom progress type for data pipeline

&nbsp; // Workflow with custom progress type (3rd type parameter)

&nbsp; export class ETLWorkflow extends AgentWorkflow {

&nbsp;   async run(event, step) {

&nbsp;     await this.reportProgress({

&nbsp;       stage: "extract",

&nbsp;       recordsProcessed: 0,

&nbsp;       totalRecords: 1000,

&nbsp;       currentTable: "users",

&nbsp;     });





&nbsp;     // ... processing

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }





&nbsp; // Agent receives typed progress

&nbsp; class MyAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   async onWorkflowProgress(workflowName, instanceId, progress) {

&nbsp;     const p = progress;

&nbsp;     console.log(`Stage: ${p.stage}, ${p.recordsProcessed}/${p.totalRecords}`);

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; import { AgentWorkflow } from "agents/workflows";

&nbsp; import type { AgentWorkflowEvent, AgentWorkflowStep } from "agents/workflows";





&nbsp; // Custom progress type for data pipeline

&nbsp; type PipelineProgress = {

&nbsp;   stage: "extract" | "transform" | "load";

&nbsp;   recordsProcessed: number;

&nbsp;   totalRecords: number;

&nbsp;   currentTable?: string;

&nbsp; };





&nbsp; // Workflow with custom progress type (3rd type parameter)

&nbsp; export class ETLWorkflow extends AgentWorkflow<

&nbsp;   MyAgent,

&nbsp;   ETLParams,

&nbsp;   PipelineProgress

&nbsp; > {

&nbsp;   async run(event: AgentWorkflowEvent<ETLParams>, step: AgentWorkflowStep) {

&nbsp;     await this.reportProgress({

&nbsp;       stage: "extract",

&nbsp;       recordsProcessed: 0,

&nbsp;       totalRecords: 1000,

&nbsp;       currentTable: "users",

&nbsp;     });





&nbsp;     // ... processing

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }





&nbsp; // Agent receives typed progress

&nbsp; class MyAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   async onWorkflowProgress(

&nbsp;     workflowName: string,

&nbsp;     instanceId: string,

&nbsp;     progress: unknown,

&nbsp;   ) {

&nbsp;     const p = progress as PipelineProgress;

&nbsp;     console.log(`Stage: ${p.stage}, ${p.recordsProcessed}/${p.totalRecords}`);

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\### Cleanup strategy



The internal `cf\_agents\_workflows` table can grow unbounded, so implement a retention policy:



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; class MyAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   // Option 1: Delete on completion

&nbsp;   async onWorkflowComplete(workflowName, instanceId, result) {

&nbsp;     // Process result first, then delete

&nbsp;     this.deleteWorkflow(instanceId);

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   // Option 2: Scheduled cleanup (keep recent history)

&nbsp;   async cleanupOldWorkflows() {

&nbsp;     this.deleteWorkflows({

&nbsp;       status: \["complete", "errored"],

&nbsp;       createdBefore: new Date(Date.now() - 7 \* 24 \* 60 \* 60 \* 1000),

&nbsp;     });

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   // Option 3: Keep all history for compliance/auditing

&nbsp;   // Don't call deleteWorkflows() - query historical data as needed

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; class MyAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   // Option 1: Delete on completion

&nbsp;   async onWorkflowComplete(

&nbsp;     workflowName: string,

&nbsp;     instanceId: string,

&nbsp;     result?: unknown,

&nbsp;   ) {

&nbsp;     // Process result first, then delete

&nbsp;     this.deleteWorkflow(instanceId);

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   // Option 2: Scheduled cleanup (keep recent history)

&nbsp;   async cleanupOldWorkflows() {

&nbsp;     this.deleteWorkflows({

&nbsp;       status: \["complete", "errored"],

&nbsp;       createdBefore: new Date(Date.now() - 7 \* 24 \* 60 \* 60 \* 1000),

&nbsp;     });

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   // Option 3: Keep all history for compliance/auditing

&nbsp;   // Don't call deleteWorkflows() - query historical data as needed

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\## Bidirectional communication



\### Workflow to Agent



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; // Direct RPC call (typed)

&nbsp; await this.agent.updateTaskStatus(taskId, "processing");

&nbsp; const data = await this.agent.getData(taskId);





&nbsp; // Non-durable callbacks (may repeat on retry, use for frequent updates)

&nbsp; await this.reportProgress({ step: "process", percent: 0.5 });

&nbsp; this.broadcastToClients({ type: "update", data });





&nbsp; // Durable callbacks via step (idempotent, won't repeat on retry)

&nbsp; await step.reportComplete(result);

&nbsp; await step.reportError("Something went wrong");

&nbsp; await step.sendEvent({ type: "custom", data: {} });





&nbsp; // Durable state synchronization via step (broadcasts to clients)

&nbsp; await step.updateAgentState({ status: "processing" });

&nbsp; await step.mergeAgentState({ progress: 0.5 });

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; // Direct RPC call (typed)

&nbsp; await this.agent.updateTaskStatus(taskId, "processing");

&nbsp; const data = await this.agent.getData(taskId);





&nbsp; // Non-durable callbacks (may repeat on retry, use for frequent updates)

&nbsp; await this.reportProgress({ step: "process", percent: 0.5 });

&nbsp; this.broadcastToClients({ type: "update", data });





&nbsp; // Durable callbacks via step (idempotent, won't repeat on retry)

&nbsp; await step.reportComplete(result);

&nbsp; await step.reportError("Something went wrong");

&nbsp; await step.sendEvent({ type: "custom", data: {} });





&nbsp; // Durable state synchronization via step (broadcasts to clients)

&nbsp; await step.updateAgentState({ status: "processing" });

&nbsp; await step.mergeAgentState({ progress: 0.5 });

&nbsp; ```



\### Agent to Workflow



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; // Send event to waiting workflow

&nbsp; await this.sendWorkflowEvent("MY\_WORKFLOW", instanceId, {

&nbsp;   type: "custom-event",

&nbsp;   payload: { action: "proceed" },

&nbsp; });





&nbsp; // Approve/reject workflows using convenience methods

&nbsp; await this.approveWorkflow(instanceId, {

&nbsp;   reason: "Approved by admin",

&nbsp;   metadata: { approvedBy: userId },

&nbsp; });





&nbsp; await this.rejectWorkflow(instanceId, { reason: "Request denied" });

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; // Send event to waiting workflow

&nbsp; await this.sendWorkflowEvent("MY\_WORKFLOW", instanceId, {

&nbsp;   type: "custom-event",

&nbsp;   payload: { action: "proceed" },

&nbsp; });





&nbsp; // Approve/reject workflows using convenience methods

&nbsp; await this.approveWorkflow(instanceId, {

&nbsp;   reason: "Approved by admin",

&nbsp;   metadata: { approvedBy: userId },

&nbsp; });





&nbsp; await this.rejectWorkflow(instanceId, { reason: "Request denied" });

&nbsp; ```



\## Best practices



1\. \*\*Keep workflows focused\*\* — One workflow per logical task

2\. \*\*Use meaningful step names\*\* — Helps with debugging and observability

3\. \*\*Report progress regularly\*\* — Keeps users informed

4\. \*\*Handle errors gracefully\*\* — Use `reportError()` before throwing

5\. \*\*Clean up completed workflows\*\* — Implement a retention policy for the tracking table

6\. \*\*Handle workflow binding renames\*\* — Use `migrateWorkflowBinding()` when renaming workflow bindings in `wrangler.jsonc`



\## Limitations



| Constraint | Limit |

| - | - |

| Maximum steps | 1,024 per workflow |

| State size | 10 MB per workflow |

| Event wait time | 1 year maximum |

| Step execution time | 30 minutes per step |



Workflows cannot open WebSocket connections directly. Use `broadcastToClients()` to communicate with connected clients through the Agent.



\## Related resources



\* \[Workflows documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workflows/)

\* \[Store and sync state](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/store-and-sync-state/)

\* \[Schedule tasks](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/schedule-tasks/)

\* \[Human-in-the-loop patterns](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/concepts/human-in-the-loop/)



</page>

title: Schedule tasks · Cloudflare Agents docs

description: An Agent can schedule tasks to be run in the future by calling

&nbsp; this.schedule(when, callback, data), where when can be a delay, a Date, or a

&nbsp; cron string; callback the function name to call, and data is an object of data

&nbsp; to pass to the function.

lastUpdated: 2026-01-16T14:17:46.000Z

chatbotDeprioritize: false

source\_url:

&nbsp; html: https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/schedule-tasks/

&nbsp; md: https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/schedule-tasks/index.md

---



An Agent can schedule tasks to be run in the future by calling `this.schedule(when, callback, data)`, where `when` can be a delay, a `Date`, or a cron string; `callback` the function name to call, and `data` is an object of data to pass to the function.



Scheduled tasks can do anything a request or message from a user can: make requests, query databases, send emails, read+write state: scheduled tasks can invoke any regular method on your Agent.



Calling destroy() in scheduled tasks



You can safely call `this.destroy()` within a scheduled task callback. The Agent will properly handle cleanup and eviction, skipping any remaining database updates after the destroy flag is set.



\### Scheduling tasks



You can call `this.schedule` within any method on an Agent, and schedule tens-of-thousands of tasks per individual Agent:



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; import { Agent } from "agents";





&nbsp; export class SchedulingAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   async onRequest(request) {

&nbsp;     // Handle an incoming request

&nbsp;     // Schedule a task 10 minutes from now

&nbsp;     // Calls the "checkFlights" method

&nbsp;     let { taskId } = await this.schedule(600, "checkFlights", {

&nbsp;       flight: "DL264",

&nbsp;       date: "2025-02-23",

&nbsp;     });

&nbsp;     return Response.json({ taskId });

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   async checkFlights(data) {

&nbsp;     // Invoked when our scheduled task runs

&nbsp;     // We can also call this.schedule here to schedule another task

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; import { Agent } from "agents"





&nbsp; export class SchedulingAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   async onRequest(request) {

&nbsp;     // Handle an incoming request

&nbsp;     // Schedule a task 10 minutes from now

&nbsp;     // Calls the "checkFlights" method

&nbsp;     let { taskId } = await this.schedule(600, "checkFlights", { flight: "DL264", date: "2025-02-23" });

&nbsp;     return Response.json({ taskId });

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   async checkFlights(data) {

&nbsp;     // Invoked when our scheduled task runs

&nbsp;     // We can also call this.schedule here to schedule another task

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



Warning



Tasks that set a callback for a method that does not exist will throw an exception: ensure that the method named in the `callback` argument of `this.schedule` exists on your `Agent` class.



You can schedule tasks in multiple ways:



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; // schedule a task to run immediately

&nbsp; let task = await this.schedule(0, "someTask", { message: "hello" });





&nbsp; // schedule a task to run in 10 seconds

&nbsp; let task = await this.schedule(10, "someTask", { message: "hello" });





&nbsp; // schedule a task to run at a specific date

&nbsp; let task = await this.schedule(new Date("2025-01-01"), "someTask", {});





&nbsp; // schedule a task to run every 10 minutes

&nbsp; let { id } = await this.schedule("\*/10 \* \* \* \*", "someTask", {

&nbsp;   message: "hello",

&nbsp; });





&nbsp; // schedule a task to run every 10 minutes, but only on Mondays

&nbsp; let task = await this.schedule("\*/10 \* \* \* 1", "someTask", {

&nbsp;   message: "hello",

&nbsp; });





&nbsp; // cancel a scheduled task

&nbsp; this.cancelSchedule(task.id);

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; // schedule a task to run immediately

&nbsp; let task = await this.schedule(0, "someTask", { message: "hello" });





&nbsp; // schedule a task to run in 10 seconds

&nbsp; let task = await this.schedule(10, "someTask", { message: "hello" });





&nbsp; // schedule a task to run at a specific date

&nbsp; let task = await this.schedule(new Date("2025-01-01"), "someTask", {});





&nbsp; // schedule a task to run every 10 minutes

&nbsp; let { id } = await this.schedule("\*/10 \* \* \* \*", "someTask", { message: "hello" });





&nbsp; // schedule a task to run every 10 minutes, but only on Mondays

&nbsp; let task = await this.schedule("\*/10 \* \* \* 1", "someTask", { message: "hello" });





&nbsp; // cancel a scheduled task

&nbsp; this.cancelSchedule(task.id);

&nbsp; ```



Calling `await this.schedule` returns a `Schedule`, which includes the task's randomly generated `id`. You can use this `id` to retrieve or cancel the task in the future. It also provides a `type` property that indicates the type of schedule, for example, one of `"scheduled" | "delayed" | "cron"`.



Maximum scheduled tasks



Each task is mapped to a row in the Agent's underlying \[SQLite database](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/sqlite-storage-api/), which means that each task can be up to 2 MB in size. The maximum number of tasks must be `(task\_size \* tasks) + all\_other\_state < maximum\_database\_size` (currently 1GB per Agent).



Destroying an Agent from a scheduled task



You can safely call `this.destroy()` from within a scheduled task callback. The Agent SDK handles this scenario by setting an internal flag to prevent database updates after destruction and deferring the context abort to allow the alarm handler to complete cleanly. This prevents errors that would otherwise occur when the alarm handler attempts to update the schedule table after storage has been cleared.



\### Managing scheduled tasks



You can get, cancel and filter across scheduled tasks within an Agent using the scheduling API:



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; // Get a specific schedule by ID

&nbsp; // Returns undefined if the task does not exist

&nbsp; let task = await this.getSchedule(task.id);





&nbsp; // Get all scheduled tasks

&nbsp; // Returns an array of Schedule objects

&nbsp; let tasks = this.getSchedules();





&nbsp; // Cancel a task by its ID

&nbsp; // Returns true if the task was cancelled, false if it did not exist

&nbsp; await this.cancelSchedule(task.id);





&nbsp; // Filter for specific tasks

&nbsp; // e.g. all tasks starting in the next hour

&nbsp; let tasks = this.getSchedules({

&nbsp;   timeRange: {

&nbsp;     start: new Date(Date.now()),

&nbsp;     end: new Date(Date.now() + 60 \* 60 \* 1000),

&nbsp;   },

&nbsp; });

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; // Get a specific schedule by ID

&nbsp; // Returns undefined if the task does not exist

&nbsp; let task = await this.getSchedule(task.id)





&nbsp; // Get all scheduled tasks

&nbsp; // Returns an array of Schedule objects

&nbsp; let tasks = this.getSchedules();





&nbsp; // Cancel a task by its ID

&nbsp; // Returns true if the task was cancelled, false if it did not exist

&nbsp; await this.cancelSchedule(task.id);





&nbsp; // Filter for specific tasks

&nbsp; // e.g. all tasks starting in the next hour

&nbsp; let tasks = this.getSchedules({

&nbsp;   timeRange: {

&nbsp;     start: new Date(Date.now()),

&nbsp;     end: new Date(Date.now() + 60 \* 60 \* 1000),

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; });

&nbsp; ```



\### Lifecycle management with scheduled tasks



When working with scheduled tasks, you can safely call `this.destroy()` from within a scheduled callback to terminate the Agent instance after completing a task. The Agent SDK properly handles the cleanup process to ensure scheduled tasks complete successfully before the Agent is evicted.



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; export class SchedulingAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   async onRequest(request) {

&nbsp;     // Schedule a self-destructing task

&nbsp;     await this.schedule(60, "cleanupAndDestroy");

&nbsp;     return new Response("Agent will self-destruct in 60 seconds");

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   async cleanupAndDestroy(data) {

&nbsp;     // Perform final cleanup operations

&nbsp;     await this.sendEmail({

&nbsp;       to: "admin@example.com",

&nbsp;       subject: "Task completed",

&nbsp;       body: "Agent task finished, shutting down",

&nbsp;     });





&nbsp;     // Safely destroy the Agent instance

&nbsp;     // The destroy operation will complete after this callback finishes

&nbsp;     await this.destroy();

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; export class SchedulingAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   async onRequest(request) {

&nbsp;     // Schedule a self-destructing task

&nbsp;     await this.schedule(60, "cleanupAndDestroy");

&nbsp;     return new Response("Agent will self-destruct in 60 seconds");

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   async cleanupAndDestroy(data) {

&nbsp;     // Perform final cleanup operations

&nbsp;     await this.sendEmail({

&nbsp;       to: "admin@example.com",

&nbsp;       subject: "Task completed",

&nbsp;       body: "Agent task finished, shutting down"

&nbsp;     });





&nbsp;     // Safely destroy the Agent instance

&nbsp;     // The destroy operation will complete after this callback finishes

&nbsp;     await this.destroy();

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



Note



When `destroy()` is called from within a scheduled task, the Agent SDK defers the destruction to ensure the scheduled callback completes successfully. The Agent instance will be evicted immediately after the callback finishes executing.



</page>

title: Store and sync state · Cloudflare Agents docs

description: Every Agent has built-in state management capabilities, including

&nbsp; built-in storage and synchronization between the Agent and frontend

&nbsp; applications.

lastUpdated: 2025-10-23T15:22:15.000Z

chatbotDeprioritize: false

source\_url:

&nbsp; html: https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/store-and-sync-state/

&nbsp; md: https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/store-and-sync-state/index.md

---



Every Agent has built-in state management capabilities, including built-in storage and synchronization between the Agent and frontend applications.



State within an Agent is:



\* Persisted across Agent restarts: data is permanently stored within an Agent.

\* Automatically serialized/deserialized: you can store any JSON-serializable data.

\* Immediately consistent within the Agent: read your own writes.

\* Thread-safe for concurrent updates

\* Fast: state is colocated wherever the Agent is running. Reads and writes do not need to traverse the network.



Agent state is stored in a SQL database that is embedded within each individual Agent instance: you can interact with it using the higher-level `this.setState` API (recommended), which allows you to sync state and trigger events on state changes, or by directly querying the database with `this.sql`.



\#### State API



Every Agent has built-in state management capabilities. You can set and update the Agent's state directly using `this.setState`:



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; import { Agent } from "agents";





&nbsp; export class MyAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   // Update state in response to events

&nbsp;   async incrementCounter() {

&nbsp;     this.setState({

&nbsp;       ...this.state,

&nbsp;       counter: this.state.counter + 1,

&nbsp;     });

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   // Handle incoming messages

&nbsp;   async onMessage(message) {

&nbsp;     if (message.type === "update") {

&nbsp;       this.setState({

&nbsp;         ...this.state,

&nbsp;         ...message.data,

&nbsp;       });

&nbsp;     }

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   // Handle state updates

&nbsp;   onStateUpdate(state, source) {

&nbsp;     console.log("state updated", state);

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; import { Agent } from "agents";





&nbsp; export class MyAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   // Update state in response to events

&nbsp;   async incrementCounter() {

&nbsp;     this.setState({

&nbsp;       ...this.state,

&nbsp;       counter: this.state.counter + 1,

&nbsp;     });

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   // Handle incoming messages

&nbsp;   async onMessage(message) {

&nbsp;     if (message.type === "update") {

&nbsp;       this.setState({

&nbsp;         ...this.state,

&nbsp;         ...message.data,

&nbsp;       });

&nbsp;     }

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   // Handle state updates

&nbsp;   onStateUpdate(state, source: "server" | Connection) {

&nbsp;     console.log("state updated", state);

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



If you're using TypeScript, you can also provide a type for your Agent's state by passing in a type as a \[type parameter](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/2/generics.html#using-type-parameters-in-generic-constraints) as the \*second\* type parameter to the `Agent` class definition.



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; import { Agent } from "agents";





&nbsp; // Define a type for your Agent's state

&nbsp; // Pass in the type of your Agent's state

&nbsp; export class MyAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   // This allows this.setState and the onStateUpdate method to

&nbsp;   // be typed:

&nbsp;   async onStateUpdate(state) {

&nbsp;     console.log("state updated", state);

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   async someOtherMethod() {

&nbsp;     this.setState({

&nbsp;       ...this.state,

&nbsp;       price: this.state.price + 10,

&nbsp;     });

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; import { Agent } from "agents";





&nbsp; interface Env {}





&nbsp; // Define a type for your Agent's state

&nbsp; interface FlightRecord {

&nbsp;   id: string;

&nbsp;   departureIata: string;

&nbsp;   arrival: Date;

&nbsp;   arrivalIata: string;

&nbsp;   price: number;

&nbsp; }





&nbsp; // Pass in the type of your Agent's state

&nbsp; export class MyAgent extends Agent<Env, FlightRecord> {

&nbsp;   // This allows this.setState and the onStateUpdate method to

&nbsp;   // be typed:

&nbsp;    async onStateUpdate(state: FlightRecord) {

&nbsp;     console.log("state updated", state);

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   async someOtherMethod() {

&nbsp;     this.setState({

&nbsp;       ...this.state,

&nbsp;       price: this.state.price + 10,

&nbsp;     });

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\### Set the initial state for an Agent



You can also set the initial state for an Agent via the `initialState` property on the `Agent` class:



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; class MyAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   // Set a default, initial state

&nbsp;   initialState = {

&nbsp;     counter: 0,

&nbsp;     text: "",

&nbsp;     color: "#3B82F6",

&nbsp;   };





&nbsp;   doSomething() {

&nbsp;     console.log(this.state); // {counter: 0, text: "", color: "#3B82F6"}, if you haven't set the state yet

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; type State = {

&nbsp;   counter: number;

&nbsp;   text: string;

&nbsp;   color: string;

&nbsp; };





&nbsp; class MyAgent extends Agent<Env, State> {

&nbsp;   // Set a default, initial state

&nbsp;   initialState = {

&nbsp;     counter: 0,

&nbsp;     text: "",

&nbsp;     color: "#3B82F6",

&nbsp;   };





&nbsp;   doSomething() {

&nbsp;     console.log(this.state); // {counter: 0, text: "", color: "#3B82F6"}, if you haven't set the state yet

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



Any initial state is synced to clients connecting via \[the `useAgent` hook](#synchronizing-state).



\### Synchronizing state



Clients can connect to an Agent and stay synchronized with its state using the React hooks provided as part of `agents/react`.



A React application can call `useAgent` to connect to a named Agent over WebSockets at



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; import { useState } from "react";

&nbsp; import { useAgent } from "agents/react";





&nbsp; function StateInterface() {

&nbsp;   const \[state, setState] = useState({ counter: 0 });





&nbsp;   const agent = useAgent({

&nbsp;     agent: "thinking-agent",

&nbsp;     name: "my-agent",

&nbsp;     onStateUpdate: (newState) => setState(newState),

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   const increment = () => {

&nbsp;     agent.setState({ counter: state.counter + 1 });

&nbsp;   };





&nbsp;   return (

&nbsp;     <div>

&nbsp;       <div>Count: {state.counter}</div>

&nbsp;       <button onClick={increment}>Increment</button>

&nbsp;     </div>

&nbsp;   );

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; import { useState } from "react";

&nbsp; import { useAgent } from "agents/react";





&nbsp; function StateInterface() {

&nbsp;   const \[state, setState] = useState({ counter: 0 });





&nbsp;   const agent = useAgent({

&nbsp;     agent: "thinking-agent",

&nbsp;     name: "my-agent",

&nbsp;     onStateUpdate: (newState) => setState(newState),

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   const increment = () => {

&nbsp;     agent.setState({ counter: state.counter + 1 });

&nbsp;   };





&nbsp;   return (

&nbsp;     <div>

&nbsp;       <div>Count: {state.counter}</div>

&nbsp;       <button onClick={increment}>Increment</button>

&nbsp;     </div>

&nbsp;   );

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



The state synchronization system:



\* Automatically syncs the Agent's state to all connected clients

\* Handles client disconnections and reconnections gracefully

\* Provides immediate local updates

\* Supports multiple simultaneous client connections



Common use cases:



\* Real-time collaborative features

\* Multi-window/tab synchronization

\* Live updates across multiple devices

\* Maintaining consistent UI state across clients

\* When new clients connect, they automatically receive the current state from the Agent, ensuring all clients start with the latest data.



\### SQL API



Every individual Agent instance has its own SQL (SQLite) database that runs \*within the same context\* as the Agent itself. This means that inserting or querying data within your Agent is effectively zero-latency: the Agent doesn't have to round-trip across a continent or the world to access its own data.



You can access the SQL API within any method on an Agent via `this.sql`. The SQL API accepts template literals, and



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; export class MyAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   async onRequest(request) {

&nbsp;     let userId = new URL(request.url).searchParams.get("userId");





&nbsp;     // 'users' is just an example here: you can create arbitrary tables and define your own schemas

&nbsp;     // within each Agent's database using SQL (SQLite syntax).

&nbsp;     let \[user] = this.sql`SELECT \* FROM users WHERE id = ${userId}`;

&nbsp;     return Response.json(user);

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; export class MyAgent extends Agent<Env> {

&nbsp;   async onRequest(request: Request) {

&nbsp;     let userId = new URL(request.url).searchParams.get('userId');





&nbsp;     // 'users' is just an example here: you can create arbitrary tables and define your own schemas

&nbsp;     // within each Agent's database using SQL (SQLite syntax).

&nbsp;     let \[user] = this.sql`SELECT \* FROM users WHERE id = ${userId}`

&nbsp;     return Response.json(user)

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



You can also supply a \[TypeScript type argument](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/2/generics.html#using-type-parameters-in-generic-constraints) to the query, which will be used to infer the type of the result:



```ts

type User = {

&nbsp; id: string;

&nbsp; name: string;

&nbsp; email: string;

};





export class MyAgent extends Agent<Env> {

&nbsp; async onRequest(request: Request) {

&nbsp;   let userId = new URL(request.url).searchParams.get('userId');

&nbsp;   // Supply the type parameter to the query when calling this.sql

&nbsp;   // This assumes the results returns one or more User rows with "id", "name", and "email" columns

&nbsp;   const \[user] = this.sql<User>`SELECT \* FROM users WHERE id = ${userId}`;

&nbsp;   return Response.json(user)

&nbsp; }

}

```



You do not need to specify an array type (`User\[]` or `Array<User>`) as `this.sql` will always return an array of the specified type.



Providing a type parameter does not validate that the result matches your type definition. In TypeScript, properties (fields) that do not exist or conform to the type you provided will be dropped. If you need to validate incoming events, we recommend a library such as \[zod](https://zod.dev/) or your own validator logic.



Note



Learn more about the zero-latency SQL storage that powers both Agents and Durable Objects \[on our blog](https://blog.cloudflare.com/sqlite-in-durable-objects/).



The SQL API exposed to an Agent is similar to the one \[within Durable Objects](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/sqlite-storage-api/#sql-api): Durable Object SQL methods available on `this.ctx.storage.sql`. You can use the same SQL queries with the Agent's database, create tables, and query data, just as you would with Durable Objects or \[D1](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/).



\### Use Agent state as model context



You can combine the state and SQL APIs in your Agent with its ability to \[call AI models](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/using-ai-models/) to include historical context within your prompts to a model. Modern Large Language Models (LLMs) often have very large context windows (up to millions of tokens), which allows you to pull relevant context into your prompt directly.



For example, you can use an Agent's built-in SQL database to pull history, query a model with it, and append to that history ahead of the next call to the model:



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; export class ReasoningAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   async callReasoningModel(prompt) {

&nbsp;     let result = this

&nbsp;       .sql`SELECT \* FROM history WHERE user = ${prompt.userId} ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 1000`;

&nbsp;     let context = \[];

&nbsp;     for (const row of result) {

&nbsp;       context.push(row.entry);

&nbsp;     }





&nbsp;     const client = new OpenAI({

&nbsp;       apiKey: this.env.OPENAI\_API\_KEY,

&nbsp;     });





&nbsp;     // Combine user history with the current prompt

&nbsp;     const systemPrompt = prompt.system || "You are a helpful assistant.";

&nbsp;     const userPrompt = `${prompt.user}\\n\\nUser history:\\n${context.join("\\n")}`;





&nbsp;     try {

&nbsp;       const completion = await client.chat.completions.create({

&nbsp;         model: this.env.MODEL || "o3-mini",

&nbsp;         messages: \[

&nbsp;           { role: "system", content: systemPrompt },

&nbsp;           { role: "user", content: userPrompt },

&nbsp;         ],

&nbsp;         temperature: 0.7,

&nbsp;         max\_tokens: 1000,

&nbsp;       });





&nbsp;       // Store the response in history

&nbsp;       this

&nbsp;         .sql`INSERT INTO history (timestamp, user, entry) VALUES (${new Date()}, ${prompt.userId}, ${completion.choices\[0].message.content})`;





&nbsp;       return completion.choices\[0].message.content;

&nbsp;     } catch (error) {

&nbsp;       console.error("Error calling reasoning model:", error);

&nbsp;       throw error;

&nbsp;     }

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; export class ReasoningAgent extends Agent<Env> {

&nbsp;   async callReasoningModel(prompt: Prompt) {

&nbsp;     let result = this.sql<History>`SELECT \* FROM history WHERE user = ${prompt.userId} ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 1000`;

&nbsp;     let context = \[];

&nbsp;     for (const row of result) {

&nbsp;       context.push(row.entry);

&nbsp;     }





&nbsp;     const client = new OpenAI({

&nbsp;       apiKey: this.env.OPENAI\_API\_KEY,

&nbsp;     });





&nbsp;     // Combine user history with the current prompt

&nbsp;     const systemPrompt = prompt.system || 'You are a helpful assistant.';

&nbsp;     const userPrompt = `${prompt.user}\\n\\nUser history:\\n${context.join('\\n')}`;





&nbsp;     try {

&nbsp;       const completion = await client.chat.completions.create({

&nbsp;         model: this.env.MODEL || 'o3-mini',

&nbsp;         messages: \[

&nbsp;           { role: 'system', content: systemPrompt },

&nbsp;           { role: 'user', content: userPrompt },

&nbsp;         ],

&nbsp;         temperature: 0.7,

&nbsp;         max\_tokens: 1000,

&nbsp;       });





&nbsp;       // Store the response in history

&nbsp;       this

&nbsp;         .sql`INSERT INTO history (timestamp, user, entry) VALUES (${new Date()}, ${prompt.userId}, ${completion.choices\[0].message.content})`;





&nbsp;       return completion.choices\[0].message.content;

&nbsp;     } catch (error) {

&nbsp;       console.error('Error calling reasoning model:', error);

&nbsp;       throw error;

&nbsp;     }

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



This works because each instance of an Agent has its \*own\* database, the state stored in that database is private to that Agent: whether it's acting on behalf of a single user, a room or channel, or a deep research tool. By default, you don't have to manage contention or reach out over the network to a centralized database to retrieve and store state.



\### Next steps



\* Review the \[API documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/agents-api/) for the Agents class to learn how to define them.

\* \[Build a chat Agent](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/getting-started/build-a-chat-agent/) using the Agents SDK and deploy it to Workers.

\* Learn more \[using WebSockets](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/websockets/) to build interactive Agents and stream data back from your Agent.

\* \[Orchestrate asynchronous workflows](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/run-workflows) from your Agent by combining the Agents SDK and \[Workflows](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workflows).



</page>

---

title: Using AI Models · Cloudflare Agents docs

description: "Agents can communicate with AI models hosted on any provider, including:"

lastUpdated: 2026-01-29T10:38:24.000Z

chatbotDeprioritize: false

tags: AI

source\_url:

&nbsp; html: https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/using-ai-models/

&nbsp; md: https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/using-ai-models/index.md

---



Agents can communicate with AI models hosted on any provider, including:



\* \[Workers AI](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/)

\* The \[AI SDK](https://sdk.vercel.ai/docs/ai-sdk-core/overview)

\* \[OpenAI](https://platform.openai.com/docs/quickstart?language=javascript)

\* \[Anthropic](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/api/client-sdks#typescript)

\* \[Google's Gemini](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/openai)



You can also use the model routing features in \[AI Gateway](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/) to route across providers, eval responses, and manage AI provider rate limits.



Because Agents are built on top of \[Durable Objects](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/), each Agent or chat session is associated with a stateful compute instance. Traditional serverless architectures often present challenges for persistent connections needed in real-time applications like chat.



A user can disconnect during a long-running response from a modern reasoning model (such as `o3-mini` or DeepSeek R1), or lose conversational context when refreshing the browser. Instead of relying on request-response patterns and managing an external database to track \& store conversation state, state can be stored directly within the Agent. If a client disconnects, the Agent can write to its own distributed storage, and catch the client up as soon as it reconnects: even if it's hours or days later.



\## Calling AI Models



You can call models from any method within an Agent, including from HTTP requests using the \[`onRequest`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/agents-api/) handler, when a \[scheduled task](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/schedule-tasks/) runs, when handling a WebSocket message in the \[`onMessage`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/websockets/) handler, or from any of your own methods.



Importantly, Agents can call AI models on their own — autonomously — and can handle long-running responses that can take minutes (or longer) to respond in full.



\### Long-running model requests



Modern \[reasoning models](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/reasoning) or "thinking" model can take some time to both generate a response \*and\* stream the response back to the client.



Instead of buffering the entire response, or risking the client disconnecting, you can stream the response back to the client by using the \[WebSocket API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/websockets/).



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; import { Agent } from "agents";

&nbsp; import { OpenAI } from "openai";





&nbsp; export class MyAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   async onConnect(connection, ctx) {

&nbsp;     //

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   async onMessage(connection, message) {

&nbsp;     let msg = JSON.parse(message);

&nbsp;     // This can run as long as it needs to, and return as many messages as it needs to!

&nbsp;     await queryReasoningModel(connection, msg.prompt);

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   async queryReasoningModel(connection, userPrompt) {

&nbsp;     const client = new OpenAI({

&nbsp;       apiKey: this.env.OPENAI\_API\_KEY,

&nbsp;     });





&nbsp;     try {

&nbsp;       const stream = await client.chat.completions.create({

&nbsp;         model: this.env.MODEL || "o3-mini",

&nbsp;         messages: \[{ role: "user", content: userPrompt }],

&nbsp;         stream: true,

&nbsp;       });





&nbsp;       // Stream responses back as WebSocket messages

&nbsp;       for await (const chunk of stream) {

&nbsp;         const content = chunk.choices\[0]?.delta?.content || "";

&nbsp;         if (content) {

&nbsp;           connection.send(JSON.stringify({ type: "chunk", content }));

&nbsp;         }

&nbsp;       }





&nbsp;       // Send completion message

&nbsp;       connection.send(JSON.stringify({ type: "done" }));

&nbsp;     } catch (error) {

&nbsp;       connection.send(JSON.stringify({ type: "error", error: error }));

&nbsp;     }

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; import { Agent } from "agents";

&nbsp; import { OpenAI } from "openai";





&nbsp; export class MyAgent extends Agent<Env> {

&nbsp;   async onConnect(connection: Connection, ctx: ConnectionContext) {

&nbsp;     //

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   async onMessage(connection: Connection, message: WSMessage) {

&nbsp;     let msg = JSON.parse(message);

&nbsp;     // This can run as long as it needs to, and return as many messages as it needs to!

&nbsp;     await queryReasoningModel(connection, msg.prompt);

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   async queryReasoningModel(connection: Connection, userPrompt: string) {

&nbsp;     const client = new OpenAI({

&nbsp;       apiKey: this.env.OPENAI\_API\_KEY,

&nbsp;     });





&nbsp;     try {

&nbsp;       const stream = await client.chat.completions.create({

&nbsp;         model: this.env.MODEL || "o3-mini",

&nbsp;         messages: \[{ role: "user", content: userPrompt }],

&nbsp;         stream: true,

&nbsp;       });





&nbsp;       // Stream responses back as WebSocket messages

&nbsp;       for await (const chunk of stream) {

&nbsp;         const content = chunk.choices\[0]?.delta?.content || "";

&nbsp;         if (content) {

&nbsp;           connection.send(JSON.stringify({ type: "chunk", content }));

&nbsp;         }

&nbsp;       }





&nbsp;       // Send completion message

&nbsp;       connection.send(JSON.stringify({ type: "done" }));

&nbsp;     } catch (error) {

&nbsp;       connection.send(JSON.stringify({ type: "error", error: error }));

&nbsp;     }

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



You can also persist AI model responses back to \[Agent's internal state](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/store-and-sync-state/) by using the `this.setState` method. For example, if you run a \[scheduled task](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/schedule-tasks/), you can store the output of the task and read it later. Or, if a user disconnects, read the message history back and send it to the user when they reconnect.



\### Workers AI



\### Hosted models



You can use \[any of the models available in Workers AI](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/models/) within your Agent by \[configuring a binding](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/bindings/).



Workers AI supports streaming responses out-of-the-box by setting `stream: true`, and we strongly recommend using them to avoid buffering and delaying responses, especially for larger models or reasoning models that require more time to generate a response.



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; import { Agent } from "agents";





&nbsp; export class MyAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   async onRequest(request) {

&nbsp;     const response = await env.AI.run(

&nbsp;       "@cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-32b",

&nbsp;       {

&nbsp;         prompt: "Build me a Cloudflare Worker that returns JSON.",

&nbsp;         stream: true, // Stream a response and don't block the client!

&nbsp;       },

&nbsp;     );





&nbsp;     // Return the stream

&nbsp;     return new Response(answer, {

&nbsp;       headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;     });

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; import { Agent } from "agents";





&nbsp; interface Env {

&nbsp;   AI: Ai;

&nbsp; }





&nbsp; export class MyAgent extends Agent<Env> {

&nbsp;   async onRequest(request: Request) {

&nbsp;     const response = await env.AI.run(

&nbsp;       "@cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-32b",

&nbsp;       {

&nbsp;         prompt: "Build me a Cloudflare Worker that returns JSON.",

&nbsp;         stream: true, // Stream a response and don't block the client!

&nbsp;       },

&nbsp;     );





&nbsp;     // Return the stream

&nbsp;     return new Response(answer, {

&nbsp;       headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;     });

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



Your Wrangler configuration will need an `ai` binding added:



\* wrangler.jsonc



&nbsp; ```jsonc

&nbsp; {

&nbsp;   "ai": {

&nbsp;     "binding": "AI"

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* wrangler.toml



&nbsp; ```toml

&nbsp; \[ai]

&nbsp; binding = "AI"

&nbsp; ```



\### Model routing



You can also use the model routing features in \[AI Gateway](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/) directly from an Agent by specifying a \[`gateway` configuration](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/usage/providers/workersai/) when calling the AI binding.



Note



Model routing allows you to route requests to different AI models based on whether they are reachable, rate-limiting your client, and/or if you've exceeded your cost budget for a specific provider.



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; import { Agent } from "agents";





&nbsp; export class MyAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   async onRequest(request) {

&nbsp;     const response = await env.AI.run(

&nbsp;       "@cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-32b",

&nbsp;       {

&nbsp;         prompt: "Build me a Cloudflare Worker that returns JSON.",

&nbsp;       },

&nbsp;       {

&nbsp;         gateway: {

&nbsp;           id: "{gateway\_id}", // Specify your AI Gateway ID here

&nbsp;           skipCache: false,

&nbsp;           cacheTtl: 3360,

&nbsp;         },

&nbsp;       },

&nbsp;     );





&nbsp;     return Response.json(response);

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; import { Agent } from "agents";





&nbsp; interface Env {

&nbsp;   AI: Ai;

&nbsp; }





&nbsp; export class MyAgent extends Agent<Env> {

&nbsp;   async onRequest(request: Request) {

&nbsp;     const response = await env.AI.run(

&nbsp;       "@cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-32b",

&nbsp;       {

&nbsp;         prompt: "Build me a Cloudflare Worker that returns JSON.",

&nbsp;       },

&nbsp;       {

&nbsp;         gateway: {

&nbsp;           id: "{gateway\_id}", // Specify your AI Gateway ID here

&nbsp;           skipCache: false,

&nbsp;           cacheTtl: 3360,

&nbsp;         },

&nbsp;       },

&nbsp;     );





&nbsp;     return Response.json(response);

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



Your Wrangler configuration will need an `ai` binding added. This is shared across both Workers AI and AI Gateway.



\* wrangler.jsonc



&nbsp; ```jsonc

&nbsp; {

&nbsp;   "ai": {

&nbsp;     "binding": "AI"

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* wrangler.toml



&nbsp; ```toml

&nbsp; \[ai]

&nbsp; binding = "AI"

&nbsp; ```



Visit the \[AI Gateway documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/) to learn how to configure a gateway and retrieve a gateway ID.



\### AI SDK



The \[AI SDK](https://sdk.vercel.ai/docs/introduction) provides a unified API for using AI models, including for text generation, tool calling, structured responses, image generation, and more.



To use the AI SDK, install the `ai` package and use it within your Agent. The example below shows how it use it to generate text on request, but you can use it from any method within your Agent, including WebSocket handlers, as part of a scheduled task, or even when the Agent is initialized.



\* npm



&nbsp; ```sh

&nbsp; npm i ai @ai-sdk/openai

&nbsp; ```



\* yarn



&nbsp; ```sh

&nbsp; yarn add ai @ai-sdk/openai

&nbsp; ```



\* pnpm



&nbsp; ```sh

&nbsp; pnpm add ai @ai-sdk/openai

&nbsp; ```



\- JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; import { Agent } from "agents";

&nbsp; import { generateText } from "ai";

&nbsp; import { openai } from "@ai-sdk/openai";





&nbsp; export class MyAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   async onRequest(request) {

&nbsp;     const { text } = await generateText({

&nbsp;       model: openai("o3-mini"),

&nbsp;       prompt: "Build me an AI agent on Cloudflare Workers",

&nbsp;     });





&nbsp;     return Response.json({ modelResponse: text });

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\- TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; import { Agent } from "agents";

&nbsp; import { generateText } from "ai";

&nbsp; import { openai } from "@ai-sdk/openai";





&nbsp; export class MyAgent extends Agent<Env> {

&nbsp;   async onRequest(request: Request): Promise<Response> {

&nbsp;     const { text } = await generateText({

&nbsp;       model: openai("o3-mini"),

&nbsp;       prompt: "Build me an AI agent on Cloudflare Workers",

&nbsp;     });





&nbsp;     return Response.json({ modelResponse: text });

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\### OpenAI compatible endpoints



Agents can call models across any service, including those that support the OpenAI API. For example, you can use the OpenAI SDK to use one of \[Google's Gemini models](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/openai#node.js) directly from your Agent.



Agents can stream responses back over HTTP using Server Sent Events (SSE) from within an `onRequest` handler, or by using the native \[WebSockets](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/websockets/) API in your Agent to responses back to a client, which is especially useful for larger models that can take over 30+ seconds to reply.



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; import { Agent } from "agents";

&nbsp; import { OpenAI } from "openai";





&nbsp; export class MyAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   async onRequest(request) {

&nbsp;     const openai = new OpenAI({

&nbsp;       apiKey: this.env.GEMINI\_API\_KEY,

&nbsp;       baseURL: "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/",

&nbsp;     });





&nbsp;     // Create a TransformStream to handle streaming data

&nbsp;     let { readable, writable } = new TransformStream();

&nbsp;     let writer = writable.getWriter();

&nbsp;     const textEncoder = new TextEncoder();





&nbsp;     // Use ctx.waitUntil to run the async function in the background

&nbsp;     // so that it doesn't block the streaming response

&nbsp;     ctx.waitUntil(

&nbsp;       (async () => {

&nbsp;         const stream = await openai.chat.completions.create({

&nbsp;           model: "4o",

&nbsp;           messages: \[

&nbsp;             { role: "user", content: "Write me a Cloudflare Worker." },

&nbsp;           ],

&nbsp;           stream: true,

&nbsp;         });





&nbsp;         // loop over the data as it is streamed and write to the writeable

&nbsp;         for await (const part of stream) {

&nbsp;           writer.write(

&nbsp;             textEncoder.encode(part.choices\[0]?.delta?.content || ""),

&nbsp;           );

&nbsp;         }

&nbsp;         writer.close();

&nbsp;       })(),

&nbsp;     );





&nbsp;     // Return the readable stream back to the client

&nbsp;     return new Response(readable);

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; import { Agent } from "agents";

&nbsp; import { OpenAI } from "openai";





&nbsp; export class MyAgent extends Agent<Env> {

&nbsp;   async onRequest(request: Request): Promise<Response> {

&nbsp;     const openai = new OpenAI({

&nbsp;       apiKey: this.env.GEMINI\_API\_KEY,

&nbsp;       baseURL: "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/",

&nbsp;     });





&nbsp;     // Create a TransformStream to handle streaming data

&nbsp;     let { readable, writable } = new TransformStream();

&nbsp;     let writer = writable.getWriter();

&nbsp;     const textEncoder = new TextEncoder();





&nbsp;     // Use ctx.waitUntil to run the async function in the background

&nbsp;     // so that it doesn't block the streaming response

&nbsp;     ctx.waitUntil(

&nbsp;       (async () => {

&nbsp;         const stream = await openai.chat.completions.create({

&nbsp;           model: "4o",

&nbsp;           messages: \[

&nbsp;             { role: "user", content: "Write me a Cloudflare Worker." },

&nbsp;           ],

&nbsp;           stream: true,

&nbsp;         });





&nbsp;         // loop over the data as it is streamed and write to the writeable

&nbsp;         for await (const part of stream) {

&nbsp;           writer.write(

&nbsp;             textEncoder.encode(part.choices\[0]?.delta?.content || ""),

&nbsp;           );

&nbsp;         }

&nbsp;         writer.close();

&nbsp;       })(),

&nbsp;     );





&nbsp;     // Return the readable stream back to the client

&nbsp;     return new Response(readable);

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



</page>
