title: Using WebSockets · Cloudflare Agents docs

description: Users and clients can connect to an Agent directly over WebSockets,

&nbsp; allowing long-running, bi-directional communication with your Agent as it

&nbsp; operates.

lastUpdated: 2025-03-18T12:13:40.000Z

chatbotDeprioritize: false

source\_url:

&nbsp; html: https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/websockets/

&nbsp; md: https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/websockets/index.md

---



Users and clients can connect to an Agent directly over WebSockets, allowing long-running, bi-directional communication with your Agent as it operates.



To enable an Agent to accept WebSockets, define `onConnect` and `onMessage` methods on your Agent.



\* `onConnect(connection: Connection, ctx: ConnectionContext)` is called when a client establishes a new WebSocket connection. The original HTTP request, including request headers, cookies, and the URL itself, are available on `ctx.request`.

\* `onMessage(connection: Connection, message: WSMessage)` is called for each incoming WebSocket message. Messages are one of `ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView | string`, and you can send messages back to a client using `connection.send()`. You can distinguish between client connections by checking `connection.id`, which is unique for each connected client.



Here's an example of an Agent that echoes back any message it receives:



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; import { Agent, Connection } from "agents";





&nbsp; export class ChatAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   async onConnect(connection, ctx) {

&nbsp;     // Connections are automatically accepted by the SDK.

&nbsp;     // You can also explicitly close a connection here with connection.close()

&nbsp;     // Access the Request on ctx.request to inspect headers, cookies and the URL

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   async onMessage(connection, message) {

&nbsp;     // const response = await longRunningAITask(message)

&nbsp;     await connection.send(message);

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; import { Agent, Connection } from "agents";





&nbsp; export class ChatAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   async onConnect(connection: Connection, ctx: ConnectionContext) {

&nbsp;     // Connections are automatically accepted by the SDK.

&nbsp;     // You can also explicitly close a connection here with connection.close()

&nbsp;     // Access the Request on ctx.request to inspect headers, cookies and the URL

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   async onMessage(connection: Connection, message: WSMessage) {

&nbsp;     // const response = await longRunningAITask(message)

&nbsp;     await connection.send(message)

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\### Connecting clients



The Agent framework includes a useful helper package for connecting directly to your Agent (or other Agents) from a client application. Import `agents/client`, create an instance of `AgentClient` and use it to connect to an instance of your Agent:



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; import { AgentClient } from "agents/client";





&nbsp; const connection = new AgentClient({

&nbsp;   agent: "dialogue-agent",

&nbsp;   name: "insight-seeker",

&nbsp; });





&nbsp; connection.addEventListener("message", (event) => {

&nbsp;   console.log("Received:", event.data);

&nbsp; });





&nbsp; connection.send(

&nbsp;   JSON.stringify({

&nbsp;     type: "inquiry",

&nbsp;     content: "What patterns do you see?",

&nbsp;   }),

&nbsp; );

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; import { AgentClient } from "agents/client";





&nbsp; const connection = new AgentClient({

&nbsp;   agent: "dialogue-agent",

&nbsp;   name: "insight-seeker",

&nbsp; });





&nbsp; connection.addEventListener("message", (event) => {

&nbsp;   console.log("Received:", event.data);

&nbsp; });





&nbsp; connection.send(

&nbsp;   JSON.stringify({

&nbsp;     type: "inquiry",

&nbsp;     content: "What patterns do you see?",

&nbsp;   })

&nbsp; );

&nbsp; ```



\### React clients



React-based applications can import `agents/react` and use the `useAgent` hook to connect to an instance of an Agent directly:



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; import { useAgent } from "agents/react";





&nbsp; function AgentInterface() {

&nbsp;   const connection = useAgent({

&nbsp;     agent: "dialogue-agent",

&nbsp;     name: "insight-seeker",

&nbsp;     onMessage: (message) => {

&nbsp;       console.log("Understanding received:", message.data);

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;     onOpen: () => console.log("Connection established"),

&nbsp;     onClose: () => console.log("Connection closed"),

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   const inquire = () => {

&nbsp;     connection.send(

&nbsp;       JSON.stringify({

&nbsp;         type: "inquiry",

&nbsp;         content: "What insights have you gathered?",

&nbsp;       }),

&nbsp;     );

&nbsp;   };





&nbsp;   return (

&nbsp;     <div className="agent-interface">

&nbsp;       <button onClick={inquire}>Seek Understanding</button>

&nbsp;     </div>

&nbsp;   );

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; import { useAgent } from "agents/react";





&nbsp; function AgentInterface() {

&nbsp;   const connection = useAgent({

&nbsp;     agent: "dialogue-agent",

&nbsp;     name: "insight-seeker",

&nbsp;     onMessage: (message) => {

&nbsp;       console.log("Understanding received:", message.data);

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;     onOpen: () => console.log("Connection established"),

&nbsp;     onClose: () => console.log("Connection closed"),

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   const inquire = () => {

&nbsp;     connection.send(

&nbsp;       JSON.stringify({

&nbsp;         type: "inquiry",

&nbsp;         content: "What insights have you gathered?",

&nbsp;       })

&nbsp;     );

&nbsp;   };





&nbsp;   return (

&nbsp;     <div className="agent-interface">

&nbsp;       <button onClick={inquire}>Seek Understanding</button>

&nbsp;     </div>

&nbsp;   );

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



The `useAgent` hook automatically handles the lifecycle of the connection, ensuring that it is properly initialized and cleaned up when the component mounts and unmounts. You can also \[combine `useAgent` with `useState`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/store-and-sync-state/) to automatically synchronize state across all clients connected to your Agent.



\### Handling WebSocket events



Define `onError` and `onClose` methods on your Agent to explicitly handle WebSocket client errors and close events. Log errors, clean up state, and/or emit metrics:



\* JavaScript



&nbsp; ```js

&nbsp; import { Agent, Connection } from "agents";





&nbsp; export class ChatAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;   // onConnect and onMessage methods

&nbsp;   // ...





&nbsp;   // WebSocket error and disconnection (close) handling.

&nbsp;   async onError(connection, error) {

&nbsp;     console.error(`WS error: ${error}`);

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp;   async onClose(connection, code, reason, wasClean) {

&nbsp;     console.log(`WS closed: ${code} - ${reason} - wasClean: ${wasClean}`);

&nbsp;     connection.close();

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* TypeScript



&nbsp; ```ts

&nbsp; import { Agent, Connection } from "agents";





&nbsp; export class ChatAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;    // onConnect and onMessage methods

&nbsp;   // ...





&nbsp;   // WebSocket error and disconnection (close) handling.

&nbsp;   async onError(connection: Connection, error: unknown): Promise<void> {

&nbsp;     console.error(`WS error: ${error}`);

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp;   async onClose(connection: Connection, code: number, reason: string, wasClean: boolean): Promise<void> {

&nbsp;     console.log(`WS closed: ${code} - ${reason} - wasClean: ${wasClean}`);

&nbsp;     connection.close();

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```

title: Testing your Agents · Cloudflare Agents docs

description: Because Agents run on Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects, they

&nbsp; can be tested using the same tools and techniques as Workers and Durable

&nbsp; Objects.

lastUpdated: 2026-01-29T10:38:24.000Z

chatbotDeprioritize: false

source\_url:

&nbsp; html: https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/getting-started/testing-your-agent/

&nbsp; md: https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/getting-started/testing-your-agent/index.md

---



Because Agents run on Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects, they can be tested using the same tools and techniques as Workers and Durable Objects.



\## Writing and running tests



\### Setup



Note



The `agents-starter` template and new Cloudflare Workers projects already include the relevant `vitest` and `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` packages, as well as a valid `vitest.config.js` file.



Before you write your first test, install the necessary packages:



```sh

npm install vitest@~3.0.0 --save-dev --save-exact

npm install @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers --save-dev

```



Ensure that your `vitest.config.js` file is identical to the following:



```js

import { defineWorkersConfig } from "@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers/config";





export default defineWorkersConfig({

&nbsp; test: {

&nbsp;   poolOptions: {

&nbsp;     workers: {

&nbsp;       wrangler: { configPath: "./wrangler.jsonc" },

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   },

&nbsp; },

});

```



\### Add the Agent configuration



Add a `durableObjects` configuration to `vitest.config.js` with the name of your Agent class:



```js

import { defineWorkersConfig } from "@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers/config";





export default defineWorkersConfig({

&nbsp; test: {

&nbsp;   poolOptions: {

&nbsp;     workers: {

&nbsp;       main: "./src/index.ts",

&nbsp;       miniflare: {

&nbsp;         durableObjects: {

&nbsp;           NAME: "MyAgent",

&nbsp;         },

&nbsp;       },

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   },

&nbsp; },

});

```



\### Write a test



Note



Review the \[Vitest documentation](https://vitest.dev/) for more information on testing, including the test API reference and advanced testing techniques.



Tests use the `vitest` framework. A basic test suite for your Agent can validate how your Agent responds to requests, but can also unit test your Agent's methods and state.



```ts

import {

&nbsp; env,

&nbsp; createExecutionContext,

&nbsp; waitOnExecutionContext,

&nbsp; SELF,

} from "cloudflare:test";

import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest";

import worker from "../src";

import { Env } from "../src";





interface ProvidedEnv extends Env {}





describe("make a request to my Agent", () => {

&nbsp; // Unit testing approach

&nbsp; it("responds with state", async () => {

&nbsp;   // Provide a valid URL that your Worker can use to route to your Agent

&nbsp;   // If you are using routeAgentRequest, this will be /agent/:agent/:name

&nbsp;   const request = new Request<unknown, IncomingRequestCfProperties>(

&nbsp;     "http://example.com/agent/my-agent/agent-123",

&nbsp;   );

&nbsp;   const ctx = createExecutionContext();

&nbsp;   const response = await worker.fetch(request, env, ctx);

&nbsp;   await waitOnExecutionContext(ctx);

&nbsp;   expect(await response.text()).toMatchObject({ hello: "from your agent" });

&nbsp; });





&nbsp; it("also responds with state", async () => {

&nbsp;   const request = new Request("http://example.com/agent/my-agent/agent-123");

&nbsp;   const response = await SELF.fetch(request);

&nbsp;   expect(await response.text()).toMatchObject({ hello: "from your agent" });

&nbsp; });

});

```



\### Run tests



Running tests is done using the `vitest` CLI:



```sh

$ npm run test

\# or run vitest directly

$ npx vitest

```



```sh

&nbsp; MyAgent

&nbsp;   ✓ should return a greeting (1 ms)





Test Files  1 passed (1)

```



Review the \[documentation on testing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/testing/vitest-integration/write-your-first-test/) for additional examples and test configuration.



\## Running Agents locally



You can also run an Agent locally using the `wrangler` CLI:



```sh

$ npx wrangler dev

```



```sh

Your Worker and resources are simulated locally via Miniflare. For more information, see: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/testing/local-development.





Your worker has access to the following bindings:

\- Durable Objects:

&nbsp; - MyAgent: MyAgent

&nbsp; Starting local server...

\[wrangler:inf] Ready on http://localhost:53645

```



This spins up a local development server that runs the same runtime as Cloudflare Workers, and allows you to iterate on your Agent's code and test it locally without deploying it.



Visit the \[`wrangler dev`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/commands/#dev) docs to review the CLI flags and configuration options.

title: Build an Interactive ChatGPT App · Cloudflare Agents docs

description: "This guide will show you how to build and deploy an interactive

&nbsp; ChatGPT App on Cloudflare Workers that can:"

lastUpdated: 2026-02-02T18:38:11.000Z

chatbotDeprioritize: false

source\_url:

&nbsp; html: https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/guides/chatgpt-app/

&nbsp; md: https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/guides/chatgpt-app/index.md

---



\## Deploy your first ChatGPT App



This guide will show you how to build and deploy an interactive ChatGPT App on Cloudflare Workers that can:



\* Render rich, interactive UI widgets directly in ChatGPT conversations

\* Maintain real-time, multi-user state using Durable Objects

\* Enable bidirectional communication between your app and ChatGPT

\* Build multiplayer experiences that run entirely within ChatGPT



You will build a real-time multiplayer chess game that demonstrates these capabilities. Players can start or join games, make moves on an interactive chessboard, and even ask ChatGPT for strategic advice—all without leaving the conversation.



Your ChatGPT App will use the \*\*Model Context Protocol (MCP)\*\* to expose tools and UI resources that ChatGPT can invoke on your behalf.



You can view the full code for this example \[here](https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/tree/main/openai-sdk/chess-app).



\## Prerequisites



Before you begin, you will need:



\* A \[Cloudflare account](https://dash.cloudflare.com/sign-up)

\* \[Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) installed (v18 or later)

\* A \[ChatGPT Plus or Team account](https://chat.openai.com/) with developer mode enabled

\* Basic knowledge of React and TypeScript



\## 1. Enable ChatGPT Developer Mode



To use ChatGPT Apps (also called connectors), you need to enable developer mode:



1\. Open \[ChatGPT](https://chat.openai.com/).

2\. Go to \*\*Settings\*\* > \*\*Apps \& Connectors\*\* > \*\*Advanced Settings\*\*

3\. Toggle \*\*Developer mode ON\*\*



Once enabled, you will be able to install custom apps during development and testing.



\## 2. Create your ChatGPT App project



1\. Create a new project for your Chess App:



\* npm



&nbsp; ```sh

&nbsp; npm create cloudflare@latest -- my-chess-app

&nbsp; ```



\* yarn



&nbsp; ```sh

&nbsp; yarn create cloudflare my-chess-app

&nbsp; ```



\* pnpm



&nbsp; ```sh

&nbsp; pnpm create cloudflare@latest my-chess-app

&nbsp; ```



1\. Navigate into your project:



```sh

cd my-chess-app

```



1\. Install the required dependencies:



```sh

npm install agents @modelcontextprotocol/sdk chess.js react react-dom react-chessboard

```



1\. Install development dependencies:



```sh

npm install -D @cloudflare/vite-plugin @vitejs/plugin-react vite vite-plugin-singlefile @types/react @types/react-dom

```



\## 3. Configure your project



1\. Update your `wrangler.jsonc` to configure Durable Objects and assets:



\* wrangler.jsonc



&nbsp; ```jsonc

&nbsp; {

&nbsp;   "name": "my-chess-app",

&nbsp;   "main": "src/index.ts",

&nbsp;   "compatibility\_date": "2026-02-04",

&nbsp;   "compatibility\_flags": \["nodejs\_compat"],

&nbsp;   "durable\_objects": {

&nbsp;     "bindings": \[

&nbsp;       {

&nbsp;         "name": "CHESS",

&nbsp;         "class\_name": "ChessGame"

&nbsp;       }

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   },

&nbsp;   "migrations": \[

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       "tag": "v1",

&nbsp;       "new\_sqlite\_classes": \["ChessGame"]

&nbsp;     }

&nbsp;   ],

&nbsp;   "assets": {

&nbsp;     "directory": "dist",

&nbsp;     "binding": "ASSETS"

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* wrangler.toml



&nbsp; ```toml

&nbsp; name = "my-chess-app"

&nbsp; main = "src/index.ts"

&nbsp; compatibility\_date = "2026-02-04"

&nbsp; compatibility\_flags = \[ "nodejs\_compat" ]





&nbsp; \[\[durable\_objects.bindings]]

&nbsp; name = "CHESS"

&nbsp; class\_name = "ChessGame"





&nbsp; \[\[migrations]]

&nbsp; tag = "v1"

&nbsp; new\_sqlite\_classes = \[ "ChessGame" ]





&nbsp; \[assets]

&nbsp; directory = "dist"

&nbsp; binding = "ASSETS"

&nbsp; ```



1\. Create a `vite.config.ts` for building your React UI:



```ts

import { cloudflare } from "@cloudflare/vite-plugin";

import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react";

import { defineConfig } from "vite";

import { viteSingleFile } from "vite-plugin-singlefile";





export default defineConfig({

&nbsp; plugins: \[react(), cloudflare(), viteSingleFile()],

&nbsp; build: {

&nbsp;   minify: false

&nbsp; }

});

```



1\. Update your `package.json` scripts:



```json

{

&nbsp; "scripts": {

&nbsp;   "dev": "vite",

&nbsp;   "build": "vite build",

&nbsp;   "deploy": "vite build \&\& wrangler deploy"

&nbsp; }

}

```



\## 4. Create the Chess game engine



1\. Create the game logic using Durable Objects at `src/chess.tsx`:



```tsx

import { Agent, callable, getCurrentAgent } from "agents";

import { Chess } from "chess.js";





type Color = "w" | "b";





type ConnectionState = {

&nbsp; playerId: string;

};





export type State = {

&nbsp; board: string;

&nbsp; players: { w?: string; b?: string };

&nbsp; status: "waiting" | "active" | "mate" | "draw" | "resigned";

&nbsp; winner?: Color;

&nbsp; lastSan?: string;

};





export class ChessGame extends Agent<Env, State> {

&nbsp; initialState: State = {

&nbsp;   board: new Chess().fen(),

&nbsp;   players: {},

&nbsp;   status: "waiting"

&nbsp; };





&nbsp; game = new Chess();





&nbsp; constructor(ctx: DurableObjectState, public env: Env) {

&nbsp;   super(ctx, env);

&nbsp;   this.game.load(this.state.board);

&nbsp; }





&nbsp; private colorOf(playerId: string): Color | undefined {

&nbsp;   const { players } = this.state;

&nbsp;   if (players.w === playerId) return "w";

&nbsp;   if (players.b === playerId) return "b";

&nbsp;   return undefined;

&nbsp; }





&nbsp; @callable()

&nbsp; join(params: { playerId: string; preferred?: Color | "any" }) {

&nbsp;   const { playerId, preferred = "any" } = params;

&nbsp;   const { connection } = getCurrentAgent();

&nbsp;   if (!connection) throw new Error("Not connected");





&nbsp;   connection.setState({ playerId });

&nbsp;   const s = this.state;





&nbsp;   // Already seated? Return seat

&nbsp;   const already = this.colorOf(playerId);

&nbsp;   if (already) {

&nbsp;     return { ok: true, role: already as Color, state: s };

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   // Choose a seat

&nbsp;   const free: Color\[] = (\["w", "b"] as const).filter((c) => !s.players\[c]);

&nbsp;   if (free.length === 0) {

&nbsp;     return { ok: true, role: "spectator" as const, state: s };

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   let seat: Color = free\[0];

&nbsp;   if (preferred === "w" \&\& free.includes("w")) seat = "w";

&nbsp;   if (preferred === "b" \&\& free.includes("b")) seat = "b";





&nbsp;   s.players\[seat] = playerId;

&nbsp;   s.status = s.players.w \&\& s.players.b ? "active" : "waiting";

&nbsp;   this.setState(s);

&nbsp;   return { ok: true, role: seat, state: s };

&nbsp; }





&nbsp; @callable()

&nbsp; move(

&nbsp;   move: { from: string; to: string; promotion?: string },

&nbsp;   expectedFen?: string

&nbsp; ) {

&nbsp;   if (this.state.status === "waiting") {

&nbsp;     return {

&nbsp;       ok: false,

&nbsp;       reason: "not-in-game",

&nbsp;       fen: this.game.fen(),

&nbsp;       status: this.state.status

&nbsp;     };

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   const { connection } = getCurrentAgent();

&nbsp;   if (!connection) throw new Error("Not connected");

&nbsp;   const { playerId } = connection.state as ConnectionState;





&nbsp;   const seat = this.colorOf(playerId);

&nbsp;   if (!seat) {

&nbsp;     return {

&nbsp;       ok: false,

&nbsp;       reason: "not-in-game",

&nbsp;       fen: this.game.fen(),

&nbsp;       status: this.state.status

&nbsp;     };

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   if (seat !== this.game.turn()) {

&nbsp;     return {

&nbsp;       ok: false,

&nbsp;       reason: "not-your-turn",

&nbsp;       fen: this.game.fen(),

&nbsp;       status: this.state.status

&nbsp;     };

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   // Optimistic sync guard

&nbsp;   if (expectedFen \&\& expectedFen !== this.game.fen()) {

&nbsp;     return {

&nbsp;       ok: false,

&nbsp;       reason: "stale",

&nbsp;       fen: this.game.fen(),

&nbsp;       status: this.state.status

&nbsp;     };

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   const res = this.game.move(move);

&nbsp;   if (!res) {

&nbsp;     return {

&nbsp;       ok: false,

&nbsp;       reason: "illegal",

&nbsp;       fen: this.game.fen(),

&nbsp;       status: this.state.status

&nbsp;     };

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   const fen = this.game.fen();

&nbsp;   let status: State\["status"] = "active";

&nbsp;   if (this.game.isCheckmate()) status = "mate";

&nbsp;   else if (this.game.isDraw()) status = "draw";





&nbsp;   this.setState({

&nbsp;     ...this.state,

&nbsp;     board: fen,

&nbsp;     lastSan: res.san,

&nbsp;     status,

&nbsp;     winner: status === "mate" ? (this.game.turn() === "w" ? "b" : "w") : undefined

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return { ok: true, fen, san: res.san, status };

&nbsp; }





&nbsp; @callable()

&nbsp; resign() {

&nbsp;   const { connection } = getCurrentAgent();

&nbsp;   if (!connection) throw new Error("Not connected");

&nbsp;   const { playerId } = connection.state as ConnectionState;





&nbsp;   const seat = this.colorOf(playerId);

&nbsp;   if (!seat) return { ok: false, reason: "not-in-game", state: this.state };





&nbsp;   const winner = seat === "w" ? "b" : "w";

&nbsp;   this.setState({ ...this.state, status: "resigned", winner });

&nbsp;   return { ok: true, state: this.state };

&nbsp; }

}

```



\## 5. Create the MCP server and UI resource



1\. Create your main worker at `src/index.ts`:



```ts

import { createMcpHandler } from "agents/mcp";

import { routeAgentRequest } from "agents";

import { McpServer } from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/mcp.js";

import { env } from "cloudflare:workers";





const getWidgetHtml = async (host: string) => {

&nbsp; let html = await (await env.ASSETS.fetch("http://localhost/")).text();

&nbsp; html = html.replace(

&nbsp;   "<!--RUNTIME\_CONFIG-->",

&nbsp;   `<script>window.HOST = \\`${host}\\`;</script>`

&nbsp; );

&nbsp; return html;

};





const server = new McpServer({ name: "Chess", version: "v1.0.0" });





// Register a UI resource that ChatGPT can render

server.registerResource(

&nbsp; "chess",

&nbsp; "ui://widget/index.html",

&nbsp; {},

&nbsp; async (\_uri, extra) => {

&nbsp;   return {

&nbsp;     contents: \[

&nbsp;       {

&nbsp;         uri: "ui://widget/index.html",

&nbsp;         mimeType: "text/html+skybridge",

&nbsp;         text: await getWidgetHtml(extra.requestInfo?.headers.host as string)

&nbsp;       }

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   };

&nbsp; }

);





// Register a tool that ChatGPT can call to render the UI

server.registerTool(

&nbsp; "playChess",

&nbsp; {

&nbsp;   title: "Renders a chess game menu, ready to start or join a game.",

&nbsp;   annotations: { readOnlyHint: true },

&nbsp;   \_meta: {

&nbsp;     "openai/outputTemplate": "ui://widget/index.html",

&nbsp;     "openai/toolInvocation/invoking": "Opening chess widget",

&nbsp;     "openai/toolInvocation/invoked": "Chess widget opened"

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; },

&nbsp; async (\_, \_extra) => {

&nbsp;   return {

&nbsp;     content: \[{ type: "text", text: "Successfully rendered chess game menu" }]

&nbsp;   };

&nbsp; }

);





const mcpHandler = createMcpHandler(server);





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(req: Request, env: Env, ctx: ExecutionContext) {

&nbsp;   const url = new URL(req.url);

&nbsp;   if (url.pathname.startsWith("/mcp")) return mcpHandler(req, env, ctx);





&nbsp;   return (

&nbsp;     (await routeAgentRequest(req, env)) ??

&nbsp;     new Response("Not found", { status: 404 })

&nbsp;   );

&nbsp; }

};





export { ChessGame } from "./chess";

```



\## 6. Build the React UI



1\. Create the HTML entry point at `index.html`:



```html

<!doctype html>

<html>

&nbsp; <head>

&nbsp;   <!--RUNTIME\_CONFIG-->

&nbsp; </head>

&nbsp; <body>

&nbsp;   <div id="root" style="font-family: verdana"></div>

&nbsp;   <script type="module" src="/src/app.tsx"></script>

&nbsp; </body>

</html>

```



1\. Create the React app at `src/app.tsx`:



```tsx

import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";

import { useAgent } from "agents/react";

import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";

import { Chess, type Square } from "chess.js";

import { Chessboard, type PieceDropHandlerArgs } from "react-chessboard";

import type { State as ServerState } from "./chess";





function usePlayerId() {

&nbsp; const \[pid] = useState(() => {

&nbsp;   const existing = localStorage.getItem("playerId");

&nbsp;   if (existing) return existing;

&nbsp;   const id = crypto.randomUUID();

&nbsp;   localStorage.setItem("playerId", id);

&nbsp;   return id;

&nbsp; });

&nbsp; return pid;

}





function App() {

&nbsp; const playerId = usePlayerId();

&nbsp; const \[gameId, setGameId] = useState<string | null>(null);

&nbsp; const \[gameIdInput, setGameIdInput] = useState("");

&nbsp; const \[menuError, setMenuError] = useState<string | null>(null);





&nbsp; const gameRef = useRef(new Chess());

&nbsp; const \[fen, setFen] = useState(gameRef.current.fen());

&nbsp; const \[myColor, setMyColor] = useState<"w" | "b" | "spectator">("spectator");

&nbsp; const \[pending, setPending] = useState(false);

&nbsp; const \[serverState, setServerState] = useState<ServerState | null>(null);

&nbsp; const \[joined, setJoined] = useState(false);





&nbsp; const host = window.HOST ?? "http://localhost:5173/";





&nbsp; const { stub } = useAgent<ServerState>({

&nbsp;   host,

&nbsp;   name: gameId ?? "\_\_lobby\_\_",

&nbsp;   agent: "chess",

&nbsp;   onStateUpdate: (s) => {

&nbsp;     if (!gameId) return;

&nbsp;     gameRef.current.load(s.board);

&nbsp;     setFen(s.board);

&nbsp;     setServerState(s);

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; });





&nbsp; useEffect(() => {

&nbsp;   if (!gameId || joined) return;





&nbsp;   (async () => {

&nbsp;     try {

&nbsp;       const res = await stub.join({ playerId, preferred: "any" });

&nbsp;       if (!res?.ok) return;





&nbsp;       setMyColor(res.role);

&nbsp;       gameRef.current.load(res.state.board);

&nbsp;       setFen(res.state.board);

&nbsp;       setServerState(res.state);

&nbsp;       setJoined(true);

&nbsp;     } catch (error) {

&nbsp;       console.error("Failed to join game", error);

&nbsp;     }

&nbsp;   })();

&nbsp; }, \[playerId, gameId, stub, joined]);





&nbsp; async function handleStartNewGame() {

&nbsp;   const newId = crypto.randomUUID();

&nbsp;   setGameId(newId);

&nbsp;   setGameIdInput(newId);

&nbsp;   setMenuError(null);

&nbsp;   setJoined(false);

&nbsp; }





&nbsp; async function handleJoinGame() {

&nbsp;   const trimmed = gameIdInput.trim();

&nbsp;   if (!trimmed) {

&nbsp;     setMenuError("Enter a game ID to join.");

&nbsp;     return;

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp;   setGameId(trimmed);

&nbsp;   setMenuError(null);

&nbsp;   setJoined(false);

&nbsp; }





&nbsp; const handleHelpClick = () => {

&nbsp;   window.openai?.sendFollowUpMessage?.({

&nbsp;     prompt: `Help me with my chess game. I am playing as ${myColor} and the board is: ${fen}. Please only offer written advice.`

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; };





&nbsp; function onPieceDrop({ sourceSquare, targetSquare }: PieceDropHandlerArgs) {

&nbsp;   if (!gameId || !sourceSquare || !targetSquare || pending) return false;





&nbsp;   const game = gameRef.current;

&nbsp;   if (myColor === "spectator" || game.turn() !== myColor) return false;





&nbsp;   const piece = game.get(sourceSquare as Square);

&nbsp;   if (!piece || piece.color !== myColor) return false;





&nbsp;   const prevFen = game.fen();





&nbsp;   try {

&nbsp;     const local = game.move({ from: sourceSquare, to: targetSquare, promotion: "q" });

&nbsp;     if (!local) return false;

&nbsp;   } catch {

&nbsp;     return false;

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   const nextFen = game.fen();

&nbsp;   setFen(nextFen);

&nbsp;   setPending(true);





&nbsp;   stub

&nbsp;     .move({ from: sourceSquare, to: targetSquare, promotion: "q" }, prevFen)

&nbsp;     .then((r) => {

&nbsp;       if (!r.ok) {

&nbsp;         game.load(r.fen);

&nbsp;         setFen(r.fen);

&nbsp;       }

&nbsp;     })

&nbsp;     .finally(() => setPending(false));





&nbsp;   return true;

&nbsp; }





&nbsp; return (

&nbsp;   <div style={{ padding: "20px", background: "#f8fafc", minHeight: "100vh" }}>

&nbsp;     {!gameId ? (

&nbsp;       <div style={{ maxWidth: "420px", margin: "0 auto", background: "#fff", borderRadius: "16px", padding: "24px" }}>

&nbsp;         <h1>Ready to play?</h1>

&nbsp;         <p>Start a new match or join an existing game.</p>

&nbsp;         <button onClick={handleStartNewGame} style={{ padding: "12px", background: "#2563eb", color: "#fff", border: "none", borderRadius: "8px", cursor: "pointer", width: "100%" }}>

&nbsp;           Start a new game

&nbsp;         </button>

&nbsp;         <div style={{ marginTop: "16px" }}>

&nbsp;           <input

&nbsp;             placeholder="Paste a game ID"

&nbsp;             value={gameIdInput}

&nbsp;             onChange={(e) => setGameIdInput(e.target.value)}

&nbsp;             style={{ width: "100%", padding: "10px", borderRadius: "8px", border: "1px solid #ccc" }}

&nbsp;           />

&nbsp;           <button onClick={handleJoinGame} style={{ marginTop: "8px", padding: "10px", background: "#0f172a", color: "#fff", border: "none", borderRadius: "8px", cursor: "pointer", width: "100%" }}>

&nbsp;             Join

&nbsp;           </button>

&nbsp;           {menuError \&\& <p style={{ color: "red", fontSize: "0.85rem" }}>{menuError}</p>}

&nbsp;         </div>

&nbsp;       </div>

&nbsp;     ) : (

&nbsp;       <div style={{ maxWidth: "600px", margin: "0 auto" }}>

&nbsp;         <div style={{ background: "#fff", padding: "16px", borderRadius: "16px", marginBottom: "16px" }}>

&nbsp;           <h2>Game {gameId}</h2>

&nbsp;           <p>Status: {serverState?.status}</p>

&nbsp;           <button onClick={handleHelpClick} style={{ padding: "10px", background: "#2563eb", color: "#fff", border: "none", borderRadius: "8px", cursor: "pointer" }}>

&nbsp;             Ask for help

&nbsp;           </button>

&nbsp;         </div>

&nbsp;         <div style={{ background: "#fff", padding: "16px", borderRadius: "16px" }}>

&nbsp;           <Chessboard

&nbsp;             position={fen}

&nbsp;             onPieceDrop={onPieceDrop}

&nbsp;             boardOrientation={myColor === "b" ? "black" : "white"}

&nbsp;           />

&nbsp;         </div>

&nbsp;       </div>

&nbsp;     )}

&nbsp;   </div>

&nbsp; );

}





const root = createRoot(document.getElementById("root")!);

root.render(<App />);

```



Note



This is a simplified version of the UI. For the complete implementation with player slots, better styling, and game state management, check out the \[full example on GitHub](https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/tree/main/openai-sdk/chess-app/src/app.tsx).



\## 7. Build and deploy



1\. Build your React UI:



```sh

npm run build

```



This compiles your React app into a single HTML file in the `dist` directory.



1\. Deploy to Cloudflare:



```sh

npx wrangler deploy

```



After deployment, you will see your app URL:



```plaintext

https://my-chess-app.YOUR\_SUBDOMAIN.workers.dev

```



\## 8. Connect to ChatGPT



Now connect your deployed app to ChatGPT:



1\. Open \[ChatGPT](https://chat.openai.com/).

2\. Go to \*\*Settings\*\* > \*\*Apps \& Connectors\*\* > \*\*Create\*\*

3\. Give your app a \*\*name\*\*, and optionally a \*\*description\*\* and \*\*icon\*\*.

4\. Enter your MCP endpoint: `https://my-chess-app.YOUR\_SUBDOMAIN.workers.dev/mcp`.

5\. Select \*\*"No authentication"\*\*.

6\. Select \*\*"Create"\*\*.



\## 9. Play chess in ChatGPT



Try it out:



1\. In your ChatGPT conversation, type: "Let's play chess".

2\. ChatGPT will call the `playChess` tool and render your interactive chess widget.

3\. Select \*\*"Start a new game"\*\* to create a game.

4\. Share the game ID with a friend who can join via their own ChatGPT conversation.

5\. Make moves by dragging pieces on the board.

6\. Select \*\*"Ask for help"\*\* to get strategic advice from ChatGPT



Note



You might need to manually select the connector in the prompt box the first time you use it. Select \*\*"+"\*\* > \*\*"More"\*\* > \*\*\\\[App name]\*\*.



\## Key concepts



\### MCP Server



The Model Context Protocol (MCP) server defines tools and resources that ChatGPT can access:



```ts

const server = new McpServer({ name: "Chess", version: "v1.0.0" });





// Register a UI resource that ChatGPT can render

server.registerResource(

&nbsp; "chess",

&nbsp; "ui://widget/index.html",

&nbsp; {},

&nbsp; async (\_uri, extra) => {

&nbsp;   return {

&nbsp;     contents: \[

&nbsp;       {

&nbsp;         uri: "ui://widget/index.html",

&nbsp;         mimeType: "text/html+skybridge",

&nbsp;         text: await getWidgetHtml(extra.requestInfo?.headers.host as string)

&nbsp;       }

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   };

&nbsp; }

);





// Register a tool that ChatGPT can call to render the UI

server.registerTool(

&nbsp; "playChess",

&nbsp; {

&nbsp;   title: "Renders a chess game menu, ready to start or join a game.",

&nbsp;   annotations: { readOnlyHint: true },

&nbsp;   \_meta: {

&nbsp;     "openai/outputTemplate": "ui://widget/index.html",

&nbsp;     "openai/toolInvocation/invoking": "Opening chess widget",

&nbsp;     "openai/toolInvocation/invoked": "Chess widget opened"

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; },

&nbsp; async (\_, \_extra) => {

&nbsp;   return {

&nbsp;     content: \[{ type: "text", text: "Successfully rendered chess game menu" }]

&nbsp;   };

&nbsp; }

);

```



\### Game Engine with Agents



The `ChessGame` class extends `Agent` to create a stateful game engine:



```tsx

export class ChessGame extends Agent<Env, State> {

&nbsp; initialState: State = {

&nbsp;   board: new Chess().fen(),

&nbsp;   players: {},

&nbsp;   status: "waiting"

&nbsp; };





&nbsp; game = new Chess();





&nbsp; constructor(

&nbsp;   ctx: DurableObjectState,

&nbsp;   public env: Env

&nbsp; ) {

&nbsp;   super(ctx, env);

&nbsp;   this.game.load(this.state.board);

&nbsp; }

```



Each game gets its own Agent instance, enabling:



\* \*\*Isolated state\*\* per game

\* \*\*Real-time synchronization\*\* across players

\* \*\*Persistent storage\*\* that survives worker restarts



\### Callable methods



Use the `@callable()` decorator to expose methods that clients can invoke:



```ts

@callable()

join(params: { playerId: string; preferred?: Color | "any" }) {

&nbsp; const { playerId, preferred = "any" } = params;

&nbsp; const { connection } = getCurrentAgent();

&nbsp; if (!connection) throw new Error("Not connected");





&nbsp; connection.setState({ playerId });

&nbsp; const s = this.state;





&nbsp; // Already seated? Return seat

&nbsp; const already = this.colorOf(playerId);

&nbsp; if (already) {

&nbsp;   return { ok: true, role: already as Color, state: s };

&nbsp; }





&nbsp; // Choose a seat

&nbsp; const free: Color\[] = (\["w", "b"] as const).filter((c) => !s.players\[c]);

&nbsp; if (free.length === 0) {

&nbsp;   return { ok: true, role: "spectator" as const, state: s };

&nbsp; }





&nbsp; let seat: Color = free\[0];

&nbsp; if (preferred === "w" \&\& free.includes("w")) seat = "w";

&nbsp; if (preferred === "b" \&\& free.includes("b")) seat = "b";





&nbsp; s.players\[seat] = playerId;

&nbsp; s.status = s.players.w \&\& s.players.b ? "active" : "waiting";

&nbsp; this.setState(s);

&nbsp; return { ok: true, role: seat, state: s };

}

```



\### React integration



The `useAgent` hook connects your React app to the Durable Object:



```tsx

const { stub } = useAgent<ServerState>({

&nbsp; host,

&nbsp; name: gameId ?? "\_\_lobby\_\_",

&nbsp; agent: "chess",

&nbsp; onStateUpdate: (s) => {

&nbsp;   gameRef.current.load(s.board);

&nbsp;   setFen(s.board);

&nbsp;   setServerState(s);

&nbsp; }

});

```



Call methods on the agent:



```tsx

const res = await stub.join({ playerId, preferred: "any" });

await stub.move({ from: "e2", to: "e4" });

```



\### Bidirectional communication



Your app can send messages to ChatGPT:



```ts

const handleHelpClick = () => {

&nbsp; window.openai?.sendFollowUpMessage?.({

&nbsp;   prompt: `Help me with my chess game. I am playing as ${myColor} and the board is: ${fen}. Please only offer written advice as there are no tools for you to use.`

&nbsp; });

};

```



This creates a new message in the ChatGPT conversation with context about the current game state.

source\_url:

---



Your Agent can connect to external \[Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) servers to access their tools and extend your Agent's capabilities. In this tutorial, you'll create an Agent that connects to an MCP server and uses one of its tools.



\## What you will build



An Agent with endpoints to:



\* Connect to an MCP server

\* List available tools from connected servers

\* Get the connection status



\## Prerequisites



An MCP server to connect to (or use the public example in this tutorial).



\## 1. Create a basic Agent



1\. Create a new Agent project using the `hello-world` template:



&nbsp;  \* npm



&nbsp;    ```sh

&nbsp;    npm create cloudflare@latest -- my-mcp-client --template=cloudflare/ai/demos/hello-world

&nbsp;    ```



&nbsp;  \* yarn



&nbsp;    ```sh

&nbsp;    yarn create cloudflare my-mcp-client --template=cloudflare/ai/demos/hello-world

&nbsp;    ```



&nbsp;  \* pnpm



&nbsp;    ```sh

&nbsp;    pnpm create cloudflare@latest my-mcp-client --template=cloudflare/ai/demos/hello-world

&nbsp;    ```



2\. Move into the project directory:



&nbsp;  ```sh

&nbsp;  cd my-mcp-client

&nbsp;  ```



&nbsp;  Your Agent is ready! The template includes a minimal Agent in `src/index.ts`:



&nbsp;  \* JavaScript



&nbsp;    ```js

&nbsp;    import { Agent, routeAgentRequest } from "agents";





&nbsp;    export class HelloAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;      async onRequest(request) {

&nbsp;        return new Response("Hello, Agent!", { status: 200 });

&nbsp;      }

&nbsp;    }





&nbsp;    export default {

&nbsp;      async fetch(request, env) {

&nbsp;        return (

&nbsp;          (await routeAgentRequest(request, env, { cors: true })) ||

&nbsp;          new Response("Not found", { status: 404 })

&nbsp;        );

&nbsp;      },

&nbsp;    };

&nbsp;    ```



&nbsp;  \* TypeScript



&nbsp;    ```ts

&nbsp;    import { Agent, routeAgentRequest } from "agents";





&nbsp;    type Env = {

&nbsp;      HelloAgent: DurableObjectNamespace<HelloAgent>;

&nbsp;    };





&nbsp;    export class HelloAgent extends Agent<Env, never> {

&nbsp;      async onRequest(request: Request): Promise<Response> {

&nbsp;        return new Response("Hello, Agent!", { status: 200 });

&nbsp;      }

&nbsp;    }





&nbsp;    export default {

&nbsp;      async fetch(request: Request, env: Env) {

&nbsp;        return (

&nbsp;          (await routeAgentRequest(request, env, { cors: true })) ||

&nbsp;          new Response("Not found", { status: 404 })

&nbsp;        );

&nbsp;      },

&nbsp;    } satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

&nbsp;    ```



\## 2. Add MCP connection endpoint



1\. Add an endpoint to connect to MCP servers. Update your Agent class in `src/index.ts`:



&nbsp;  \* JavaScript



&nbsp;    ```js

&nbsp;    export class HelloAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;      async onRequest(request) {

&nbsp;        const url = new URL(request.url);





&nbsp;        // Connect to an MCP server

&nbsp;        if (url.pathname.endsWith("add-mcp") \&\& request.method === "POST") {

&nbsp;          const { serverUrl, name } = await request.json();





&nbsp;          const { id, authUrl } = await this.addMcpServer(name, serverUrl);





&nbsp;          if (authUrl) {

&nbsp;            // OAuth required - return auth URL

&nbsp;            return new Response(JSON.stringify({ serverId: id, authUrl }), {

&nbsp;              headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },

&nbsp;            });

&nbsp;          }





&nbsp;          return new Response(

&nbsp;            JSON.stringify({ serverId: id, status: "connected" }),

&nbsp;            { headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" } },

&nbsp;          );

&nbsp;        }





&nbsp;        return new Response("Not found", { status: 404 });

&nbsp;      }

&nbsp;    }

&nbsp;    ```



&nbsp;  \* TypeScript



&nbsp;    ```ts

&nbsp;    export class HelloAgent extends Agent<Env, never> {

&nbsp;      async onRequest(request: Request): Promise<Response> {

&nbsp;        const url = new URL(request.url);





&nbsp;        // Connect to an MCP server

&nbsp;        if (url.pathname.endsWith("add-mcp") \&\& request.method === "POST") {

&nbsp;          const { serverUrl, name } = (await request.json()) as {

&nbsp;            serverUrl: string;

&nbsp;            name: string;

&nbsp;          };





&nbsp;          const { id, authUrl } = await this.addMcpServer(name, serverUrl);





&nbsp;          if (authUrl) {

&nbsp;            // OAuth required - return auth URL

&nbsp;            return new Response(

&nbsp;              JSON.stringify({ serverId: id, authUrl }),

&nbsp;              { headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" } },

&nbsp;            );

&nbsp;          }





&nbsp;          return new Response(

&nbsp;            JSON.stringify({ serverId: id, status: "connected" }),

&nbsp;            { headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" } },

&nbsp;          );

&nbsp;        }





&nbsp;        return new Response("Not found", { status: 404 });

&nbsp;      }

&nbsp;    }

&nbsp;    ```



The `addMcpServer()` method connects to an MCP server. If the server requires OAuth authentication, it returns an `authUrl` that users must visit to complete authorization.



\## 3. Test the connection



1\. Start your development server:



&nbsp;  ```sh

&nbsp;  npm start

&nbsp;  ```



2\. In a new terminal, connect to an MCP server (using a public example):



&nbsp;  ```sh

&nbsp;  curl -X POST http://localhost:8788/agents/hello-agent/default/add-mcp \\

&nbsp;    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\

&nbsp;    -d '{

&nbsp;      "serverUrl": "https://docs.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp",

&nbsp;      "name": "Example Server"

&nbsp;    }'

&nbsp;  ```



&nbsp;  You should see a response with the server ID:



&nbsp;  ```json

&nbsp;  {

&nbsp;    "serverId": "example-server-id",

&nbsp;    "status": "connected"

&nbsp;  }

&nbsp;  ```



\## 4. List available tools



1\. Add an endpoint to see which tools are available from connected servers:



&nbsp;  \* JavaScript



&nbsp;    ```js

&nbsp;    export class HelloAgent extends Agent {

&nbsp;      async onRequest(request) {

&nbsp;        const url = new URL(request.url);





&nbsp;        // ... previous add-mcp endpoint ...





&nbsp;        // List MCP state (servers, tools, etc)

&nbsp;        if (url.pathname.endsWith("mcp-state") \&\& request.method === "GET") {

&nbsp;          const mcpState = this.getMcpServers();





&nbsp;          return new Response(JSON.stringify(mcpState, null, 2), {

&nbsp;            headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },

&nbsp;          });

&nbsp;        }





&nbsp;        return new Response("Not found", { status: 404 });

&nbsp;      }

&nbsp;    }

&nbsp;    ```



&nbsp;  \* TypeScript



&nbsp;    ```ts

&nbsp;    export class HelloAgent extends Agent<Env, never> {

&nbsp;      async onRequest(request: Request): Promise<Response> {

&nbsp;        const url = new URL(request.url);





&nbsp;        // ... previous add-mcp endpoint ...





&nbsp;        // List MCP state (servers, tools, etc)

&nbsp;        if (url.pathname.endsWith("mcp-state") \&\& request.method === "GET") {

&nbsp;          const mcpState = this.getMcpServers();





&nbsp;          return new Response(JSON.stringify(mcpState, null, 2), {

&nbsp;            headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },

&nbsp;          });

&nbsp;        }





&nbsp;        return new Response("Not found", { status: 404 });

&nbsp;      }

&nbsp;    }

&nbsp;    ```



2\. Test it:



&nbsp;  ```sh

&nbsp;  curl http://localhost:8788/agents/hello-agent/default/mcp-state

&nbsp;  ```



&nbsp;  You'll see all connected servers, their connection states, and available tools:



&nbsp;  ```json

&nbsp;  {

&nbsp;    "servers": {

&nbsp;      "example-server-id": {

&nbsp;        "name": "Example Server",

&nbsp;        "state": "ready",

&nbsp;        "server\_url": "https://docs.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp",

&nbsp;        ...

&nbsp;      }

&nbsp;    },

&nbsp;    "tools": \[

&nbsp;      {

&nbsp;        "name": "add",

&nbsp;        "description": "Add two numbers",

&nbsp;        "serverId": "example-server-id",

&nbsp;        ...

&nbsp;      }

&nbsp;    ]

&nbsp;  }

&nbsp;  ```



\## Summary



You created an Agent that can:



\* Connect to external MCP servers dynamically

\* Handle OAuth authentication flows when required

\* List all available tools from connected servers

\* Monitor connection status



Connections persist in the Agent's \[SQL storage](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/store-and-sync-state/), so they remain active across requests.



\## Next steps



\* \[Handle OAuth flows](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/guides/oauth-mcp-client) — Configure OAuth callbacks and error handling

\* \[McpClient — API reference](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/model-context-protocol/mcp-client-api/) — Complete API documentation



</page>

\## Build an AI Agent with Human Oversight



This guide will show you how to build and deploy an AI agent on Cloudflare Workers that implements human-in-the-loop functionality, allowing AI agents to request human approval before executing certain actions.



Your Human-in-the-Loop Agent will be able to:



\* Request human approval for sensitive tool executions

\* Stream real-time responses using WebSocket connections

\* Persist conversation state across sessions

\* Differentiate between automatic and confirmation-required tools



This pattern is crucial for scenarios where human oversight and confirmation are required before taking important actions like making purchases, sending emails, or modifying data.



You can view the full code for this example \[here](https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/tree/main/guides/human-in-the-loop).



\## Prerequisites



Before you begin, you will need:



\* A \[Cloudflare account](https://dash.cloudflare.com/sign-up)

\* \[Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) installed (v18 or later)

\* An \[OpenAI API key](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys) (or another LLM provider)



\## 1. Create your project



1\. Create a new project for your Human-in-the-Loop Agent:



\* npm



&nbsp; ```sh

&nbsp; npm create cloudflare@latest -- human-in-the-loop

&nbsp; ```



\* yarn



&nbsp; ```sh

&nbsp; yarn create cloudflare human-in-the-loop

&nbsp; ```



\* pnpm



&nbsp; ```sh

&nbsp; pnpm create cloudflare@latest human-in-the-loop

&nbsp; ```



1\. Navigate into your project:



```sh

cd human-in-the-loop

```



1\. Install the required dependencies:



```sh

npm install agents @ai-sdk/openai ai zod react react-dom

```



\## 2. Set up your environment variables



1\. Create a `.dev.vars` file in your project root for local development secrets:



```sh

touch .dev.vars

```



1\. Add your credentials to `.dev.vars`:



```sh

OPENAI\_API\_KEY="your-openai-api-key"

```



1\. Update your wrangler configuration for your Agent:



\* wrangler.jsonc



&nbsp; ```jsonc

&nbsp; {

&nbsp;   "$schema": "./node\_modules/wrangler/config-schema.json",

&nbsp;   "name": "human-in-the-loop",

&nbsp;   "main": "./src/server.ts",

&nbsp;   "compatibility\_date": "2026-02-04",

&nbsp;   "compatibility\_flags": \[

&nbsp;     "nodejs\_compat",

&nbsp;     "nodejs\_compat\_populate\_process\_env"

&nbsp;   ],

&nbsp;   "assets": {

&nbsp;     "directory": "public"

&nbsp;   },

&nbsp;   "durable\_objects": {

&nbsp;     "bindings": \[

&nbsp;       {

&nbsp;         "name": "HumanInTheLoop",

&nbsp;         "class\_name": "HumanInTheLoop"

&nbsp;       }

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   },

&nbsp;   "migrations": \[

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       "tag": "v1",

&nbsp;       "new\_sqlite\_classes": \[

&nbsp;         "HumanInTheLoop"

&nbsp;       ]

&nbsp;     }

&nbsp;   ]

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* wrangler.toml



&nbsp; ```toml

&nbsp; "$schema" = "./node\_modules/wrangler/config-schema.json"

&nbsp; name = "human-in-the-loop"

&nbsp; main = "./src/server.ts"

&nbsp; compatibility\_date = "2026-02-04"

&nbsp; compatibility\_flags = \[ "nodejs\_compat", "nodejs\_compat\_populate\_process\_env" ]





&nbsp; \[assets]

&nbsp; directory = "public"





&nbsp; \[\[durable\_objects.bindings]]

&nbsp; name = "HumanInTheLoop"

&nbsp; class\_name = "HumanInTheLoop"





&nbsp; \[\[migrations]]

&nbsp; tag = "v1"

&nbsp; new\_sqlite\_classes = \[ "HumanInTheLoop" ]

&nbsp; ```



\## 3. Define your tools



Create your tool definitions at `src/tools.ts`. Tools can be configured to either require human confirmation or execute automatically:



```ts

import { tool } from "ai";

import { z } from "zod";

import type { AITool } from "agents/ai-react";





// Server-side tool that requires confirmation (no execute function)

const getWeatherInformationTool = tool({

&nbsp; description:

&nbsp;   "Get the current weather information for a specific city. Always use this tool when the user asks about weather.",

&nbsp; inputSchema: z.object({

&nbsp;   city: z.string().describe("The name of the city to get weather for")

&nbsp; })

&nbsp; // no execute function - requires human approval

});





// Client-side tool that requires confirmation

const getLocalTimeTool = tool({

&nbsp; description: "Get the local time for a specified location",

&nbsp; inputSchema: z.object({ location: z.string() }),

&nbsp; execute: async ({ location }) => {

&nbsp;   console.log(`Getting local time for ${location}`);

&nbsp;   await new Promise((res) => setTimeout(res, 2000));

&nbsp;   return "10am";

&nbsp; }

});





// Server-side tool that does NOT require confirmation

const getLocalNewsTool = tool({

&nbsp; description: "Get local news for a specified location",

&nbsp; inputSchema: z.object({ location: z.string() }),

&nbsp; execute: async ({ location }) => {

&nbsp;   console.log(`Getting local news for ${location}`);

&nbsp;   await new Promise((res) => setTimeout(res, 2000));

&nbsp;   return `${location} kittens found drinking tea this last weekend`;

&nbsp; }

});





// Export AI SDK tools for server-side use

export const tools = {

&nbsp; getLocalTime: {

&nbsp;   description: getLocalTimeTool.description,

&nbsp;   inputSchema: getLocalTimeTool.inputSchema

&nbsp; },

&nbsp; getWeatherInformation: getWeatherInformationTool,

&nbsp; getLocalNews: getLocalNewsTool

};





// Export AITool format for client-side use

export const clientTools: Record<string, AITool> = {

&nbsp; getLocalTime: getLocalTimeTool as AITool,

&nbsp; getWeatherInformation: {

&nbsp;   description: getWeatherInformationTool.description,

&nbsp;   inputSchema: getWeatherInformationTool.inputSchema

&nbsp; },

&nbsp; getLocalNews: {

&nbsp;   description: getLocalNewsTool.description,

&nbsp;   inputSchema: getLocalNewsTool.inputSchema

&nbsp; }

};

```



Note



Tools \*\*without\*\* an `execute` function require human approval before they can run. The server will handle execution after the user confirms. Tools \*\*with\*\* an `execute` function can either run automatically or require confirmation based on your configuration.



\## 4. Create utility functions



Create helper functions at `src/utils.ts` to handle tool confirmations and processing:



```ts

import type { UIMessage } from "@ai-sdk/react";

import type { UIMessageStreamWriter, ToolSet } from "ai";

import type { z } from "zod";





// Approval constants

export const APPROVAL = {

&nbsp; NO: "No, denied.",

&nbsp; YES: "Yes, confirmed."

} as const;





// Tools that require Human-In-The-Loop confirmation

export const toolsRequiringConfirmation = \[

&nbsp; "getLocalTime",

&nbsp; "getWeatherInformation"

];





// Type guard to check if part has required properties

function isToolConfirmationPart(part: unknown): part is {

&nbsp; type: string;

&nbsp; output: string;

&nbsp; input?: Record<string, unknown>;

} {

&nbsp; return (

&nbsp;   typeof part === "object" \&\&

&nbsp;   part !== null \&\&

&nbsp;   "type" in part \&\&

&nbsp;   "output" in part \&\&

&nbsp;   typeof (part as { type: unknown }).type === "string" \&\&

&nbsp;   typeof (part as { output: unknown }).output === "string"

&nbsp; );

}





// Check if a message contains tool confirmations

export function hasToolConfirmation(message: UIMessage): boolean {

&nbsp; return (

&nbsp;   message?.parts?.some(

&nbsp;     (part) =>

&nbsp;       part.type?.startsWith("tool-") \&\&

&nbsp;       toolsRequiringConfirmation.includes(part.type?.slice("tool-".length)) \&\&

&nbsp;       "output" in part

&nbsp;   ) || false

&nbsp; );

}





// Weather tool implementation

export async function getWeatherInformation(args: unknown): Promise<string> {

&nbsp; const { city } = args as { city: string };

&nbsp; const conditions = \["sunny", "cloudy", "rainy", "snowy"];

&nbsp; return `The weather in ${city} is ${

&nbsp;   conditions\[Math.floor(Math.random() \* conditions.length)]

&nbsp; }.`;

}

```



\## 5. Create your Agent



Create your agent implementation at `src/server.ts`:



```ts

import { openai } from "@ai-sdk/openai";

import { routeAgentRequest } from "agents";

import { AIChatAgent } from "agents/ai-chat-agent";

import {

&nbsp; convertToModelMessages,

&nbsp; createUIMessageStream,

&nbsp; createUIMessageStreamResponse,

&nbsp; type StreamTextOnFinishCallback,

&nbsp; streamText,

&nbsp; stepCountIs

} from "ai";

import { tools } from "./tools";

import {

&nbsp; processToolCalls,

&nbsp; hasToolConfirmation,

&nbsp; getWeatherInformation

} from "./utils";





type Env = {

&nbsp; OPENAI\_API\_KEY: string;

};





export class HumanInTheLoop extends AIChatAgent<Env> {

&nbsp; async onChatMessage(onFinish: StreamTextOnFinishCallback<{}>) {

&nbsp;   const startTime = Date.now();

&nbsp;   const lastMessage = this.messages\[this.messages.length - 1];





&nbsp;   // Check if the last message contains tool confirmations

&nbsp;   if (hasToolConfirmation(lastMessage)) {

&nbsp;     // Process tool confirmations using UI stream

&nbsp;     const stream = createUIMessageStream({

&nbsp;       execute: async ({ writer }) => {

&nbsp;         await processToolCalls(

&nbsp;           { writer, messages: this.messages, tools },

&nbsp;           { getWeatherInformation }

&nbsp;         );

&nbsp;       }

&nbsp;     });

&nbsp;     return createUIMessageStreamResponse({ stream });

&nbsp;   }





&nbsp;   // Normal message flow - stream AI response

&nbsp;   const result = streamText({

&nbsp;     messages: convertToModelMessages(this.messages),

&nbsp;     model: openai("gpt-4o"),

&nbsp;     onFinish,

&nbsp;     tools,

&nbsp;     stopWhen: stepCountIs(5)

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return result.toUIMessageStreamResponse({

&nbsp;     messageMetadata: ({ part }) => {

&nbsp;       if (part.type === "start") {

&nbsp;         return {

&nbsp;           model: "gpt-4o",

&nbsp;           createdAt: Date.now(),

&nbsp;           messageCount: this.messages.length

&nbsp;         };

&nbsp;       }

&nbsp;       if (part.type === "finish") {

&nbsp;         return {

&nbsp;           responseTime: Date.now() - startTime,

&nbsp;           totalTokens: part.totalUsage?.totalTokens

&nbsp;         };

&nbsp;       }

&nbsp;     }

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; }

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request: Request, env: Env, \_ctx: ExecutionContext) {

&nbsp;   return (

&nbsp;     (await routeAgentRequest(request, env)) ||

&nbsp;     new Response("Not found", { status: 404 })

&nbsp;   );

&nbsp; }

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



\## 6. Build the React frontend



Create your React chat interface at `src/app.tsx`:



```tsx

import type { UIMessage as Message } from "ai";

import { getToolName, isToolUIPart } from "ai";

import { clientTools } from "./tools";

import { APPROVAL, toolsRequiringConfirmation } from "./utils";

import { useAgentChat, type AITool } from "agents/ai-react";

import { useAgent } from "agents/react";

import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";





export default function Chat() {

&nbsp; const messagesEndRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);





&nbsp; const scrollToBottom = useCallback(() => {

&nbsp;   messagesEndRef.current?.scrollIntoView({ behavior: "smooth" });

&nbsp; }, \[]);





&nbsp; const agent = useAgent({

&nbsp;   agent: "human-in-the-loop"

&nbsp; });





&nbsp; const { messages, sendMessage, addToolResult, clearHistory } = useAgentChat({

&nbsp;   agent,

&nbsp;   experimental\_automaticToolResolution: true,

&nbsp;   toolsRequiringConfirmation,

&nbsp;   tools: clientTools satisfies Record<string, AITool>

&nbsp; });





&nbsp; const \[input, setInput] = useState("");





&nbsp; const handleSubmit = useCallback(

&nbsp;   (e: React.FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) => {

&nbsp;     e.preventDefault();

&nbsp;     if (input.trim()) {

&nbsp;       sendMessage({ role: "user", parts: \[{ type: "text", text: input }] });

&nbsp;       setInput("");

&nbsp;     }

&nbsp;   },

&nbsp;   \[input, sendMessage]

&nbsp; );





&nbsp; // Scroll to bottom when messages change

&nbsp; useEffect(() => {

&nbsp;   messages.length > 0 \&\& scrollToBottom();

&nbsp; }, \[messages, scrollToBottom]);





&nbsp; // Check if there's a pending tool confirmation

&nbsp; const pendingToolCallConfirmation = messages.some((m: Message) =>

&nbsp;   m.parts?.some(

&nbsp;     (part) => isToolUIPart(part) \&\& part.state === "input-available"

&nbsp;   )

&nbsp; );





&nbsp; return (

&nbsp;   <div className="chat-container">

&nbsp;     <div className="messages-wrapper">

&nbsp;       {messages?.map((m: Message) => (

&nbsp;         <div key={m.id} className="message">

&nbsp;           <strong>{`${m.role}: `}</strong>

&nbsp;           {m.parts?.map((part, i) => {

&nbsp;             switch (part.type) {

&nbsp;               case "text":

&nbsp;                 return (

&nbsp;                   <div key={i} className="message-content">

&nbsp;                     {part.text}

&nbsp;                   </div>

&nbsp;                 );

&nbsp;               default:

&nbsp;                 if (isToolUIPart(part)) {

&nbsp;                   const toolCallId = part.toolCallId;

&nbsp;                   const toolName = getToolName(part);





&nbsp;                   // Show tool results for automatic tools

&nbsp;                   if (part.state === "output-available") {

&nbsp;                     return (

&nbsp;                       <div key={toolCallId} className="tool-invocation">

&nbsp;                         <span className="tool-name">{toolName}</span>{" "}

&nbsp;                         returned:{" "}

&nbsp;                         <span className="tool-result">

&nbsp;                           {JSON.stringify(part.output, null, 2)}

&nbsp;                         </span>

&nbsp;                       </div>

&nbsp;                     );

&nbsp;                   }





&nbsp;                   // Render confirmation UI for tools requiring approval

&nbsp;                   if (part.state === "input-available") {

&nbsp;                     const tool = clientTools\[toolName];





&nbsp;                     if (!toolsRequiringConfirmation.includes(toolName)) {

&nbsp;                       return (

&nbsp;                         <div key={toolCallId} className="tool-invocation">

&nbsp;                           <span className="tool-name">{toolName}</span>{" "}

&nbsp;                           executing...

&nbsp;                         </div>

&nbsp;                       );

&nbsp;                     }





&nbsp;                     return (

&nbsp;                       <div key={toolCallId} className="tool-invocation">

&nbsp;                         Run <span className="tool-name">{toolName}</span> with

&nbsp;                         args:{" "}

&nbsp;                         <span className="tool-args">

&nbsp;                           {JSON.stringify(part.input)}

&nbsp;                         </span>

&nbsp;                         <div className="button-container">

&nbsp;                           <button

&nbsp;                             type="button"

&nbsp;                             className="button-approve"

&nbsp;                             onClick={async () => {

&nbsp;                               const output = tool.execute

&nbsp;                                 ? await tool.execute(part.input)

&nbsp;                                 : APPROVAL.YES;

&nbsp;                               addToolResult({

&nbsp;                                 tool: toolName,

&nbsp;                                 output,

&nbsp;                                 toolCallId

&nbsp;                               });

&nbsp;                             }}

&nbsp;                           >

&nbsp;                             Approve

&nbsp;                           </button>

&nbsp;                           <button

&nbsp;                             type="button"

&nbsp;                             className="button-reject"

&nbsp;                             onClick={() => {

&nbsp;                               const output = tool.execute

&nbsp;                                 ? "User declined to run tool"

&nbsp;                                 : APPROVAL.NO;

&nbsp;                               addToolResult({

&nbsp;                                 tool: toolName,

&nbsp;                                 output,

&nbsp;                                 toolCallId

&nbsp;                               });

&nbsp;                             }}

&nbsp;                           >

&nbsp;                             Reject

&nbsp;                           </button>

&nbsp;                         </div>

&nbsp;                       </div>

&nbsp;                     );

&nbsp;                   }

&nbsp;                 }

&nbsp;                 return null;

&nbsp;             }

&nbsp;           })}

&nbsp;         </div>

&nbsp;       ))}

&nbsp;       <div ref={messagesEndRef} />

&nbsp;     </div>





&nbsp;     <form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>

&nbsp;       <input

&nbsp;         disabled={pendingToolCallConfirmation}

&nbsp;         className="chat-input"

&nbsp;         value={input}

&nbsp;         placeholder="Say something..."

&nbsp;         onChange={(e) => setInput(e.target.value)}

&nbsp;       />

&nbsp;     </form>

&nbsp;   </div>

&nbsp; );

}

```



\## 7. Test locally



Start your development server:



```sh

npm run dev

```



Your agent is now running at `http://localhost:8787`.



\### Test the approval flow



1\. Open `http://localhost:8787` in your browser.

2\. Ask the agent about the weather: "What's the weather in San Francisco?"

3\. The agent will attempt to call the `getWeatherInformation` tool.

4\. You will see an approval prompt with \*\*Approve\*\* and \*\*Reject\*\* buttons.

5\. Click \*\*Approve\*\* to allow the tool execution, or \*\*Reject\*\* to deny it.

6\. The agent will respond with the result or acknowledge the rejection.



\### Test automatic tools



1\. Ask the agent for news: "What's the news in London?"

2\. The `getLocalNews` tool will execute automatically without requiring approval.



\## 8. Deploy to production



1\. Before deploying, add your secrets to Cloudflare:



```sh

npx wrangler secret put OPENAI\_API\_KEY

```



1\. Build and deploy your agent:



```sh

npm run deploy

```



After deploying, you will get a production URL like:



```plaintext

https://human-in-the-loop.your-account.workers.dev

```



\## How it works



\### Tool approval flow



The human-in-the-loop pattern works by intercepting tool calls before execution:



1\. \*\*Tool invocation\*\*: The AI decides to call a tool based on user input.

2\. \*\*Approval check\*\*: The system checks if the tool requires human confirmation.

3\. \*\*Confirmation prompt\*\*: If approval is required, the UI displays the tool name and arguments with Approve/Reject buttons.

4\. \*\*User decision\*\*: The user reviews the action and makes a decision.

5\. \*\*Execution or rejection\*\*: Based on the user's choice, the tool either executes or returns a rejection message.



\### Message streaming with confirmations



The agent uses the Vercel AI SDK's streaming capabilities:



\* `createUIMessageStream` creates a stream for processing tool confirmations.

\* `streamText` handles normal AI responses with tool calls.

\* The `hasToolConfirmation` function detects when a message contains a tool confirmation response.



\### State persistence



Your agent uses \[Durable Objects](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/) to maintain conversation state:



\* Conversation history persists across browser refreshes.

\* Each agent instance has isolated storage.

\* Tool confirmation states are tracked in the message history.



\## Customizing your agent



\### Add more tools requiring confirmation



Add new tools to the `toolsRequiringConfirmation` array in `src/utils.ts`:



```ts

export const toolsRequiringConfirmation = \[

&nbsp; "getLocalTime",

&nbsp; "getWeatherInformation",

&nbsp; "sendEmail", // Add your new tools here

&nbsp; "makePurchase"

];

```



\### Implement custom tool handlers



For server-side tools requiring confirmation, add execute functions in your agent:



```ts

if (hasToolConfirmation(lastMessage)) {

&nbsp; const stream = createUIMessageStream({

&nbsp;   execute: async ({ writer }) => {

&nbsp;     await processToolCalls(

&nbsp;       { writer, messages: this.messages, tools },

&nbsp;       {

&nbsp;         getWeatherInformation,

&nbsp;         sendEmail: async ({ to, subject, body }) => {

&nbsp;           // Your email sending logic

&nbsp;           return `Email sent to ${to}`;

&nbsp;         }

&nbsp;       }

&nbsp;     );

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; });

&nbsp; return createUIMessageStreamResponse({ stream });

}

```



\### Customize the approval UI



Enhance the confirmation interface with more context:



```tsx

if (part.state === "input-available") {

&nbsp; return (

&nbsp;   <div className="tool-approval-card">

&nbsp;     <h3>Action Required</h3>

&nbsp;     <p>

&nbsp;       The AI wants to execute: <strong>{toolName}</strong>

&nbsp;     </p>

&nbsp;     <pre>{JSON.stringify(part.input, null, 2)}</pre>

&nbsp;     <div className="approval-buttons">

&nbsp;       <button className="approve" onClick={() => handleApprove(part)}>

&nbsp;         ✓ Approve

&nbsp;       </button>

&nbsp;       <button className="reject" onClick={() => handleReject(part)}>

&nbsp;         ✗ Reject

&nbsp;       </button>

&nbsp;     </div>

&nbsp;   </div>

&nbsp; );

}

```



\### Use different LLM providers



Replace OpenAI with \[Workers AI](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/):



```ts

import { createWorkersAI } from "workers-ai-provider";





export class HumanInTheLoop extends AIChatAgent<Env> {

&nbsp; async onChatMessage(onFinish: StreamTextOnFinishCallback<{}>) {

&nbsp;   const workersai = createWorkersAI({ binding: this.env.AI });





&nbsp;   const result = streamText({

&nbsp;     messages: convertToModelMessages(this.messages),

&nbsp;     model: workersai("@cf/meta/llama-3-8b-instruct"),

&nbsp;     onFinish,

&nbsp;     tools

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return result.toUIMessageStreamResponse();

&nbsp; }

}

```



\## Best practices



\* \*\*Define clear approval workflows\*\* — Only require confirmation for actions with meaningful consequences (payments, emails, data changes).

\* \*\*Provide detailed context\*\* — Show users exactly what the tool will do, including all arguments.

\* \*\*Implement timeouts\*\* — Consider auto-rejecting tools after a reasonable timeout period.

\* \*\*Handle connection drops\*\* — Ensure the UI can recover if the WebSocket connection is interrupted.

\* \*\*Log all decisions\*\* — Track approval/rejection decisions for audit trails.

\* \*\*Graceful degradation\*\* — Provide fallback behavior if tools are rejected.



\## Next steps



\* Add \[email notifications](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-routing/email-workers/send-email-workers/) for pending approvals

\* Implement approval timeouts with \[Schedules](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/schedule-tasks)

\* Connect your Agent to an \[MCP server](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/model-context-protocol/mcp-client-api/)

\* Add \[analytics](https://developers.cloudflare.com/analytics/analytics-engine/) to track approval patterns

\* Implement multi-user approval workflows
