\# gemma-7b-it-lora Beta



Text Generation • Google



@cf/google/gemma-7b-it-lora



This is a Gemma-7B base model that Cloudflare dedicates for inference with LoRA adapters. Gemma is a family of lightweight, state-of-the-art open models from Google, built from the same research and technology used to create the Gemini models.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 3,500 tokens |

| LoRA | Yes |

| Beta | Yes |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/google/gemma-7b-it-lora)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/google/gemma-7b-it-lora", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/google/gemma-7b-it-lora", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/google/gemma-7b-it-lora",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/google/gemma-7b-it-lora \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.

\# gemma-sea-lion-v4-27b-it



Text Generation • aisingapore



@cf/aisingapore/gemma-sea-lion-v4-27b-it



SEA-LION stands for Southeast Asian Languages In One Network, which is a collection of Large Language Models (LLMs) which have been pretrained and instruct-tuned for the Southeast Asia (SEA) region.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 128,000 tokens |

| Unit Pricing | $0.35 per M input tokens, $0.56 per M output tokens |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/aisingapore/gemma-sea-lion-v4-27b-it)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/aisingapore/gemma-sea-lion-v4-27b-it", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/aisingapore/gemma-sea-lion-v4-27b-it", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/aisingapore/gemma-sea-lion-v4-27b-it",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/aisingapore/gemma-sea-lion-v4-27b-it \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```

Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 2000



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.

&nbsp;       \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5

&nbsp;       \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;         Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp;       \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50

&nbsp;       \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2

&nbsp;         Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp;       \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;         Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.

\# gpt-oss-120b



Text Generation • OpenAI



@cf/openai/gpt-oss-120b



OpenAI’s open-weight models designed for powerful reasoning, agentic tasks, and versatile developer use cases – gpt-oss-120b is for production, general purpose, high reasoning use-cases.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 128,000 tokens |

| Unit Pricing | $0.35 per M input tokens, $0.75 per M output tokens |



\## Usage



Worker



```ts

export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run('@cf/openai/gpt-oss-120b', {

&nbsp;     instructions: 'You are a concise assistant.',

&nbsp;     input: 'What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World?',

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID")

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/v1/responses",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "model": "@cf/openai/gpt-oss-120b",

&nbsp;     "input": "Tell me all about PEP-8"

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/v1/responses   -H "Content-Type: application/json"   -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN"   -d '{

&nbsp;   "model": "@cf/openai/gpt-oss-120b",

&nbsp;   "input": "What are the benefits of open-source models?"

&nbsp; }'

```



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `input` required



&nbsp;   \* `0` string



&nbsp;     Responses API Input messages. Refer to OpenAI Responses API docs to learn more about supported content types



&nbsp;   \* `1` array



&nbsp;     Responses API Input messages. Refer to OpenAI Responses API docs to learn more about supported content types



&nbsp; \* `reasoning` object



&nbsp;   \* `effort` string



&nbsp;     Constrains effort on reasoning for reasoning models. Currently supported values are low, medium, and high. Reducing reasoning effort can result in faster responses and fewer tokens used on reasoning in a response.



&nbsp;   \* `summary` string



&nbsp;     A summary of the reasoning performed by the model. This can be useful for debugging and understanding the model's reasoning process. One of auto, concise, or detailed.



\* `1` object



&nbsp; \* `requests` array required

&nbsp;         Responses API Input messages. Refer to OpenAI Responses API docs to learn more about supported content types

&nbsp;       \* `effort` string

&nbsp;       \* `summary` string



&nbsp;         A summary of the reasoning performed by the model. This can be useful for debugging and understanding the model's reasoning process. One of auto, concise, or detailed.

!\[IBM logo](https://developers.cloudflare.com/\_astro/ibm.Bqbnu\_R0.svg)



\# granite-4.0-h-micro



Text Generation • IBM



@cf/ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-micro



Granite 4.0 instruct models deliver strong performance across benchmarks, achieving industry-leading results in key agentic tasks like instruction following and function calling. These efficiencies make the models well-suited for a wide range of use cases like retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), multi-agent workflows, and edge deployments.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 131,000 tokens |

| Function calling\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/function-calling) | Yes |

| Unit Pricing | $0.017 per M input tokens, $0.11 per M output tokens |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-micro)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-micro", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```

Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



\* `1` object

&nbsp;   An array of message objects representing the conversation history.



&nbsp;   \* `items` object

&nbsp;       The role of the message sender (e.g., 'user', 'assistant', 'system', 'tool').

&nbsp;     \* `name` string required

\# hermes-2-pro-mistral-7b Beta



Text Generation • nousresearch



@hf/nousresearch/hermes-2-pro-mistral-7b



Hermes 2 Pro on Mistral 7B is the new flagship 7B Hermes! Hermes 2 Pro is an upgraded, retrained version of Nous Hermes 2, consisting of an updated and cleaned version of the OpenHermes 2.5 Dataset, as well as a newly introduced Function Calling and JSON Mode dataset developed in-house.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 24,000 tokens |

| More information | \[link](https://huggingface.co/NousResearch/Hermes-2-Pro-Mistral-7B) |

| Function calling\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/function-calling) | Yes |

| Beta | Yes |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@hf/nousresearch/hermes-2-pro-mistral-7b)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@hf/nousresearch/hermes-2-pro-mistral-7b", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@hf/nousresearch/hermes-2-pro-mistral-7b", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@hf/nousresearch/hermes-2-pro-mistral-7b",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@hf/nousresearch/hermes-2-pro-mistral-7b \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



\* `1` object

\# indictrans2-en-indic-1B



Translation • ai4bharat



@cf/ai4bharat/indictrans2-en-indic-1B



IndicTrans2 is the first open-source transformer-based multilingual NMT model that supports high-quality translations across all the 22 scheduled Indic languages



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Unit Pricing | $0.34 per M input tokens, $0.34 per M output tokens |



\## Usage



Workers - TypeScript



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run(

&nbsp;     "@cf/ai4bharat/indictrans2-en-indic-1B",

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       text: "I'll have an order of the moule frites",

&nbsp;       source\_lang: "english", // defaults to english

&nbsp;       target\_lang: "french",

&nbsp;     }

&nbsp;   );





&nbsp;   return new Response(JSON.stringify(response));

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import requests





API\_BASE\_URL = "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/"

headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer {API\_TOKEN}"}





def run(model, input):

&nbsp;   response = requests.post(f"{API\_BASE\_URL}{model}", headers=headers, json=input)

&nbsp;   return response.json()





output = run('@cf/ai4bharat/indictrans2-en-indic-1B', {

&nbsp; "text": "I'll have an order of the moule frites",

&nbsp; "source\_lang": "english",

&nbsp; "target\_lang": "french"

})





print(output)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/ai4bharat/indictrans2-en-indic-1B  \\

&nbsp;   -X POST  \\

&nbsp;   -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_API\_TOKEN"  \\

&nbsp;   -d '{ "text": "Ill have an order of the moule frites", "source\_lang": "english", "target\_lang": "french" }'

```

&nbsp;   Input text to translate. Can be a single string or a list of strings.



&nbsp; \* `1` array



&nbsp;   Input text to translate. Can be a single string or a list of strings.



&nbsp;   \* `items` string



\* `target\_language` string required default hin\\\_Deva



&nbsp; Target langauge to translate to



\### Output



\* `translations` array required



&nbsp; Translated texts



&nbsp; \* `items` string

\# llama-2-13b-chat-awq Beta



Text Generation • thebloke



@hf/thebloke/llama-2-13b-chat-awq



Llama 2 13B Chat AWQ is an efficient, accurate and blazing-fast low-bit weight quantized Llama 2 variant.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Deprecated | 10/1/2025 |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 4,096 tokens |

| More information | \[link](https://huggingface.co/TheBloke/Llama-2-13B-chat-AWQ) |

| Beta | Yes |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@hf/thebloke/llama-2-13b-chat-awq)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@hf/thebloke/llama-2-13b-chat-awq", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker

OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



\* `1` object



&nbsp; \* `messages` array required



&nbsp;   An array of message objects representing the conversation history.



&nbsp;   \* `items` object



&nbsp;     \* `role` string required



&nbsp;       The role of the message sender (e.g., 'user', 'assistant', 'system', 'tool').



&nbsp;     \* `content` string required



&nbsp;       The content of the message as a string.



&nbsp; \* `functions` array



&nbsp;   \* `items` object



&nbsp;     \* `name` string required



&nbsp;     \* `code` string required



&nbsp; \* `tools` array



&nbsp;   A list of tools available for the assistant to use.



&nbsp;   \* `items` one of



&nbsp;     \* `0` object



&nbsp;       \* `name` string required



&nbsp;         The name of the tool. More descriptive the better.



&nbsp;       \* `description` string required



&nbsp;         A brief description of what the tool does.



&nbsp;       \* `parameters` object required



&nbsp;         Schema defining the parameters accepted by the tool.



&nbsp;         \* `type` string required



&nbsp;           The type of the parameters object (usually 'object').

&nbsp;           \* `items` string



&nbsp;         \* `properties` object required

&nbsp;             \* `type` string required

&nbsp;               A description of the expected parameter.



&nbsp;     \* `1` object



&nbsp;       \* `type` string required



&nbsp;         Specifies the type of tool (e.g., 'function').



&nbsp;       \* `function` object required



&nbsp;         Details of the function tool.



&nbsp;         \* `name` string required



&nbsp;           The name of the function.



&nbsp;         \* `description` string required



&nbsp;           A brief description of what the function does.



&nbsp;         \* `parameters` object required



&nbsp;           Schema defining the parameters accepted by the function.



&nbsp;           \* `type` string required



&nbsp;             The type of the parameters object (usually 'object').



&nbsp;           \* `required` array



&nbsp;             List of required parameter names.



&nbsp;             \* `items` string



&nbsp;           \* `properties` object required



&nbsp;             Definitions of each parameter.



&nbsp;             \* `additionalProperties` object



&nbsp;               \* `type` string required



&nbsp;                 The data type of the parameter.



&nbsp;               \* `description` string required



&nbsp;                 A description of the expected parameter.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



\### Output



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `response` string required



&nbsp;   The generated text response from the model



&nbsp; \* `usage` object



&nbsp;   Usage statistics for the inference request



&nbsp;   \* `prompt\_tokens` number 0



&nbsp;     Total number of tokens in input



&nbsp;   \* `completion\_tokens` number 0



&nbsp;     Total number of tokens in output



&nbsp;   \* `total\_tokens` number 0



&nbsp;     Total number of input and output tokens



&nbsp; \* `tool\_calls` array



&nbsp;   An array of tool calls requests made during the response generation



&nbsp;   \* `items` object



&nbsp;     \* `arguments` object



&nbsp;       The arguments passed to be passed to the tool call request



&nbsp;     \* `name` string



&nbsp;       The name of the tool to be called



\* `1` string

\# llama-2-7b-chat-fp16



Text Generation • Meta



@cf/meta/llama-2-7b-chat-fp16



Full precision (fp16) generative text model with 7 billion parameters from Meta



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 4,096 tokens |

| Terms and License | \[link](https://ai.meta.com/resources/models-and-libraries/llama-downloads/) |

| More information | \[link](https://ai.meta.com/llama/) |

| Unit Pricing | $0.56 per M input tokens, $6.67 per M output tokens |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/meta/llama-2-7b-chat-fp16)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-2-7b-chat-fp16", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-2-7b-chat-fp16", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-2-7b-chat-fp16",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-2-7b-chat-fp16 \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string

&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string

&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.

&nbsp;               A description of the expected parameter.



&nbsp;     \* `1` object



&nbsp;       \* `type` string required



&nbsp;         Specifies the type of tool (e.g., 'function').



&nbsp;       \* `function` object required



&nbsp;         Details of the function tool.

&nbsp;           The name of the function.



&nbsp;         \* `description` string required



&nbsp;           A brief description of what the function does.



&nbsp;         \* `parameters` object required



&nbsp;           Schema defining the parameters accepted by the function.



&nbsp;           \* `type` string required



&nbsp;             The type of the parameters object (usually 'object').



&nbsp;           \* `required` array



&nbsp;             List of required parameter names.



&nbsp;             \* `items` string



&nbsp;           \* `properties` object required



&nbsp;             Definitions of each parameter.



&nbsp;             \* `additionalProperties` object



&nbsp;               \* `type` string required



&nbsp;                 The data type of the parameter.



&nbsp;               \* `description` string required



&nbsp;                 A description of the expected parameter.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



\### Output



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `response` string required



&nbsp;   The generated text response from the model

&nbsp;   \* `total\_tokens` number 0

&nbsp;   \* `items` object



&nbsp;     \* `arguments` object



&nbsp;       The arguments passed to be passed to the tool call request



&nbsp;     \* `name` string



&nbsp;       The name of the tool to be called



\* `1` string

\# llama-2-7b-chat-hf-lora Beta



Text Generation • meta-llama



@cf/meta-llama/llama-2-7b-chat-hf-lora



This is a Llama2 base model that Cloudflare dedicated for inference with LoRA adapters. Llama 2 is a collection of pretrained and fine-tuned generative text models ranging in scale from 7 billion to 70 billion parameters. This is the repository for the 7B fine-tuned model, optimized for dialogue use cases and converted for the Hugging Face Transformers format.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 8,192 tokens |

| LoRA | Yes |

| Beta | Yes |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/meta-llama/llama-2-7b-chat-hf-lora)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta-llama/llama-2-7b-chat-hf-lora", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta-llama/llama-2-7b-chat-hf-lora", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/meta-llama/llama-2-7b-chat-hf-lora",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/meta-llama/llama-2-7b-chat-hf-lora \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string

&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



\* `1` object

&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256

&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999

&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.

\# llama-2-7b-chat-int8



Text Generation • Meta



@cf/meta/llama-2-7b-chat-int8



Quantized (int8) generative text model with 7 billion parameters from Meta



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 8,192 tokens |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/meta/llama-2-7b-chat-int8)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-2-7b-chat-int8", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-2-7b-chat-int8", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-2-7b-chat-int8",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-2-7b-chat-int8 \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



\* `1` object



&nbsp; \* `messages` array required



&nbsp;   An array of message objects representing the conversation history.



&nbsp;   \* `items` object



&nbsp;     \* `role` string required



&nbsp;       The role of the message sender (e.g., 'user', 'assistant', 'system', 'tool').



&nbsp;     \* `content` string required



&nbsp;       The content of the message as a string.



&nbsp; \* `functions` array



&nbsp;   \* `items` object



&nbsp;     \* `name` string required



&nbsp;     \* `code` string required

\# llama-3-8b-instruct



Text Generation • Meta



@cf/meta/llama-3-8b-instruct



Generation over generation, Meta Llama 3 demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on a wide range of industry benchmarks and offers new capabilities, including improved reasoning.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 7,968 tokens |

| Terms and License | \[link](https://llama.meta.com/llama3/license/#) |

| More information | \[link](https://llama.meta.com) |

| Unit Pricing | $0.28 per M input tokens, $0.83 per M output tokens |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/meta/llama-3-8b-instruct)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-3-8b-instruct", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-3-8b-instruct", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-3-8b-instruct",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-3-8b-instruct \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



\* `1` object



&nbsp; \* `messages` array required



&nbsp;   An array of message objects representing the conversation history.



&nbsp;   \* `items` object

&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.

\# llama-3-8b-instruct-awq



Text Generation • Meta



@cf/meta/llama-3-8b-instruct-awq



Quantized (int4) generative text model with 8 billion parameters from Meta.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 8,192 tokens |

| Terms and License | \[link](https://llama.meta.com/llama3/license/#) |

| More information | \[link](https://llama.meta.com) |

| Unit Pricing | $0.12 per M input tokens, $0.27 per M output tokens |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/meta/llama-3-8b-instruct-awq)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-3-8b-instruct-awq", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-3-8b-instruct-awq", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-3-8b-instruct-awq",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-3-8b-instruct-awq \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2

&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.

&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.

\# llama-3.1-70b-instruct



Text Generation • Meta



@cf/meta/llama-3.1-70b-instruct



The Meta Llama 3.1 collection of multilingual large language models (LLMs) is a collection of pretrained and instruction tuned generative models. The Llama 3.1 instruction tuned text only models are optimized for multilingual dialogue use cases and outperform many of the available open source and closed chat models on common industry benchmarks.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 24,000 tokens |

| Terms and License | \[link](https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-models/blob/main/models/llama3\_1/LICENSE) |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/meta/llama-3.1-70b-instruct)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-3.1-70b-instruct", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-3.1-70b-instruct", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-3.1-70b-instruct",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-3.1-70b-instruct \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `image` one of



&nbsp;   \* `0` array



&nbsp;     An array of integers that represent the image data constrained to 8-bit unsigned integer values



&nbsp;     \* `items` number



&nbsp;       A value between 0 and 255



&nbsp;   \* `1` string



&nbsp;     Binary string representing the image contents.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1 max 131072



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



\* `1` object

&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.
