\# llama-3.1-8b-instruct



Text Generation • Meta



@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct



The Meta Llama 3.1 collection of multilingual large language models (LLMs) is a collection of pretrained and instruction tuned generative models. The Llama 3.1 instruction tuned text only models are optimized for multilingual dialogue use cases and outperform many of the available open source and closed chat models on common industry benchmarks.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 7,968 tokens |

| Terms and License | \[link](https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-models/blob/main/models/llama3\_1/LICENSE) |

| Unit Pricing | $0.28 per M input tokens, $0.83 per M output tokens |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.

\# llama-3.1-8b-instruct-awq



Text Generation • Meta



@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-awq



Quantized (int4) generative text model with 8 billion parameters from Meta.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 8,192 tokens |

| Terms and License | \[link](https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-models/blob/main/models/llama3\_1/LICENSE) |

| Unit Pricing | $0.12 per M input tokens, $0.27 per M output tokens |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-awq)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-awq", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-awq", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-awq",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-awq \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```

&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.

\# llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fast



Text Generation • Meta



@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fast



\\\[Fast version] The Meta Llama 3.1 collection of multilingual large language models (LLMs) is a collection of pretrained and instruction tuned generative models. The Llama 3.1 instruction tuned text only models are optimized for multilingual dialogue use cases and outperform many of the available open source and closed chat models on common industry benchmarks.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 128,000 tokens |

| Terms and License | \[link](https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-models/blob/main/models/llama3\_1/LICENSE) |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fast)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fast", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fast", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fast",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```

```sh
&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).

\# llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fp8



Text Generation • Meta



@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fp8



Llama 3.1 8B quantized to FP8 precision



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 32,000 tokens |

| Terms and License | \[link](https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-models/blob/main/models/llama3\_1/LICENSE) |

| Unit Pricing | $0.15 per M input tokens, $0.29 per M output tokens |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fp8)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fp8", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fp8", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fp8",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```




OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.

\# llama-3.2-11b-vision-instruct



Text Generation • Meta



@cf/meta/llama-3.2-11b-vision-instruct



The Llama 3.2-Vision instruction-tuned models are optimized for visual recognition, image reasoning, captioning, and answering general questions about an image.



Note



To use Llama 3.2 11b Vision Instruct, you need to agree to the \[Meta License ](https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-models/blob/main/models/llama3\_2/LICENSE)and \[Acceptable Use Policy ](https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-models/blob/main/models/llama3\_2/USE\_POLICY.md). To do so, please send an initial request to `@cf/meta/llama-3.2-11b-vision-instruct` with `"prompt" : "agree"`. After that, you'll be able to use the model as normal.



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-3.2-11b-vision-instruct \\

&nbsp;  -X POST \\

&nbsp;  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp;  -d '{ "prompt": "agree"}'

```



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 128,000 tokens |

| Terms and License | \[link](https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-models/blob/main/models/llama3\_2/LICENSE) |

| LoRA | Yes |

| Unit Pricing | $0.049 per M input tokens, $0.68 per M output tokens |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/meta/llama-3.2-11b-vision-instruct)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-3.2-11b-vision-instruct", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];
```

```py
prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-3.2-11b-vision-instruct",

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)
```

\# llama-3.2-3b-instruct



Text Generation • Meta



@cf/meta/llama-3.2-3b-instruct



The Llama 3.2 instruction-tuned text only models are optimized for multilingual dialogue use cases, including agentic retrieval and summarization tasks.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 128,000 tokens |

| Terms and License | \[link](https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-models/blob/main/models/llama3\_2/LICENSE) |

| Unit Pricing | $0.051 per M input tokens, $0.34 per M output tokens |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/meta/llama-3.2-3b-instruct)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-3.2-3b-instruct", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-3.2-3b-instruct", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-3.2-3b-instruct",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-3.2-3b-instruct \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



\* `1` object



&nbsp; \* `messages` array required



&nbsp;   An array of message objects representing the conversation history.



&nbsp;   \* `items` object



&nbsp;     \* `role` string required



&nbsp;       The role of the message sender (e.g., 'user', 'assistant', 'system', 'tool').



&nbsp;     \* `content` string required



&nbsp;       The content of the message as a string.

&nbsp;   \* `items` object



&nbsp;     \* `name` string required



&nbsp;     \* `code` string required



&nbsp; \* `tools` array



&nbsp;   A list of tools available for the assistant to use.



&nbsp;   \* `items` one of



&nbsp;     \* `0` object



&nbsp;       \* `name` string required



&nbsp;         The name of the tool. More descriptive the better.



&nbsp;       \* `description` string required



&nbsp;         A brief description of what the tool does.

\# llama-3.2-1b-instruct



Text Generation • Meta



@cf/meta/llama-3.2-1b-instruct



The Llama 3.2 instruction-tuned text only models are optimized for multilingual dialogue use cases, including agentic retrieval and summarization tasks.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 60,000 tokens |

| Terms and License | \[link](https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-models/blob/main/models/llama3\_2/LICENSE) |

| Unit Pricing | $0.027 per M input tokens, $0.20 per M output tokens |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/meta/llama-3.2-1b-instruct)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-3.2-1b-instruct", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-3.2-1b-instruct", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-3.2-1b-instruct",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-3.2-1b-instruct \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



\* `1` object



&nbsp; \* `messages` array required



&nbsp;   An array of message objects representing the conversation history.



&nbsp;   \* `items` object



&nbsp;     \* `role` string required



&nbsp;       The role of the message sender (e.g., 'user', 'assistant', 'system', 'tool').



&nbsp;     \* `content` string required

&nbsp;     \* `code` string required

&nbsp;     \* `0` object

\# llama-3.3-70b-instruct-fp8-fast



Text Generation • Meta



@cf/meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct-fp8-fast



Llama 3.3 70B quantized to fp8 precision, optimized to be faster.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 24,000 tokens |

| Terms and License | \[link](https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-models/blob/main/models/llama3\_3/LICENSE) |

| Function calling\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/function-calling) | Yes |

| Batch | Yes |

| Unit Pricing | $0.29 per M input tokens, $2.25 per M output tokens |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct-fp8-fast)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct-fp8-fast", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker




Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct-fp8-fast",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```

\# llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct



Text Generation • Meta



@cf/meta/llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct



Meta's Llama 4 Scout is a 17 billion parameter model with 16 experts that is natively multimodal. These models leverage a mixture-of-experts architecture to offer industry-leading performance in text and image understanding.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 131,000 tokens |

| Terms and License | \[link](https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-models/blob/main/models/llama4/LICENSE) |

| Function calling\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/function-calling) | Yes |

| Batch | Yes |

| Unit Pricing | $0.27 per M input tokens, $0.85 per M output tokens |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/meta/llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```

\## API Schemas



The following schemas are based on JSON Schema



\* Input

!\[Meta logo](https://developers.cloudflare.com/\_astro/meta.x5nlFKBG.svg)



\# llama-guard-3-8b



Text Generation • Meta



@cf/meta/llama-guard-3-8b



Llama Guard 3 is a Llama-3.1-8B pretrained model, fine-tuned for content safety classification. Similar to previous versions, it can be used to classify content in both LLM inputs (prompt classification) and in LLM responses (response classification). It acts as an LLM – it generates text in its output that indicates whether a given prompt or response is safe or unsafe, and if unsafe, it also lists the content categories violated.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 131,072 tokens |

| LoRA | Yes |

| Unit Pricing | $0.48 per M input tokens, $0.03 per M output tokens |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/meta/llama-guard-3-8b)



\## Usage



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {

&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: 'user',

&nbsp;       content: 'I wanna bully someone online',

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: 'assistant',

&nbsp;       content: 'That sounds interesting, how can I help?',

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-guard-3-8b", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-guard-3-8b",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": "I want to bully somebody online"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "assistant", "content": "Interesting. Let me know how I can be of assistance?"},

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/meta/llama-guard-3-8b \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "user", "content": "I want to bully someone online" }, {"role": "assistant", "content": "Interesting. How can I assist you?"}]}'

```



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `messages` array required



&nbsp; An array of message objects representing the conversation history.



&nbsp; \* `items` object



&nbsp;   \* `role` required



&nbsp;     The role of the message sender must alternate between 'user' and 'assistant'.



&nbsp;   \* `content` string required



&nbsp;     The content of the message as a string.



\* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp; The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



\* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp; Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



\* `response\_format` object



&nbsp; Dictate the output format of the generated response.



&nbsp; \* `type` string



&nbsp;   Set to json\\\_object to process and output generated text as JSON.



\### Output



\* `response` one of



&nbsp; \* `0` string



&nbsp;   The generated text response from the model.



&nbsp; \* `1` object



&nbsp;   The json response parsed from the generated text response from the model.



&nbsp;   \* `safe` boolean



&nbsp;     Whether the conversation is safe or not.



&nbsp;   \* `categories` array



&nbsp;     A list of what hazard categories predicted for the conversation, if the conversation is deemed unsafe.



&nbsp;     \* `items` string



&nbsp;       Hazard category classname, from S1 to S14.



\* `usage` object



&nbsp; Usage statistics for the inference request



&nbsp; \* `prompt\_tokens` number 0



&nbsp;   Total number of tokens in input



&nbsp; \* `completion\_tokens` number 0



&nbsp;   Total number of tokens in output



&nbsp; \* `total\_tokens` number 0



&nbsp;   Total number of input and output tokens

\# llamaguard-7b-awq Beta



Text Generation • thebloke



@hf/thebloke/llamaguard-7b-awq



Llama Guard is a model for classifying the safety of LLM prompts and responses, using a taxonomy of safety risks.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Deprecated | 10/1/2025 |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 4,096 tokens |

| Beta | Yes |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@hf/thebloke/llamaguard-7b-awq)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@hf/thebloke/llamaguard-7b-awq", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@hf/thebloke/llamaguard-7b-awq", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python

```py
import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@hf/thebloke/llamaguard-7b-awq",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@hf/thebloke/llamaguard-7b-awq \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'
```

OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



\* `1` object



&nbsp; \* `messages` array required



&nbsp;   An array of message objects representing the conversation history.



&nbsp;   \* `items` object



&nbsp;     \* `role` string required



&nbsp;       The role of the message sender (e.g., 'user', 'assistant', 'system', 'tool').



&nbsp;     \* `content` string required



&nbsp;       The content of the message as a string.



&nbsp; \* `functions` array



&nbsp;   \* `items` object



&nbsp;     \* `name` string required



&nbsp;     \* `code` string required



&nbsp; \* `tools` array



&nbsp;   A list of tools available for the assistant to use.



&nbsp;   \* `items` one of



&nbsp;     \* `0` object



&nbsp;       \* `name` string required



&nbsp;         The name of the tool. More descriptive the better.



&nbsp;       \* `description` string required

\# llava-1.5-7b-hf Beta



Image-to-Text • llava-hf



@cf/llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf



LLaVA is an open-source chatbot trained by fine-tuning LLaMA/Vicuna on GPT-generated multimodal instruction-following data. It is an auto-regressive language model, based on the transformer architecture.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Beta | Yes |



\## Usage



Workers - TypeScript



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}









export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request: Request, env: Env): Promise<Response> {

&nbsp;   const res = await fetch("https://cataas.com/cat");

&nbsp;   const blob = await res.arrayBuffer();

&nbsp;   const input = {

&nbsp;     image: \[...new Uint8Array(blob)],

&nbsp;     prompt: "Generate a caption for this image",

&nbsp;     max\_tokens: 512,

&nbsp;   };

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run(

&nbsp;     "@cf/llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf",

&nbsp;     input

&nbsp;     );

&nbsp;   return new Response(JSON.stringify(response));

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` string



&nbsp; Binary string representing the image contents.



\* `1` object



&nbsp; \* `image` one of required



&nbsp;   \* `0` array



&nbsp;     An array of integers that represent the image data constrained to 8-bit unsigned integer values



&nbsp;     \* `items` number



&nbsp;       A value between 0 and 255



&nbsp;   \* `1` string



&nbsp;     Binary string representing the image contents.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number



&nbsp;   Controls the creativity of the AI's responses by adjusting how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` number



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` number



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 512



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



\### Output



\* `description` string

\# lucid-origin



Text-to-Image • Leonardo



@cf/leonardo/lucid-origin



Lucid Origin from Leonardo.AI is their most adaptable and prompt-responsive model to date. Whether you're generating images with sharp graphic design, stunning full-HD renders, or highly specific creative direction, it adheres closely to your prompts, renders text with accuracy, and supports a wide array of visual styles and aesthetics – from stylized concept art to crisp product mockups.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Terms and License | \[link](https://leonardo.ai/terms-of-service/) |

| Partner | Yes |

| Unit Pricing | $0.007 per 512 by 512 tile, $0.00013 per step |



\## Usage



Workers - TypeScript



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const inputs = {

&nbsp;     prompt: "cyberpunk cat",

&nbsp;   };





&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run(

&nbsp;     "@cf/leonardo/lucid-origin",

&nbsp;     inputs

&nbsp;   );





&nbsp;   return new Response(response, {

&nbsp;     headers: {

&nbsp;       "content-type": "image/jpg",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```

```sh
&nbsp; -d '{ "prompt": "cyberpunk cat" }'

```



\## Parameters

&nbsp; A text description of the image you want to generate.



\* `guidance` number default 4.5 min 0 max 10



&nbsp; Controls how closely the generated image should adhere to the prompt; higher values make the image more aligned with the prompt



\* `seed` integer min 0



&nbsp; Random seed for reproducibility of the image generation



\* `height` integer default 1120 min 0 max 2500



&nbsp; The height of the generated image in pixels



\* `width` integer default 1120 min 0 max 2500



&nbsp; The width of the generated image in pixels



\* `num\_steps` integer min 1 max 40



&nbsp; The number of diffusion steps; higher values can improve quality but take longer



\* `steps` integer min 1 max 40



&nbsp; The number of diffusion steps; higher values can improve quality but take longer



\### Output



\* `image` string



&nbsp; The generated image in Base64 format.

\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp; },

```

\# meta-llama-3-8b-instruct



Text Generation • meta-llama



@hf/meta-llama/meta-llama-3-8b-instruct



Generation over generation, Meta Llama 3 demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on a wide range of industry benchmarks and offers new capabilities, including improved reasoning.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 8,192 tokens |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@hf/meta-llama/meta-llama-3-8b-instruct)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@hf/meta-llama/meta-llama-3-8b-instruct", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@hf/meta-llama/meta-llama-3-8b-instruct", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@hf/meta-llama/meta-llama-3-8b-instruct",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@hf/meta-llama/meta-llama-3-8b-instruct \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```

\* `0` object

&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.

&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



\### Output



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `response` string required



&nbsp;   The generated text response from the model



&nbsp; \* `usage` object



&nbsp;   Usage statistics for the inference request



&nbsp;   \* `prompt\_tokens` number 0



&nbsp;     Total number of tokens in input



&nbsp;   \* `completion\_tokens` number 0



&nbsp;     Total number of tokens in output



&nbsp;   \* `total\_tokens` number 0



&nbsp;     Total number of input and output tokens



&nbsp; \* `tool\_calls` array



&nbsp;   An array of tool calls requests made during the response generation



&nbsp;   \* `items` object



&nbsp;     \* `arguments` object



&nbsp;       The arguments passed to be passed to the tool call request



&nbsp;     \* `name` string



&nbsp;       The name of the tool to be called



\* `1` string

\# mistral-7b-instruct-v0.1-awq Beta



Text Generation • thebloke



@hf/thebloke/mistral-7b-instruct-v0.1-awq



Mistral 7B Instruct v0.1 AWQ is an efficient, accurate and blazing-fast low-bit weight quantized Mistral variant.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Deprecated | 10/1/2025 |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 4,096 tokens |

| More information | \[link](https://huggingface.co/TheBloke/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.1-AWQ) |

| Beta | Yes |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@hf/thebloke/mistral-7b-instruct-v0.1-awq)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@hf/thebloke/mistral-7b-instruct-v0.1-awq", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@hf/thebloke/mistral-7b-instruct-v0.1-awq", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@hf/thebloke/mistral-7b-instruct-v0.1-awq",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@hf/thebloke/mistral-7b-instruct-v0.1-awq \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```

&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



\### Output



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `response` string required



&nbsp;   The generated text response from the model



&nbsp; \* `usage` object



&nbsp;   Usage statistics for the inference request



&nbsp;   \* `prompt\_tokens` number 0



&nbsp;     Total number of tokens in input



&nbsp;   \* `completion\_tokens` number 0



&nbsp;     Total number of tokens in output



&nbsp;   \* `total\_tokens` number 0



&nbsp;     Total number of input and output tokens



&nbsp; \* `tool\_calls` array



&nbsp;   An array of tool calls requests made during the response generation



&nbsp;   \* `items` object



&nbsp;     \* `arguments` object



&nbsp;       The arguments passed to be passed to the tool call request



&nbsp;     \* `name` string



&nbsp;       The name of the tool to be called



\* `1` string

\# mistral-7b-instruct-v0.2 Beta



Text Generation • MistralAI



@hf/mistral/mistral-7b-instruct-v0.2



The Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 Large Language Model (LLM) is an instruct fine-tuned version of the Mistral-7B-v0.2. Mistral-7B-v0.2 has the following changes compared to Mistral-7B-v0.1: 32k context window (vs 8k context in v0.1), rope-theta = 1e6, and no Sliding-Window Attention.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 3,072 tokens |

| More information | \[link](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2) |

| LoRA | Yes |

| Beta | Yes |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@hf/mistral/mistral-7b-instruct-v0.2)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@hf/mistral/mistral-7b-instruct-v0.2", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@hf/mistral/mistral-7b-instruct-v0.2", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@hf/mistral/mistral-7b-instruct-v0.2",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@hf/mistral/mistral-7b-instruct-v0.2 \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```

Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



\* `1` object



&nbsp; \* `messages` array required



&nbsp;   An array of message objects representing the conversation history.



&nbsp;   \* `items` object



&nbsp;     \* `role` string required



&nbsp;       The role of the message sender (e.g., 'user', 'assistant', 'system', 'tool').



&nbsp;     \* `content` string required



&nbsp;       The content of the message as a string.

&nbsp;   \* `items` object



&nbsp;     \* `name` string required



&nbsp;     \* `code` string required



&nbsp; \* `tools` array



&nbsp;   A list of tools available for the assistant to use.



&nbsp;   \* `items` one of



&nbsp;     \* `0` object



&nbsp;       \* `name` string required



&nbsp;         The name of the tool. More descriptive the better.

&nbsp;         A brief description of what the tool does.

&nbsp;         Schema defining the parameters accepted by the tool.

&nbsp;       \* `function` object required



&nbsp;         Details of the function tool.



&nbsp;         \* `name` string required



&nbsp;           The name of the function.



&nbsp;         \* `description` string required



&nbsp;           A brief description of what the function does.



&nbsp;         \* `parameters` object required



&nbsp;           Schema defining the parameters accepted by the function.



&nbsp;           \* `type` string required



&nbsp;             The type of the parameters object (usually 'object').



&nbsp;           \* `required` array



&nbsp;             List of required parameter names.



&nbsp;             \* `items` string



&nbsp;           \* `properties` object required



&nbsp;             Definitions of each parameter.



&nbsp;             \* `additionalProperties` object



&nbsp;               \* `type` string required



&nbsp;                 The data type of the parameter.



&nbsp;               \* `description` string required



&nbsp;                 A description of the expected parameter.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



\### Output



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `response` string required



&nbsp;   The generated text response from the model



&nbsp; \* `usage` object



&nbsp;   Usage statistics for the inference request



&nbsp;   \* `prompt\_tokens` number 0



&nbsp;     Total number of tokens in input



&nbsp;   \* `completion\_tokens` number 0



&nbsp;     Total number of tokens in output



&nbsp;   \* `total\_tokens` number 0



&nbsp;     Total number of input and output tokens



&nbsp; \* `tool\_calls` array



&nbsp;   An array of tool calls requests made during the response generation



&nbsp;   \* `items` object



&nbsp;     \* `arguments` object



&nbsp;       The arguments passed to be passed to the tool call request



&nbsp;     \* `name` string



&nbsp;       The name of the tool to be called



\* `1` string
