\# mistral-7b-instruct-v0.2-lora Beta



Text Generation • MistralAI



@cf/mistral/mistral-7b-instruct-v0.2-lora



The Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 Large Language Model (LLM) is an instruct fine-tuned version of the Mistral-7B-v0.2.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 15,000 tokens |

| LoRA | Yes |

| Beta | Yes |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/mistral/mistral-7b-instruct-v0.2-lora)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/mistral/mistral-7b-instruct-v0.2-lora", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/mistral/mistral-7b-instruct-v0.2-lora", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/mistral/mistral-7b-instruct-v0.2-lora",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/mistral/mistral-7b-instruct-v0.2-lora \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



\* `1` object

&nbsp;   An array of message objects representing the conversation history.

&nbsp;             List of required parameter names.

&nbsp;                 The data type of the parameter.

&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.

\# mistral-small-3.1-24b-instruct



Text Generation • MistralAI



@cf/mistralai/mistral-small-3.1-24b-instruct



Building upon Mistral Small 3 (2501), Mistral Small 3.1 (2503) adds state-of-the-art vision understanding and enhances long context capabilities up to 128k tokens without compromising text performance. With 24 billion parameters, this model achieves top-tier capabilities in both text and vision tasks.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 128,000 tokens |

| Function calling\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/function-calling) | Yes |

| Unit Pricing | $0.35 per M input tokens, $0.56 per M output tokens |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/mistralai/mistral-small-3.1-24b-instruct)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/mistralai/mistral-small-3.1-24b-instruct", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/mistralai/mistral-small-3.1-24b-instruct", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/mistralai/mistral-small-3.1-24b-instruct",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/mistralai/mistral-small-3.1-24b-instruct \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `guided\_json` object



&nbsp;   JSON schema that should be fulfilled for the response.



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.15 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



\* `1` object



&nbsp; \* `messages` array required



&nbsp;   An array of message objects representing the conversation history.



&nbsp;   \* `items` object



&nbsp;     \* `role` string



&nbsp;       The role of the message sender (e.g., 'user', 'assistant', 'system', 'tool').



&nbsp;     \* `tool\_call\_id` string



&nbsp;       The tool call id. Must be supplied for tool calls for Mistral-3. If you don't know what to put here you can fall back to 000000001



&nbsp;     \* `content` one of

&nbsp;               \* `description` string required



&nbsp;                 A description of the expected parameter.



&nbsp; \* `guided\_json` object



&nbsp;   JSON schema that should be fufilled for the response.



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.15 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.

\# neural-chat-7b-v3-1-awq Beta



Text Generation • thebloke



@hf/thebloke/neural-chat-7b-v3-1-awq



This model is a fine-tuned 7B parameter LLM on the Intel Gaudi 2 processor from the mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1 on the open source dataset Open-Orca/SlimOrca.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Deprecated | 10/1/2025 |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 4,096 tokens |

| Beta | Yes |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@hf/thebloke/neural-chat-7b-v3-1-awq)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@hf/thebloke/neural-chat-7b-v3-1-awq", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@hf/thebloke/neural-chat-7b-v3-1-awq", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@hf/thebloke/neural-chat-7b-v3-1-awq",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@hf/thebloke/neural-chat-7b-v3-1-awq \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.

!\[Deepgram logo](https://developers.cloudflare.com/\_astro/deepgram.DVGPhlbc.svg)



\# nova-3



Automatic Speech Recognition • Deepgram



@cf/deepgram/nova-3



Transcribe audio using Deepgram’s speech-to-text model



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Terms and License | \[link](https://deepgram.com/terms) |

| Batch | Yes |

| Partner | Yes |

| Real-time | Yes |

| Unit Pricing | $0.0052 per audio minute, $0.0092 per audio minute (websocket) |



Note



The \[pricing of this model](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/platform/pricing) is different based on transport. Transport-based pricing does not apply to all models.



\* WebSocket: $0.0092 per audio minute output (836.36 neurons per audio minute output)

\* Regular HTTP: $0.0052 per audio minute output (472.73 neurons per audio minute output)



\## Usage



Worker



```ts

export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env, ctx): Promise<Response> {

&nbsp;   const URL = "https://URL\_TO\_MP3\_FILE/audio.mp3";

&nbsp;   const mp3 = await fetch(URL);









&nbsp;   const resp = await env.AI.run("@cf/deepgram/nova-3", {

&nbsp;     "audio": {

&nbsp;       body: mp3.body,

&nbsp;       contentType: "audio/mpeg"

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;     "detect\_language": true

&nbsp;   }, {

&nbsp;     returnRawResponse: true

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp;   return resp;

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



curl



```sh

curl --request POST   --url 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/deepgram/nova-3?detect\_language=true'   --header 'Authorization: Bearer {TOKEN}'   --header 'Content-Type: audio/mpeg'   --data-binary "@/path/to/your-mp3-file.mp3"

```



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `audio` object required



&nbsp; \* `body` object required



&nbsp; \* `contentType` string required



\* `custom\_topic\_mode` string



&nbsp; Sets how the model will interpret strings submitted to the custom\\\_topic param. When strict, the model will only return topics submitted using the custom\\\_topic param. When extended, the model will return its own detected topics in addition to those submitted using the custom\\\_topic param.



\* `custom\_topic` string



&nbsp; Custom topics you want the model to detect within your input audio or text if present Submit up to 100



\* `custom\_intent\_mode` string



&nbsp; Sets how the model will interpret intents submitted to the custom\\\_intent param. When strict, the model will only return intents submitted using the custom\\\_intent param. When extended, the model will return its own detected intents in addition those submitted using the custom\\\_intents param



\* `custom\_intent` string



&nbsp; Custom intents you want the model to detect within your input audio if present



\* `detect\_entities` boolean



&nbsp; Identifies and extracts key entities from content in submitted audio



\* `detect\_language` boolean



&nbsp; Identifies the dominant language spoken in submitted audio



\* `diarize` boolean



&nbsp; Recognize speaker changes. Each word in the transcript will be assigned a speaker number starting at 0



\* `dictation` boolean



&nbsp; Identify and extract key entities from content in submitted audio



\* `encoding` string



&nbsp; Specify the expected encoding of your submitted audio



\* `extra` string



&nbsp; Arbitrary key-value pairs that are attached to the API response for usage in downstream processing



\* `filler\_words` boolean



&nbsp; Filler Words can help transcribe interruptions in your audio, like 'uh' and 'um'



\* `keyterm` string



&nbsp; Key term prompting can boost or suppress specialized terminology and brands.



\* `keywords` string



&nbsp; Keywords can boost or suppress specialized terminology and brands.



\* `language` string



&nbsp; The BCP-47 language tag that hints at the primary spoken language. Depending on the Model and API endpoint you choose only certain languages are available.



\* `measurements` boolean



&nbsp; Spoken measurements will be converted to their corresponding abbreviations.



\* `mip\_opt\_out` boolean



&nbsp; Opts out requests from the Deepgram Model Improvement Program. Refer to our Docs for pricing impacts before setting this to true. https\\://dpgr.am/deepgram-mip.



\* `mode` string



&nbsp; Mode of operation for the model representing broad area of topic that will be talked about in the supplied audio



\* `multichannel` boolean



&nbsp; Transcribe each audio channel independently.



\* `numerals` boolean



&nbsp; Numerals converts numbers from written format to numerical format.



\* `paragraphs` boolean



&nbsp; Splits audio into paragraphs to improve transcript readability.



\* `profanity\_filter` boolean



&nbsp; Profanity Filter looks for recognized profanity and converts it to the nearest recognized non-profane word or removes it from the transcript completely.



\* `punctuate` boolean



&nbsp; Add punctuation and capitalization to the transcript.



\* `redact` string



&nbsp; Redaction removes sensitive information from your transcripts.



\* `replace` string



&nbsp; Search for terms or phrases in submitted audio and replaces them.



\* `search` string



&nbsp; Search for terms or phrases in submitted audio.



\* `sentiment` boolean



&nbsp; Recognizes the sentiment throughout a transcript or text.



\* `smart\_format` boolean



&nbsp; Apply formatting to transcript output. When set to true, additional formatting will be applied to transcripts to improve readability.



\* `topics` boolean



&nbsp; Detect topics throughout a transcript or text.



\* `utterances` boolean



&nbsp; Segments speech into meaningful semantic units.



\* `utt\_split` number



&nbsp; Seconds to wait before detecting a pause between words in submitted audio.



\* `channels` number



&nbsp; The number of channels in the submitted audio



\* `interim\_results` boolean



&nbsp; Specifies whether the streaming endpoint should provide ongoing transcription updates as more audio is received. When set to true, the endpoint sends continuous updates, meaning transcription results may evolve over time. Note: Supported only for webosockets.



\* `endpointing` string



&nbsp; Indicates how long model will wait to detect whether a speaker has finished speaking or pauses for a significant period of time. When set to a value, the streaming endpoint immediately finalizes the transcription for the processed time range and returns the transcript with a speech\\\_final parameter set to true. Can also be set to false to disable endpointing



\* `vad\_events` boolean



&nbsp; Indicates that speech has started. You'll begin receiving Speech Started messages upon speech starting. Note: Supported only for webosockets.



\* `utterance\_end\_ms` boolean



&nbsp; Indicates how long model will wait to send an UtteranceEnd message after a word has been transcribed. Use with interim\\\_results. Note: Supported only for webosockets.

\# openchat-3.5-0106 Beta



Text Generation • openchat



@cf/openchat/openchat-3.5-0106



OpenChat is an innovative library of open-source language models, fine-tuned with C-RLFT - a strategy inspired by offline reinforcement learning.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Deprecated | 10/1/2025 |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 8,192 tokens |

| More information | \[link](https://huggingface.co/openchat/openchat-3.5-0106) |

| Beta | Yes |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/openchat/openchat-3.5-0106)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/openchat/openchat-3.5-0106", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/openchat/openchat-3.5-0106", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/openchat/openchat-3.5-0106",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/openchat/openchat-3.5-0106 \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



\* `1` object

&nbsp;   An array of message objects representing the conversation history.



&nbsp;   \* `items` object

\# openhermes-2.5-mistral-7b-awq Beta



Text Generation • thebloke



@hf/thebloke/openhermes-2.5-mistral-7b-awq



OpenHermes 2.5 Mistral 7B is a state of the art Mistral Fine-tune, a continuation of OpenHermes 2 model, which trained on additional code datasets.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Deprecated | 10/1/2025 |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 4,096 tokens |

| Beta | Yes |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@hf/thebloke/openhermes-2.5-mistral-7b-awq)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@hf/thebloke/openhermes-2.5-mistral-7b-awq", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@hf/thebloke/openhermes-2.5-mistral-7b-awq", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@hf/thebloke/openhermes-2.5-mistral-7b-awq",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@hf/thebloke/openhermes-2.5-mistral-7b-awq \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string

&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.

&nbsp;     \* `arguments` object



&nbsp;       The arguments passed to be passed to the tool call request



&nbsp;     \* `name` string



&nbsp;       The name of the tool to be called



\* `1` string

!\[Microsoft logo](https://developers.cloudflare.com/\_astro/microsoft.BfW2Sks3.svg)



\# phi-2 Beta



Text Generation • Microsoft



@cf/microsoft/phi-2



Phi-2 is a Transformer-based model with a next-word prediction objective, trained on 1.4T tokens from multiple passes on a mixture of Synthetic and Web datasets for NLP and coding.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 2,048 tokens |

| More information | \[link](https://huggingface.co/microsoft/phi-2) |

| Beta | Yes |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/microsoft/phi-2)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/microsoft/phi-2", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/microsoft/phi-2", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/microsoft/phi-2",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/microsoft/phi-2 \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.

\# phoenix-1.0



Text-to-Image • Leonardo



@cf/leonardo/phoenix-1.0



Phoenix 1.0 is a model by Leonardo.Ai that generates images with exceptional prompt adherence and coherent text.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Terms and License | \[link](https://leonardo.ai/terms-of-service/) |

| Partner | Yes |

| Unit Pricing | $0.0058 per 512 by 512 tile, $0.00011 per step |



\## Usage



Workers - TypeScript



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const inputs = {

&nbsp;     prompt: "cyberpunk cat",

&nbsp;   };





&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run(

&nbsp;     "@cf/leonardo/phoenix-1.0",

&nbsp;     inputs

&nbsp;   );





&nbsp;   return new Response(response, {

&nbsp;     headers: {

&nbsp;       "content-type": "image/jpg",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/leonardo/phoenix-1.0  \\

&nbsp; -X POST  \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_API\_TOKEN"  \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "prompt": "cyberpunk cat" }'

```



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp; A text description of the image you want to generate.



\* `guidance` number default 2 min 2 max 10



&nbsp; Controls how closely the generated image should adhere to the prompt; higher values make the image more aligned with the prompt



\* `seed` integer min 0



&nbsp; Random seed for reproducibility of the image generation



\* `height` integer default 1024 min 0 max 2048



&nbsp; The height of the generated image in pixels



\* `width` integer default 1024 min 0 max 2048



&nbsp; The width of the generated image in pixels



\* `num\_steps` integer default 25 min 1 max 50



&nbsp; The number of diffusion steps; higher values can improve quality but take longer



\* `negative\_prompt` string min 1



&nbsp; Specify what to exclude from the generated images



\### Output



The binding returns a `ReadableStream` with the image in JPEG or PNG format (check the model's output schema).



\## API Schemas



The following schemas are based on JSON Schema



\* Input



&nbsp; ```json

&nbsp;     "type": "object",

&nbsp;     "properties": {

&nbsp;         "prompt": {

&nbsp;             "type": "string",

&nbsp;             "minLength": 1,

&nbsp;             "description": "A text description of the image you want to generate."

&nbsp;         },

&nbsp;         "guidance": {

&nbsp;             "type": "number",

&nbsp;             "default": 2,

&nbsp;             "minimum": 2,

&nbsp;             "maximum": 10,

&nbsp;             "description": "Controls how closely the generated image should adhere to the prompt; higher values make the image more aligned with the prompt"

&nbsp;         },

&nbsp;         "seed": {

&nbsp;             "type": "integer",

&nbsp;             "minimum": 0,

&nbsp;             "description": "Random seed for reproducibility of the image generation"

&nbsp;         },

&nbsp;         "height": {

&nbsp;             "type": "integer",

&nbsp;             "minimum": 0,

&nbsp;             "maximum": 2048,

&nbsp;             "default": 1024,

&nbsp;             "description": "The height of the generated image in pixels"

&nbsp;         },

&nbsp;         "width": {

&nbsp;             "type": "integer",

&nbsp;             "minimum": 0,

&nbsp;             "maximum": 2048,

&nbsp;             "default": 1024,

&nbsp;             "description": "The width of the generated image in pixels"

&nbsp;         },

&nbsp;         "num\_steps": {

&nbsp;             "type": "integer",

&nbsp;             "default": 25,

&nbsp;             "minimum": 1,

&nbsp;             "maximum": 50,

&nbsp;             "description": "The number of diffusion steps; higher values can improve quality but take longer"

&nbsp;         },

&nbsp;         "negative\_prompt": {

&nbsp;             "minLength": 1,

&nbsp;             "description": "Specify what to exclude from the generated images"

\# plamo-embedding-1b



Text Embeddings • pfnet



@cf/pfnet/plamo-embedding-1b



PLaMo-Embedding-1B is a Japanese text embedding model developed by Preferred Networks, Inc. It can convert Japanese text input into numerical vectors and can be used for a wide range of applications, including information retrieval, text classification, and clustering.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Unit Pricing | $0.019 per M input tokens |



\## Usage



Workers - TypeScript



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   // Can be a string or array of strings]

&nbsp;   const stories = \[

&nbsp;     "This is a story about an orange cloud",

&nbsp;     "This is a story about a llama",

&nbsp;     "This is a story about a hugging emoji",

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const embeddings = await env.AI.run(

&nbsp;     "@cf/pfnet/plamo-embedding-1b",

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       text: stories,

&nbsp;     }

&nbsp;   );





&nbsp;   return Response.json(embeddings);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests









ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





stories = \[

&nbsp; 'This is a story about an orange cloud',

&nbsp; 'This is a story about a llama',

&nbsp; 'This is a story about a hugging emoji'

]





response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/pfnet/plamo-embedding-1b",

&nbsp; headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp; json={"text": stories}

)





print(response.json())

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/pfnet/plamo-embedding-1b  \\

&nbsp; -X POST  \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_API\_TOKEN"  \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "text": \["This is a story about an orange cloud", "This is a story about a llama", "This is a story about a hugging emoji"] }'

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `text` one of required



&nbsp; \* `0` string



&nbsp;   Input text to embed. Can be a single string or a list of strings.



&nbsp; \* `1` array



&nbsp;   Input text to embed. Can be a single string or a list of strings.



&nbsp;   \* `items` string



\### Output



\* `data` array required



&nbsp; Embedding vectors, where each vector is a list of floats.



&nbsp; \* `items` array



&nbsp;   \* `items` number



\* `shape` array required



&nbsp; Shape of the embedding data as \\\[number\\\_of\\\_embeddings, embedding\\\_dimension].



&nbsp; \* `items` integer



\## API Schemas



The following schemas are based on JSON Schema



\* Input



&nbsp; ```json

&nbsp; {

&nbsp;     "type": "object",

&nbsp;     "properties": {

&nbsp;         "text": {

&nbsp;             "oneOf": \[

&nbsp;                 {

&nbsp;                     "type": "string"

&nbsp;                 },

&nbsp;                 {

&nbsp;                     "type": "array",

&nbsp;                     "items": {

&nbsp;                         "type": "string"

&nbsp;                     }

\# qwen1.5-0.5b-chat Beta



Text Generation • Qwen



@cf/qwen/qwen1.5-0.5b-chat



Qwen1.5 is the improved version of Qwen, the large language model series developed by Alibaba Cloud.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Deprecated | 10/1/2025 |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 32,000 tokens |

| More information | \[link](https://huggingface.co/qwen/qwen1.5-0.5b-chat) |

| Beta | Yes |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/qwen/qwen1.5-0.5b-chat)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/qwen/qwen1.5-0.5b-chat", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/qwen/qwen1.5-0.5b-chat", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/qwen/qwen1.5-0.5b-chat",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/qwen/qwen1.5-0.5b-chat \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



\* `1` object



&nbsp; \* `messages` array required



&nbsp;   An array of message objects representing the conversation history.



&nbsp;   \* `items` object



&nbsp;     \* `role` string required



&nbsp;       The role of the message sender (e.g., 'user', 'assistant', 'system', 'tool').



&nbsp;     \* `content` string required



&nbsp;       The content of the message as a string.

&nbsp;     \* `name` string required



&nbsp;     \* `code` string required



&nbsp; \* `tools` array



&nbsp;   A list of tools available for the assistant to use.



&nbsp;   \* `items` one of



&nbsp;     \* `0` object



&nbsp;       \* `name` string required



&nbsp;         The name of the tool. More descriptive the better.



&nbsp;       \* `description` string required



&nbsp;         A brief description of what the tool does.



&nbsp;       \* `parameters` object required

\# qwen1.5-1.8b-chat Beta



Text Generation • Qwen



@cf/qwen/qwen1.5-1.8b-chat



Qwen1.5 is the improved version of Qwen, the large language model series developed by Alibaba Cloud.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Deprecated | 10/1/2025 |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 32,000 tokens |

| More information | \[link](https://huggingface.co/qwen/qwen1.5-1.8b-chat) |

| Beta | Yes |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/qwen/qwen1.5-1.8b-chat)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/qwen/qwen1.5-1.8b-chat", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/qwen/qwen1.5-1.8b-chat", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/qwen/qwen1.5-1.8b-chat",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/qwen/qwen1.5-1.8b-chat \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



\* `1` object



&nbsp; \* `messages` array required



&nbsp;   An array of message objects representing the conversation history.



&nbsp;   \* `items` object



&nbsp;     \* `role` string required



&nbsp;       The role of the message sender (e.g., 'user', 'assistant', 'system', 'tool').

\# qwen1.5-14b-chat-awq Beta



Text Generation • Qwen



@cf/qwen/qwen1.5-14b-chat-awq



Qwen1.5 is the improved version of Qwen, the large language model series developed by Alibaba Cloud. AWQ is an efficient, accurate and blazing-fast low-bit weight quantization method, currently supporting 4-bit quantization.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Deprecated | 10/1/2025 |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 7,500 tokens |

| More information | \[link](https://huggingface.co/qwen/qwen1.5-14b-chat-awq) |

| Beta | Yes |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/qwen/qwen1.5-14b-chat-awq)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/qwen/qwen1.5-14b-chat-awq", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/qwen/qwen1.5-14b-chat-awq", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/qwen/qwen1.5-14b-chat-awq",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/qwen/qwen1.5-14b-chat-awq \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

```

Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



\* `1` object

!\[Qwen logo](https://developers.cloudflare.com/\_astro/qwen.B8ST\_F2H.svg)



\# qwen2.5-coder-32b-instruct



Text Generation • Qwen



@cf/qwen/qwen2.5-coder-32b-instruct



Qwen2.5-Coder is the latest series of Code-Specific Qwen large language models (formerly known as CodeQwen). As of now, Qwen2.5-Coder has covered six mainstream model sizes, 0.5, 1.5, 3, 7, 14, 32 billion parameters, to meet the needs of different developers. Qwen2.5-Coder brings the following improvements upon CodeQwen1.5:



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 32,768 tokens |

| LoRA | Yes |

| Unit Pricing | $0.66 per M input tokens, $1.00 per M output tokens |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/qwen/qwen2.5-coder-32b-instruct)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/qwen/qwen2.5-coder-32b-instruct", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/qwen/qwen2.5-coder-32b-instruct", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/qwen/qwen2.5-coder-32b-instruct",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/qwen/qwen2.5-coder-32b-instruct \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

```

Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.

\# qwen1.5-7b-chat-awq Beta



Text Generation • Qwen



@cf/qwen/qwen1.5-7b-chat-awq



Qwen1.5 is the improved version of Qwen, the large language model series developed by Alibaba Cloud. AWQ is an efficient, accurate and blazing-fast low-bit weight quantization method, currently supporting 4-bit quantization.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Deprecated | 10/1/2025 |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 20,000 tokens |

| More information | \[link](https://huggingface.co/qwen/qwen1.5-7b-chat-awq) |

| Beta | Yes |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/qwen/qwen1.5-7b-chat-awq)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/qwen/qwen1.5-7b-chat-awq", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/qwen/qwen1.5-7b-chat-awq", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/qwen/qwen1.5-7b-chat-awq",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/qwen/qwen1.5-7b-chat-awq \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.
