\# qwen3-30b-a3b-fp8



Text Generation • Qwen



@cf/qwen/qwen3-30b-a3b-fp8



Qwen3 is the latest generation of large language models in Qwen series, offering a comprehensive suite of dense and mixture-of-experts (MoE) models. Built upon extensive training, Qwen3 delivers groundbreaking advancements in reasoning, instruction-following, agent capabilities, and multilingual support.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 32,768 tokens |

| Function calling\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/function-calling) | Yes |

| Batch | Yes |

| Unit Pricing | $0.051 per M input tokens, $0.34 per M output tokens |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/qwen/qwen3-30b-a3b-fp8)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/qwen/qwen3-30b-a3b-fp8", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/qwen/qwen3-30b-a3b-fp8", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/qwen/qwen3-30b-a3b-fp8",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl

&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 2000



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.

&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.

&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.

\# qwen3-embedding-0.6b



Text Embeddings • Qwen



@cf/qwen/qwen3-embedding-0.6b



The Qwen3 Embedding model series is the latest proprietary model of the Qwen family, specifically designed for text embedding and ranking tasks.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Unit Pricing | $0.012 per M input tokens |



\## Usage



Workers - TypeScript



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   // Can be a string or array of strings]

&nbsp;   const stories = \[

&nbsp;     "This is a story about an orange cloud",

&nbsp;     "This is a story about a llama",

&nbsp;     "This is a story about a hugging emoji",

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const embeddings = await env.AI.run(

&nbsp;     "@cf/qwen/qwen3-embedding-0.6b",

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       text: stories,

&nbsp;     }

&nbsp;   );





&nbsp;   return Response.json(embeddings);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests









ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





stories = \[

&nbsp; 'This is a story about an orange cloud',

&nbsp; 'This is a story about a llama',

&nbsp; 'This is a story about a hugging emoji'

]





response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/qwen/qwen3-embedding-0.6b",

&nbsp; headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp; json={"text": stories}

)





print(response.json())

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/qwen/qwen3-embedding-0.6b  \\

&nbsp; -X POST  \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_API\_TOKEN"  \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "text": \["This is a story about an orange cloud", "This is a story about a llama", "This is a story about a hugging emoji"] }'

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `queries` one of



&nbsp; \* `0` string min 1



&nbsp;   A single query string



&nbsp; \* `1` array



&nbsp;   An array of query strings



&nbsp;   \* `items` string min 1



\* `instruction` string default Given a web search query, retrieve relevant passages that answer the query



&nbsp; Optional instruction for the task



\* `documents` one of



&nbsp; \* `0` string min 1



&nbsp;   A single document string



&nbsp; \* `1` array



&nbsp;   An array of document strings



&nbsp;   \* `items` string min 1



\* `text` one of



&nbsp; \* `0` string min 1



&nbsp;   Alias for documents: a single text string



&nbsp; \* `1` array



&nbsp;   Alias for documents: an array of text strings



&nbsp;   \* `items` string min 1



\### Output



\* `data` array



&nbsp; \* `items` array



&nbsp;   \* `items` number



\* `shape` array



&nbsp; \* `items` integer

!\[Qwen logo](https://developers.cloudflare.com/\_astro/qwen.B8ST\_F2H.svg)



\# qwq-32b



Text Generation • Qwen



@cf/qwen/qwq-32b



QwQ is the reasoning model of the Qwen series. Compared with conventional instruction-tuned models, QwQ, which is capable of thinking and reasoning, can achieve significantly enhanced performance in downstream tasks, especially hard problems. QwQ-32B is the medium-sized reasoning model, which is capable of achieving competitive performance against state-of-the-art reasoning models, e.g., DeepSeek-R1, o1-mini.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 24,000 tokens |

| LoRA | Yes |

| Unit Pricing | $0.66 per M input tokens, $1.00 per M output tokens |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/qwen/qwq-32b)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/qwen/qwq-32b", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker

OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `guided\_json` object



&nbsp;   JSON schema that should be fulfilled for the response.



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.15 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



\* `1` object



&nbsp; \* `messages` array required



&nbsp;   An array of message objects representing the conversation history.



&nbsp;   \* `items` object



&nbsp;     \* `role` string



&nbsp;       The role of the message sender (e.g., 'user', 'assistant', 'system', 'tool').



&nbsp;     \* `tool\_call\_id` string



&nbsp;       The tool call id. Must be supplied for tool calls for Mistral-3. If you don't know what to put here you can fall back to 000000001



&nbsp;     \* `content` one of



&nbsp;       \* `0` string



&nbsp;         The content of the message as a string.



&nbsp;       \* `1` array



&nbsp;         \* `items` object



&nbsp;           \* `type` string



&nbsp;             Type of the content provided



&nbsp;           \* `text` string



&nbsp;           \* `image\_url` object



&nbsp;             \* `url` string



&nbsp;               image uri with data (e.g. data:image/jpeg;base64,/9j/...). HTTP URL will not be accepted



&nbsp;       \* `2` object



&nbsp;         \* `type` string



&nbsp;           Type of the content provided



&nbsp;         \* `text` string



&nbsp;         \* `image\_url` object



&nbsp;           \* `url` string



&nbsp;             image uri with data (e.g. data:image/jpeg;base64,/9j/...). HTTP URL will not be accepted



&nbsp; \* `functions` array



&nbsp;   \* `items` object



&nbsp;     \* `name` string required



&nbsp;     \* `code` string required



&nbsp; \* `tools` array



&nbsp;   A list of tools available for the assistant to use.



&nbsp;   \* `items` one of



&nbsp;     \* `0` object



&nbsp;       \* `name` string required



&nbsp;         The name of the tool. More descriptive the better.



&nbsp;       \* `description` string required



&nbsp;         A brief description of what the tool does.



&nbsp;       \* `parameters` object required



&nbsp;         Schema defining the parameters accepted by the tool.



&nbsp;         \* `type` string required



&nbsp;           The type of the parameters object (usually 'object').



&nbsp;         \* `required` array



&nbsp;           List of required parameter names.



&nbsp;           \* `items` string



&nbsp;         \* `properties` object required



&nbsp;           Definitions of each parameter.



&nbsp;           \* `additionalProperties` object



&nbsp;             \* `type` string required



&nbsp;               The data type of the parameter.

&nbsp;               A description of the expected parameter.



&nbsp;     \* `1` object



&nbsp;       \* `type` string required



&nbsp;         Specifies the type of tool (e.g., 'function').



&nbsp;       \* `function` object required



&nbsp;         Details of the function tool.



&nbsp;         \* `name` string required



&nbsp;           The name of the function.

&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.15 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



\### Output



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `response` string required



&nbsp;   The generated text response from the model



&nbsp; \* `usage` object



&nbsp;   Usage statistics for the inference request



&nbsp;   \* `prompt\_tokens` number 0



&nbsp;     Total number of tokens in input



&nbsp;   \* `completion\_tokens` number 0



&nbsp;     Total number of tokens in output



&nbsp;   \* `total\_tokens` number 0



&nbsp;     Total number of input and output tokens



&nbsp; \* `tool\_calls` array



&nbsp;   An array of tool calls requests made during the response generation



&nbsp;   \* `items` object



&nbsp;     \* `arguments` object



&nbsp;       The arguments passed to be passed to the tool call request



&nbsp;     \* `name` string



&nbsp;       The name of the tool to be called



\* `1` string

!\[Microsoft logo](https://developers.cloudflare.com/\_astro/microsoft.BfW2Sks3.svg)



\# resnet-50



Image Classification • Microsoft



@cf/microsoft/resnet-50



50 layers deep image classification CNN trained on more than 1M images from ImageNet



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| More information | \[link](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/microsoft-vision-model-resnet-50-combines-web-scale-data-and-multi-task-learning-to-achieve-state-of-the-art/) |

| Unit Pricing | $0.0000025 per inference request |



\## Usage



Workers - TypeScript



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {

&nbsp;   const res = await fetch("https://cataas.com/cat");

&nbsp;   const blob = await res.arrayBuffer();





&nbsp;   const inputs = {

&nbsp;     image: \[...new Uint8Array(blob)],

&nbsp;   };





&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run(

&nbsp;     "@cf/microsoft/resnet-50",

&nbsp;     inputs

&nbsp;   );





&nbsp;   return new Response(JSON.stringify(response));

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/microsoft/resnet-50  \\

&nbsp;   -X POST  \\

&nbsp;   -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_API\_TOKEN"  \\

&nbsp;   --data-binary "@orange-llama.png"

```



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` string



&nbsp; The image to classify



\* `1` object



&nbsp; \* `image` array required



&nbsp;   An array of integers that represent the image data constrained to 8-bit unsigned integer values



&nbsp;   \* `items` number



&nbsp;     A value between 0 and 255 (unsigned 8bit)



\### Output



\* `items` object



&nbsp; \* `score` number



&nbsp;   A confidence value, between 0 and 1, indicating how certain the model is about the predicted label



&nbsp; \* `label` string



&nbsp;   The predicted category or class for the input image based on analysis



\## API Schemas



The following schemas are based on JSON Schema



\* Input



&nbsp; ```json

&nbsp; {

&nbsp;     "oneOf": \[

&nbsp;         {

&nbsp;             "type": "string",

&nbsp;             "format": "binary",

&nbsp;             "description": "The image to classify"

&nbsp;         },

&nbsp;         {

&nbsp;             "type": "object",

&nbsp;             "properties": {

&nbsp;                 "image": {

&nbsp;                     "type": "array",

&nbsp;                     "description": "An array of integers that represent the image data constrained to 8-bit unsigned integer values",

&nbsp;                     "items": {

&nbsp;                         "type": "number",

&nbsp;                         "description": "A value between 0 and 255 (unsigned 8bit)"

&nbsp;                     }

&nbsp;                 }

&nbsp;             },

&nbsp;             "required": \[

&nbsp;                 "image"

&nbsp;             ]

&nbsp;         }

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* Output



&nbsp; ```json

&nbsp; {

&nbsp;     "type": "array",

&nbsp;     "contentType": "application/json",

&nbsp;     "items": {

&nbsp;         "type": "object",

&nbsp;         "properties": {

&nbsp;             "score": {

&nbsp;                 "type": "number",

&nbsp;                 "description": "A confidence value, between 0 and 1, indicating how certain the model is about the predicted label"

&nbsp;             },

&nbsp;             "label": {

&nbsp;                 "type": "string",

&nbsp;                 "description": "The predicted category or class for the input image based on analysis"

&nbsp;             }

&nbsp;         }

&nbsp;     }

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```

\# smart-turn-v2



Voice Activity Detection • pipecat-ai



@cf/pipecat-ai/smart-turn-v2



An open source, community-driven, native audio turn detection model in 2nd version



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Batch | Yes |

| Real-time | Yes |

| Unit Pricing | $0.00034 per audio minute |



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `audio` object required



&nbsp;   readable stream with audio data and content-type specified for that data



&nbsp;   \* `body` object required



&nbsp;   \* `contentType` string required



&nbsp; \* `dtype` string



&nbsp;   type of data PCM data that's sent to the inference server as raw array



\* `1` object



&nbsp; \* `audio` string required



&nbsp;   base64 encoded audio data



&nbsp; \* `dtype` string



&nbsp;   type of data PCM data that's sent to the inference server as raw array



\### Output



\* `is\_complete` boolean



&nbsp; if true, end-of-turn was detected



\* `probability` number



&nbsp; probability of the end-of-turn detection

\# sqlcoder-7b-2 Beta



Text Generation • defog



@cf/defog/sqlcoder-7b-2



This model is intended to be used by non-technical users to understand data inside their SQL databases.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 10,000 tokens |

| Terms and License | \[link](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/deed.en) |

| More information | \[link](https://huggingface.co/defog/sqlcoder-7b-2) |

| Beta | Yes |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/defog/sqlcoder-7b-2)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/defog/sqlcoder-7b-2", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/defog/sqlcoder-7b-2", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/defog/sqlcoder-7b-2",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/defog/sqlcoder-7b-2 \\

```

Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.

\# stable-diffusion-v1-5-img2img Beta



Text-to-Image • runwayml



@cf/runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5-img2img



Stable Diffusion is a latent text-to-image diffusion model capable of generating photo-realistic images. Img2img generate a new image from an input image with Stable Diffusion.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Terms and License | \[link](https://github.com/runwayml/stable-diffusion/blob/main/LICENSE) |

| More information | \[link](https://huggingface.co/runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5) |

| Beta | Yes |

| Unit Pricing | $0.00 per step |



\## Usage



Workers - TypeScript



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   // Picture of a dog

&nbsp;   const exampleInputImage = await fetch(

&nbsp;     "https://pub-1fb693cb11cc46b2b2f656f51e015a2c.r2.dev/dog.png"

&nbsp;   );





&nbsp;   const inputs = {

&nbsp;     prompt: "Change to a lion",

&nbsp;     image: \[...new Uint8Array(await exampleInputImage.arrayBuffer())],

&nbsp;   };





&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run(

&nbsp;     "@cf/runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5-img2img",

&nbsp;     inputs

&nbsp;   );





&nbsp;   return new Response(response, {

&nbsp;     headers: {

&nbsp;       "content-type": "image/png",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5-img2img  \\

&nbsp; -X POST  \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_API\_TOKEN"  \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "prompt": "cyberpunk cat" }'

```



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp; A text description of the image you want to generate



\* `negative\_prompt` string



&nbsp; Text describing elements to avoid in the generated image



\* `height` integer min 256 max 2048



&nbsp; The height of the generated image in pixels



\* `width` integer min 256 max 2048



&nbsp; The width of the generated image in pixels



\* `image` array



&nbsp; For use with img2img tasks. An array of integers that represent the image data constrained to 8-bit unsigned integer values



&nbsp; \* `items` number



&nbsp;   A value between 0 and 255



\* `image\_b64` string



&nbsp; For use with img2img tasks. A base64-encoded string of the input image



\* `mask` array



&nbsp; An array representing An array of integers that represent mask image data for inpainting constrained to 8-bit unsigned integer values



&nbsp; \* `items` number



&nbsp;   A value between 0 and 255



\* `num\_steps` integer default 20 max 20



&nbsp; The number of diffusion steps; higher values can improve quality but take longer



\* `strength` number default 1



&nbsp; A value between 0 and 1 indicating how strongly to apply the transformation during img2img tasks; lower values make the output closer to the input image



\* `guidance` number default 7.5



&nbsp; Controls how closely the generated image should adhere to the prompt; higher values make the image more aligned with the prompt



\* `seed` integer



&nbsp; Random seed for reproducibility of the image generation



\### Output



The binding returns a `ReadableStream` with the image in JPEG or PNG format (check the model's output schema).

Text-to-Image • runwayml



@cf/runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5-inpainting



Stable Diffusion Inpainting is a latent text-to-image diffusion model capable of generating photo-realistic images given any text input, with the extra capability of inpainting the pictures by using a mask.



| Model Info | |

```ts
&nbsp;     "https://pub-1fb693cb11cc46b2b2f656f51e015a2c.r2.dev/dog.png"

&nbsp;   );





&nbsp;   // Mask of dog

&nbsp;   const exampleMask = await fetch(

&nbsp;     "https://pub-1fb693cb11cc46b2b2f656f51e015a2c.r2.dev/dog-mask.png"

&nbsp;   );





&nbsp;   const inputs = {

&nbsp;     prompt: "Change to a lion",

&nbsp;     image: \[...new Uint8Array(await exampleInputImage.arrayBuffer())],

&nbsp;     mask: \[...new Uint8Array(await exampleMask.arrayBuffer())],

&nbsp;   };





&nbsp;   const response =

&nbsp;     await env.AI.run(

&nbsp;       "@cf/runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5-inpainting",

&nbsp;       inputs

&nbsp;     );





&nbsp;   return new Response(response, {

&nbsp;     headers: {

&nbsp;       "content-type": "image/png",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;
```

&nbsp; The number of diffusion steps; higher values can improve quality but take longer



\* `strength` number default 1



&nbsp; A value between 0 and 1 indicating how strongly to apply the transformation during img2img tasks; lower values make the output closer to the input image



\* `guidance` number default 7.5



&nbsp; Controls how closely the generated image should adhere to the prompt; higher values make the image more aligned with the prompt



\* `seed` integer



&nbsp; Random seed for reproducibility of the image generation



\### Output



The binding returns a `ReadableStream` with the image in JPEG or PNG format (check the model's output schema).

\# starling-lm-7b-beta Beta



Text Generation • nexusflow



@hf/nexusflow/starling-lm-7b-beta



We introduce Starling-LM-7B-beta, an open large language model (LLM) trained by Reinforcement Learning from AI Feedback (RLAIF). Starling-LM-7B-beta is trained from Openchat-3.5-0106 with our new reward model Nexusflow/Starling-RM-34B and policy optimization method Fine-Tuning Language Models from Human Preferences (PPO).



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Deprecated | 10/1/2025 |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 4,096 tokens |

| More information | \[link](https://huggingface.co/Nexusflow/Starling-LM-7B-beta) |

| Beta | Yes |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@hf/nexusflow/starling-lm-7b-beta)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@hf/nexusflow/starling-lm-7b-beta", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@hf/nexusflow/starling-lm-7b-beta", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@hf/nexusflow/starling-lm-7b-beta",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@hf/nexusflow/starling-lm-7b-beta \\

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters

\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string

&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.

&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2

&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.

\# tinyllama-1.1b-chat-v1.0 Beta



Text Generation • tinyllama



@cf/tinyllama/tinyllama-1.1b-chat-v1.0



The TinyLlama project aims to pretrain a 1.1B Llama model on 3 trillion tokens. This is the chat model finetuned on top of TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-intermediate-step-1431k-3T.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Deprecated | 10/1/2025 |

| Context Window\[](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/glossary/) | 2,048 tokens |

| More information | \[link](https://huggingface.co/TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0) |

| Beta | Yes |



\## Playground



Try out this model with Workers AI LLM Playground. It does not require any setup or authentication and an instant way to preview and test a model directly in the browser.



\[Launch the LLM Playground](https://playground.ai.cloudflare.com/?model=@cf/tinyllama/tinyllama-1.1b-chat-v1.0)



\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@cf/tinyllama/tinyllama-1.1b-chat-v1.0", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Worker



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/tinyllama/tinyllama-1.1b-chat-v1.0", { messages });





&nbsp;   return Response.json(response);

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



Python



```py

import os

import requests





ACCOUNT\_ID = "your-account-id"

AUTH\_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN")





prompt = "Tell me all about PEP-8"

response = requests.post(

&nbsp; f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT\_ID}/ai/run/@cf/tinyllama/tinyllama-1.1b-chat-v1.0",

&nbsp;   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH\_TOKEN}"},

&nbsp;   json={

&nbsp;     "messages": \[

&nbsp;       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant"},

&nbsp;       {"role": "user", "content": prompt}

&nbsp;     ]

&nbsp;   }

)

result = response.json()

print(result)

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/tinyllama/tinyllama-1.1b-chat-v1.0 \\

&nbsp; -X POST \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_AUTH\_TOKEN" \\

&nbsp; -d '{ "messages": \[{ "role": "system", "content": "You are a friendly assistant" }, { "role": "user", "content": "Why is pizza so good" }]}'

```



OpenAI compatible endpoints



Workers AI also supports OpenAI compatible API endpoints for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. For more details, refer to \[Configurations ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/open-ai-compatibility/).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` object



&nbsp; \* `prompt` string required min 1



&nbsp;   The input text prompt for the model to generate a response.



&nbsp; \* `lora` string



&nbsp;   Name of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model to fine-tune the base model.



&nbsp; \* `response\_format` object



&nbsp;   \* `type` string



&nbsp;   \* `json\_schema`



&nbsp; \* `raw` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, a chat template is not applied and you must adhere to the specific model's expected formatting.



&nbsp; \* `stream` boolean



&nbsp;   If true, the response will be streamed back incrementally using SSE, Server Sent Events.



&nbsp; \* `max\_tokens` integer default 256



&nbsp;   The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.



&nbsp; \* `temperature` number default 0.6 min 0 max 5



&nbsp;   Controls the randomness of the output; higher values produce more random results.



&nbsp; \* `top\_p` number min 0.001 max 1



&nbsp;   Adjusts the creativity of the AI's responses by controlling how many possible words it considers. Lower values make outputs more predictable; higher values allow for more varied and creative responses.



&nbsp; \* `top\_k` integer min 1 max 50



&nbsp;   Limits the AI to choose from the top 'k' most probable words. Lower values make responses more focused; higher values introduce more variety and potential surprises.



&nbsp; \* `seed` integer min 1 max 9999999999



&nbsp;   Random seed for reproducibility of the generation.



&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number min 0 max 2



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.



&nbsp; \* `frequency\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number min -2 max 2



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.



\* `1` object



&nbsp; \* `messages` array required



&nbsp;   An array of message objects representing the conversation history.



&nbsp;   \* `items` object



&nbsp;     \* `role` string required



&nbsp;       The role of the message sender (e.g., 'user', 'assistant', 'system', 'tool').



&nbsp;     \* `content` string required



&nbsp;       The content of the message as a string.

&nbsp;   \* `items` object



&nbsp;     \* `name` string required



&nbsp;     \* `code` string required



&nbsp; \* `tools` array



&nbsp;   A list of tools available for the assistant to use.



&nbsp;   \* `items` one of



&nbsp;     \* `0` object



&nbsp;       \* `name` string required



&nbsp;         The name of the tool. More descriptive the better.



&nbsp;       \* `description` string required



&nbsp;         A brief description of what the tool does.



&nbsp;       \* `parameters` object required



&nbsp;         Schema defining the parameters accepted by the tool.

\# uform-gen2-qwen-500m Beta



Image-to-Text • unum



@cf/unum/uform-gen2-qwen-500m



UForm-Gen is a small generative vision-language model primarily designed for Image Captioning and Visual Question Answering. The model was pre-trained on the internal image captioning dataset and fine-tuned on public instructions datasets: SVIT, LVIS, VQAs datasets.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| More information | \[link](https://www.unum.cloud/) |

| Beta | Yes |



\## Usage



Workers - TypeScript



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}









export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request: Request, env: Env): Promise<Response> {

&nbsp;   const res = await fetch("https://cataas.com/cat");

&nbsp;   const blob = await res.arrayBuffer();

&nbsp;   const input = {

&nbsp;     image: \[...new Uint8Array(blob)],

&nbsp;     prompt: "Generate a caption for this image",

&nbsp;     max\_tokens: 512,

&nbsp;   };

&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run(

&nbsp;     "@cf/unum/uform-gen2-qwen-500m",

&nbsp;     input

&nbsp;     );

&nbsp;   return new Response(JSON.stringify(response));

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```

&nbsp; \* `repetition\_penalty` number



&nbsp;   Penalty for repeated tokens; higher values discourage repetition.

&nbsp;   Decreases the likelihood of the model repeating the same lines verbatim.



&nbsp; \* `presence\_penalty` number



&nbsp;   Increases the likelihood of the model introducing new topics.

```ts

}

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;
```

!\[OpenAI logo](https://developers.cloudflare.com/\_astro/openai.ChTKThcR.svg)



\# whisper



Automatic Speech Recognition • OpenAI



@cf/openai/whisper



Whisper is a general-purpose speech recognition model. It is trained on a large dataset of diverse audio and is also a multitasking model that can perform multilingual speech recognition, speech translation, and language identification.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| More information | \[link](https://openai.com/research/whisper) |

| Unit Pricing | $0.00045 per audio minute |



\## Usage



Workers - TypeScript



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {

&nbsp;   const res = await fetch(

&nbsp;     "https://github.com/Azure-Samples/cognitive-services-speech-sdk/raw/master/samples/cpp/windows/console/samples/enrollment\_audio\_katie.wav"

&nbsp;   );

&nbsp;   const blob = await res.arrayBuffer();





&nbsp;   const input = {

&nbsp;     audio: \[...new Uint8Array(blob)],

&nbsp;   };





&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run(

&nbsp;     "@cf/openai/whisper",

&nbsp;     input

&nbsp;   );





&nbsp;   return Response.json({ input: { audio: \[] }, response });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/openai/whisper  \\

&nbsp; -X POST  \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_API\_TOKEN"  \\

&nbsp; --data-binary "@talking-llama.mp3"

```



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `0` string



\* `1` object



&nbsp; \* `audio` array required



&nbsp;   An array of integers that represent the audio data constrained to 8-bit unsigned integer values



&nbsp;   \* `items` number



&nbsp;     A value between 0 and 255



\### Output



\* `text` string required



&nbsp; The transcription



\* `word\_count` number



\* `words` array



&nbsp; \* `items` object



&nbsp;   \* `word` string



&nbsp;   \* `start` number



&nbsp;     The second this word begins in the recording



&nbsp;   \* `end` number



&nbsp;     The ending second when the word completes



\* `vtt` string

!\[OpenAI logo](https://developers.cloudflare.com/\_astro/openai.ChTKThcR.svg)



\# whisper-large-v3-turbo



Automatic Speech Recognition • OpenAI



@cf/openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo



Whisper is a pre-trained model for automatic speech recognition (ASR) and speech translation.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Unit Pricing | $0.00051 per audio minute |



\## Usage



Workers - TypeScript



```ts

import { Buffer } from 'node:buffer';

export interface Env {

&nbsp;   AI: Ai;

}

const URL = "https://pub-dbcf9f0bd3af47ca9d40971179ee62de.r2.dev/02f6edc0-1f7b-4272-bd17-f05335104725/audio.mp3";

export default {

&nbsp;   async fetch(request, env, ctx): Promise<Response> {

&nbsp;       const mp3 = await fetch(URL);

&nbsp;       if (!mp3.ok) {

&nbsp;         return Response.json({ error: `Failed to fetch MP3: ${mp3.status}` });

&nbsp;       }

&nbsp;       const mp3Buffer = await mp3.arrayBuffer();

&nbsp;       const base64 = Buffer.from(mp3Buffer, 'binary').toString("base64");

&nbsp;       try {

&nbsp;           const res = await env.AI.run("@cf/openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo", {

&nbsp;               "audio": base64

&nbsp;           });

&nbsp;           return Response.json(res);

&nbsp;       }

&nbsp;       catch (e) {

&nbsp;           console.error(e);

&nbsp;           return Response.json({ error: "An unexpected error occurred" });

&nbsp;       }

&nbsp;   },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>

```



Note



To enable built-in Node.js APIs and polyfills, add the nodejs\\\_compat compatibility flag to your \[Wrangler configuration file](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/configuration/). This also enables nodejs\\\_compat\\\_v2 as long as your compatibility date is 2024-09-23 or later. \[Learn more about the Node.js compatibility flag and v2](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/compatibility-flags/#nodejs-compatibility-flag).



\## Parameters



\\\* indicates a required field



\### Input



\* `audio` string required



&nbsp; Base64 encoded value of the audio data.



\* `task` string default transcribe



&nbsp; Supported tasks are 'translate' or 'transcribe'.



\* `language` string



&nbsp; The language of the audio being transcribed or translated.



\* `vad\_filter` boolean



&nbsp; Preprocess the audio with a voice activity detection model.



\* `initial\_prompt` string



&nbsp; A text prompt to help provide context to the model on the contents of the audio.



\* `prefix` string



&nbsp; The prefix it appended the the beginning of the output of the transcription and can guide the transcription result.



\### Output



\* `transcription\_info` object



&nbsp; \* `language` string



&nbsp;   The language of the audio being transcribed or translated.



&nbsp; \* `language\_probability` number



&nbsp;   The confidence level or probability of the detected language being accurate, represented as a decimal between 0 and 1.



&nbsp; \* `duration` number



&nbsp;   The total duration of the original audio file, in seconds.



&nbsp; \* `duration\_after\_vad` number



&nbsp;   The duration of the audio after applying Voice Activity Detection (VAD) to remove silent or irrelevant sections, in seconds.



\* `text` string required



&nbsp; The complete transcription of the audio.



\* `word\_count` number



&nbsp; The total number of words in the transcription.



\* `segments` array



&nbsp; \* `items` object



&nbsp;   \* `start` number



&nbsp;     The starting time of the segment within the audio, in seconds.



&nbsp;   \* `end` number



&nbsp;     The ending time of the segment within the audio, in seconds.



&nbsp;   \* `text` string



&nbsp;     The transcription of the segment.



&nbsp;   \* `temperature` number



&nbsp;     The temperature used in the decoding process, controlling randomness in predictions. Lower values result in more deterministic outputs.



&nbsp;   \* `avg\_logprob` number



&nbsp;     The average log probability of the predictions for the words in this segment, indicating overall confidence.



&nbsp;   \* `compression\_ratio` number



&nbsp;     The compression ratio of the input to the output, measuring how much the text was compressed during the transcription process.



&nbsp;   \* `no\_speech\_prob` number



&nbsp;     The probability that the segment contains no speech, represented as a decimal between 0 and 1.



&nbsp;   \* `words` array



&nbsp;     \* `items` object



&nbsp;       \* `word` string



&nbsp;         The individual word transcribed from the audio.



&nbsp;       \* `start` number



&nbsp;         The starting time of the word within the audio, in seconds.



&nbsp;       \* `end` number



&nbsp;         The ending time of the word within the audio, in seconds.



\* `vtt` string



&nbsp; The transcription in WebVTT format, which includes timing and text information for use in subtitles.

\# whisper-tiny-en Beta



Automatic Speech Recognition • OpenAI



@cf/openai/whisper-tiny-en



Whisper is a pre-trained model for automatic speech recognition (ASR) and speech translation. Trained on 680k hours of labelled data, Whisper models demonstrate a strong ability to generalize to many datasets and domains without the need for fine-tuning. This is the English-only version of the Whisper Tiny model which was trained on the task of speech recognition.



| Model Info | |

| - | - |

| Beta | Yes |



\## Usage



Workers - TypeScript



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {

&nbsp;   const res = await fetch(

&nbsp;     "https://github.com/Azure-Samples/cognitive-services-speech-sdk/raw/master/samples/cpp/windows/console/samples/enrollment\_audio\_katie.wav"

&nbsp;   );

&nbsp;   const blob = await res.arrayBuffer();





&nbsp;   const input = {

&nbsp;     audio: \[...new Uint8Array(blob)],

&nbsp;   };





&nbsp;   const response = await env.AI.run(

&nbsp;     "@cf/openai/whisper-tiny-en",

&nbsp;     input

&nbsp;   );





&nbsp;   return Response.json({ input: { audio: \[] }, response });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```



curl



```sh

curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE\_ACCOUNT\_ID/ai/run/@cf/openai/whisper-tiny-en  \\

&nbsp; -X POST  \\

&nbsp; -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE\_API\_TOKEN"  \\

&nbsp; --data-binary "@talking-llama.mp3"

```

&nbsp;     The second this word begins in the recording



&nbsp;   \* `end` number

\* `vtt` string

Text Generation • thebloke

Zephyr 7B Beta AWQ is an efficient, accurate and blazing-fast low-bit weight quantized Zephyr model variant.

\## Usage



Worker - Streaming



```ts

export interface Env {

&nbsp; AI: Ai;

}





export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env): Promise<Response> {





&nbsp;   const messages = \[

&nbsp;     { role: "system", content: "You are a friendly assistant" },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       role: "user",

&nbsp;       content: "What is the origin of the phrase Hello, World",

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;   ];





&nbsp;   const stream = await env.AI.run("@hf/thebloke/zephyr-7b-beta-awq", {

&nbsp;     messages,

&nbsp;     stream: true,

&nbsp;   });





&nbsp;   return new Response(stream, {

&nbsp;     headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" },

&nbsp;   });

&nbsp; },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

```

title: Cloudflare Tunnel · Cloudflare Workers VPC

description: Cloudflare Tunnel creates secure connections from your

&nbsp; infrastructure to Cloudflare's global network, providing the network

&nbsp; connectivity that allows Workers to access your private resources.

lastUpdated: 2025-11-14T21:25:44.000Z

chatbotDeprioritize: false

source\_url:

&nbsp; html: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-vpc/configuration/tunnel/

&nbsp; md: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-vpc/configuration/tunnel/index.md

---



Cloudflare Tunnel creates secure connections from your infrastructure to Cloudflare's global network, providing the network connectivity that allows Workers to access your private resources.



When you create a VPC Service, you specify a tunnel ID and target service. Workers VPC then routes requests from your Worker to the specified tunnel, which establishes a connection to the specified hostname or IP address, such that the target service receives the request and returns a response back to your Worker.



To allow members to create VPC Services that represent a target service reachable via a tunnel, you must assign them the \*\*Connectivity Directory Admin\*\* role. Members must possess \*\*Connectivity Directory Bind\*\* role to bind to existing VPC Services from worker.



The tunnel maintains persistent connections to Cloudflare, eliminating the need for inbound firewall rules or public IP addresses.



Note



This section provides tunnel configuration specific to Workers VPC use cases. For comprehensive tunnel documentation including monitoring and advanced configurations, refer to the \[full Cloudflare Tunnel documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/).



\## Create and run tunnel (`cloudflared`)



Cloudflare Tunnel requires the installation of a lightweight and highly scalable server-side daemon, `cloudflared`, to connect your infrastructure to Cloudflare.



Version and Configuration



Ensure you are running `cloudflared` version 2025.7.0 or later (latest version recommended) to ensure proper DNS resolution and connectivity. Older versions are not supported.



Workers VPC also requires Cloudflare Tunnel to connect using the \[QUIC transport protocol](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/configure-tunnels/cloudflared-parameters/run-parameters/#protocol) using `auto` or `quic`. Ensure outbound UDP traffic on port 7844 is allowed through your firewall for QUIC connections.



Cloudflare Tunnels can be created one of two ways:



1\. \*\*Remotely-managed tunnels (recommended):\*\* Remotely-managed configurations are stored on Cloudflare, allowing you to manage the tunnel from any machine using the dashboard, API, or Terraform.

2\. \*\*Locally-managed tunnels:\*\* A locally-managed tunnel is created by running `cloudflared tunnel create <NAME>` on the command line. Tunnel configuration is stored in your local cloudflared directory.



For Workers VPC, we recommend creating a remotely-managed tunnel through the dashboard. Follow the \[Tunnels for Workers VPC dashboard setup guide](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-vpc/get-started/) to create your tunnel with provided installation commands shown in the dashboard.



For locally-managed tunnels, refer to the \[`cloudflared` locally-managed tunnels](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/do-more-with-tunnels/local-management/) guide. For manual installation, refer to the \[`cloudflared` downloads page](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/downloads/) for platform-specific installation instructions.



Note



Cloudflare Tunnels can either be configured for usage with \[Cloudflare Zero Trust](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/) or \[Workers VPC](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-vpc/).



Use Tunnels with Zero Trust when you are exposing internal applications securely to your employees with Cloudflare Access and hostnames.



Use Tunnels with Workers VPC when you want to access private APIs, private databases, internal services or other HTTP services within your cloud or on-premise private network from Workers.



The same `cloudflared` instance can be used to cover both Zero Trust and Workers VPC use cases simultaneously.



Note



\[Ingress configurations](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/do-more-with-tunnels/local-management/configuration-file/) for locally-managed tunnels are only relevant when using tunnels to expose services to the public internet, and are not required for Workers VPC as routing is handled by the VPC Service configuration.



\## Cloud platform setup guides



For platform-specific tunnel deployment instructions for production workloads:



\* \[AWS](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/deployment-guides/aws/) - Deploy tunnels in Amazon Web Services

\* \[Azure](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/deployment-guides/azure/) - Deploy tunnels in Microsoft Azure

\* \[Google Cloud](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/deployment-guides/google-cloud-platform/) - Deploy tunnels in Google Cloud Platform

\* \[Kubernetes](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/deployment-guides/kubernetes/) - Deploy tunnels in Kubernetes clusters

\* \[Terraform](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/deployment-guides/terraform/) - Deploy tunnels using Infrastructure as Code



Refer to the full Cloudflare Tunnel documentation on \[how to setup Tunnels for high availability and failover with replicas](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/configure-tunnels/tunnel-availability/).



Note



We do not recommend using `cloudflared` in autoscaling setups because downscaling (removing replicas) will break existing user connections to that replica. Additionally, `cloudflared` does not load balance across replicas; replicas are strictly for high availability and requests are routed to the nearest replica.



\## Next steps



\* Configure \[VPC Services](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-vpc/configuration/vpc-services/) to connect your tunnels to Workers

\* Review \[hardware requirements](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-vpc/configuration/tunnel/hardware-requirements/) for capacity planning

\* Review the \[complete Cloudflare Tunnel documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/) for advanced features



</page>



<page>

title: VPC Services · Cloudflare Workers VPC

description: VPC Services are the core building block of Workers VPC. They

&nbsp; represent specific resources in your private network that Workers can access

&nbsp; through Cloudflare Tunnel.

lastUpdated: 2026-01-29T10:38:24.000Z

chatbotDeprioritize: false

source\_url:

&nbsp; html: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-vpc/configuration/vpc-services/

&nbsp; md: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-vpc/configuration/vpc-services/index.md

---



VPC Services are the core building block of Workers VPC. They represent specific resources in your private network that Workers can access through Cloudflare Tunnel.



You can use bindings to connect to VPC Services from Workers. Every request made to a VPC Service using its `fetch` function will be securely routed to the configured service in the private network.



VPC Services enforce that requests are routed to their intended service without exposing the entire network, securing your workloads and preventing server-side request forgery (SSRF).



Members must possess \*\*Connectivity Directory Bind\*\* role to bind to existing VPC Services from Workers. Creating VPC Services requires members to possess the \*\*Connectivity Directory Admin\*\* role.



Note



Workers VPC is currently in beta. Features and APIs may change before general availability. While in beta, Workers VPC is available for free to all Workers plans.



\## VPC Service configuration



A VPC Service consists of:



\* \*\*Type\*\*: Currently only `http` is supported (support for `tcp` coming soon)

\* \*\*Tunnel ID\*\*: The Cloudflare Tunnel that provides network connectivity

\* \*\*Hostname or IPv4/IPv6 addresses\*\*: The hostname, or IPv4 and/or IPv6 addresses to use to route to your service from the tunnel in your private network

\* \*\*Ports\*\*: HTTP and/or HTTPS port configuration (optional, defaults to 80/443)

\* \*\*Resolver IPs\*\*: Optionally, a specific resolver IP can be provided -- when not provided, `cloudflared` will direct DNS traffic to the currently configured default system resolver.



Requests are encrypted in flight until they reach your network via a tunnel, regardless of the scheme used in the URL provided to `fetch`. If the `http` scheme is used, a plaintext connection is established to the service from the tunnel.



The `https` scheme can be used for an encrypted connection within your network, between the tunnel and your service. When the `https` scheme is specified, a hostname provided to the `fetch()` operation is utilized as the Server Name Indication (SNI) value.



VPC Services default to allowing both `http` and `https` schemes to be used. You can provide values for only one of `http\_port` or `https\_port` to enforce the use of a particular scheme.



When Workers VPC is unable to establish a connection to your service, `fetch()` will throw an exception.



Note



The \[VPC Service configuration](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-vpc/configuration/vpc-services/#vpc-service-configuration) host and port(s) will always be used to connect and route requests to your services, even if a different host or port is present in the URL provided to the `fetch()` operation in the Worker code.



The host provided in the `fetch()` operation is not used to route requests, and instead only populates the `Host` field for a HTTP request, or `Host` and the Server Name Indication (SNI) value presented to your service for a HTTPS request.



The port provided in the `fetch()` operation is ignored — the port specified in the VPC Service configuration for the provided scheme will be used.



\## Configuration example



The following is an example of a VPC Service for a service using custom HTTP and HTTPS ports, and both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. These configurations represent the expected contract of the \[REST API for creating a VPC Service](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/connectivity/subresources/directory/subresources/services/), a type of service within the broader connectivity directory.



```json

{

&nbsp; "type": "http",

&nbsp; "name": "human-readable-name",





&nbsp; // Port configuration (optional - defaults to 80/443)

&nbsp; "http\_port": 80,

&nbsp; "https\_port": 443,





&nbsp; // Host configuration

&nbsp; "host": {

&nbsp;   "ipv4": "10.0.0.1",

&nbsp;   "ipv6": "fe80::",

&nbsp;   "network": {

&nbsp;     "tunnel\_id": "0191dce4-9ab4-7fce-b660-8e5dec5172da"

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

}

```



The following is an example of a VPC Service for a service using custom HTTP and HTTPS ports as well, using a hostname. Note that since we are using a hostname, we must provide our service with a `resolver\_network` that optionally has `resolver\_ips`.



```json

{

&nbsp; "type": "http",

&nbsp; "name": "human-readable-name",





&nbsp; // Port configuration (optional - defaults to 80/443)

&nbsp; "http\_port": 80,

&nbsp; "https\_port": 443,





&nbsp; // Hostname Host (with DNS resolver)

&nbsp; "host": {

&nbsp;   "hostname": "example.com",

&nbsp;   "resolver\_network": {

&nbsp;     "tunnel\_id": "0191dce4-9ab4-7fce-b660-8e5dec5172da",

&nbsp;     "resolver\_ips": \["10.0.0.1"] // Optional

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; }

}

```



\## Workers binding configuration



Once you have created a VPC Service, you can bind it to your Worker:



\* wrangler.jsonc



&nbsp; ```jsonc

&nbsp; {

&nbsp;   "$schema": "./node\_modules/wrangler/config-schema.json",

&nbsp;   "name": "my-worker",

&nbsp;   "main": "src/index.js",

&nbsp;   "vpc\_services": \[

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       "binding": "PRIVATE\_API",

&nbsp;       "service\_id": "e6a0817c-79c5-40ca-9776-a1c019defe70",

&nbsp;       "remote": true // When true, utilizes \[remote bindings](/workers/development-testing/#remote-bindings) to allow access to the VPC Service during local development.

&nbsp;     }

&nbsp;   ]

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* wrangler.toml



&nbsp; ```toml

&nbsp; "$schema" = "./node\_modules/wrangler/config-schema.json"

&nbsp; name = "my-worker"

&nbsp; main = "src/index.js"





&nbsp; \[\[vpc\_services]]

&nbsp; binding = "PRIVATE\_API"

&nbsp; service\_id = "e6a0817c-79c5-40ca-9776-a1c019defe70"

&nbsp; remote = true

&nbsp; ```



You can have multiple VPC service bindings:



\* wrangler.jsonc



&nbsp; ```jsonc

&nbsp; {

&nbsp;   "vpc\_services": \[

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       "binding": "PRIVATE\_API",

&nbsp;       "service\_id": "daf43e8c-a81a-4242-9912-4a2ebe4fdd79",

&nbsp;       "remote": true

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       "binding": "PRIVATE\_DATABASE",

&nbsp;       "service\_id": "453b6067-1327-420d-89b3-2b6ad16e6551",

&nbsp;       "remote": true

&nbsp;     },

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       "binding": "INTERNAL\_CACHE",

&nbsp;       "service\_id": "6c39b574-237e-49f4-852a-cea5a93ed8f9",

&nbsp;       "remote": true

&nbsp;     }

&nbsp;   ]

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* wrangler.toml



&nbsp; ```toml

&nbsp; \[\[vpc\_services]]

&nbsp; binding = "PRIVATE\_API"

&nbsp; service\_id = "daf43e8c-a81a-4242-9912-4a2ebe4fdd79"

&nbsp; remote = true





&nbsp; \[\[vpc\_services]]

&nbsp; binding = "PRIVATE\_DATABASE"

&nbsp; service\_id = "453b6067-1327-420d-89b3-2b6ad16e6551"

&nbsp; remote = true





&nbsp; \[\[vpc\_services]]

&nbsp; binding = "INTERNAL\_CACHE"

&nbsp; service\_id = "6c39b574-237e-49f4-852a-cea5a93ed8f9"

&nbsp; remote = true

&nbsp; ```



\## Required roles



Workers VPC uses the following account roles:



\* `Connectivity Directory Read` to view Workers VPC Services and Tunnels.

\* `Connectivity Directory Bind` to list/read services and bind them in Workers.

\* `Connectivity Directory Admin` to create, update, and delete services.



For role definitions, refer to \[Roles](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/manage-members/roles/#account-scoped-roles).



If your roles were recently updated and commands are still failing, refresh Wrangler authentication:



```sh

npx wrangler logout

npx wrangler login

```



If you authenticate with an API token (`CLOUDFLARE\_API\_TOKEN`), ensure the token belongs to a user with the required roles.



\## Next steps



\* Set up \[Cloudflare Tunnel](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-vpc/configuration/tunnel/) for your environment

\* Learn about the \[Service Binding API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-vpc/api/)

\* Refer to \[examples](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-vpc/examples/) of common use cases



</page>

title: Access a private API or website · Cloudflare Workers VPC

description: This example demonstrates how to access a private REST API that is

&nbsp; not exposed to the public internet. In this guide, we will configure a VPC

&nbsp; Service for an internal API, create a Worker that makes requests to that API,

&nbsp; and deploy the Worker to validate our changes.

lastUpdated: 2026-02-02T18:38:11.000Z

chatbotDeprioritize: false

source\_url:

&nbsp; html: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-vpc/examples/private-api/

&nbsp; md: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-vpc/examples/private-api/index.md

---



This example demonstrates how to access a private REST API that is not exposed to the public internet. In this guide, we will configure a VPC Service for an internal API, create a Worker that makes requests to that API, and deploy the Worker to validate our changes.



\## Prerequisites



\* A virtual machine/EC2 instance running in your VPC/virtual network

\* A private API or website running in your VPC/virtual network with security rules allowing access to the virtual machine that will be running `cloudflared`

\* Workers account with Workers VPC access



\## 1. Set up Cloudflare Tunnel



A Cloudflare Tunnel creates a secure connection from your private network to Cloudflare. This tunnel will allow Workers to securely access your private resources.



1\. Navigate to the \[Workers VPC dashboard](https://dash.cloudflare.com/?to=/:account/workers/vpc/tunnels) and select the \*\*Tunnels\*\* tab.



2\. Select \*\*Create\*\* to create a new tunnel.



3\. Enter a name for your tunnel (for example, `private-api-tunnel`) and select \*\*Save tunnel\*\*.



4\. Choose your operating system and architecture. The dashboard will provide specific installation instructions for your environment.



5\. Follow the provided commands to download and install `cloudflared` on your VM, and execute the service installation command with your unique token.



The dashboard will confirm when your tunnel is successfully connected. Note the tunnel ID for the next step.



\## 2. Create the Workers VPC Service



First, create a Workers VPC Service for your internal API:



```bash

npx wrangler vpc service create api-service \\

&nbsp; --type http \\

&nbsp; --tunnel-id <YOUR\_TUNNEL\_ID> \\

&nbsp; --ipv4 10.0.1.50 \\

&nbsp; --http-port 8080

```



You can also create a VPC Service for a service using its hostname:



```bash

npx wrangler vpc service create api-service \\

&nbsp; --type http \\

&nbsp; --tunnel-id <YOUR\_TUNNEL\_ID> \\

&nbsp; --hostname internal-hostname.example.com

```



Note the service ID returned for the next step.



\## 3. Configure your Worker



Update your Wrangler configuration file:



\* wrangler.jsonc



&nbsp; ```jsonc

&nbsp; {

&nbsp;   "$schema": "./node\_modules/wrangler/config-schema.json",

&nbsp;   "name": "private-api-gateway",

&nbsp;   "main": "src/index.js",

&nbsp;   "compatibility\_date": "2026-02-04",

&nbsp;   "vpc\_services": \[

&nbsp;     {

&nbsp;       "binding": "INTERNAL\_API",

&nbsp;       "service\_id": "<YOUR\_SERVICE\_ID>",

&nbsp;       "remote": true

&nbsp;     }

&nbsp;   ]

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; ```



\* wrangler.toml



&nbsp; ```toml

&nbsp; "$schema" = "./node\_modules/wrangler/config-schema.json"

&nbsp; name = "private-api-gateway"

&nbsp; main = "src/index.js"

&nbsp; compatibility\_date = "2026-02-04"





&nbsp; \[\[vpc\_services]]

&nbsp; binding = "INTERNAL\_API"

&nbsp; service\_id = "<YOUR\_SERVICE\_ID>"

&nbsp; remote = true

&nbsp; ```



\## 4. Implement the Worker



In your Workers code, use the VPC Service binding in order to send requests to the service:



```js

export default {

&nbsp; async fetch(request, env, ctx) {

&nbsp;   try {

&nbsp;     // Fetch data from internal API and process it before returning

&nbsp;     const response = await env.INTERNAL\_API.fetch("http://10.0.1.50:8080/api/data");





&nbsp;     // Use the response of the private API to perform more logic in Workers, before returning the final response

&nbsp;     return response;

&nbsp;   } catch (error) {

&nbsp;     return new Response("Service unavailable", { status: 503 });

&nbsp;   }

&nbsp; },

};

```



This guide demonstrates how you could create a simple proxy in your Workers. However, you could use VPC Services to fetch APIs directly and manipulate the responses to enable you to build more full-stack and backend functionality on Workers.



\## 5. Deploy and test



Now, you can deploy and test your Worker that you have created:



```bash

npx wrangler deploy

```



```bash

\# Test GET request

curl https://private-api-gateway.workers.dev

```



\## Next steps



\* Add \[authentication and authorization](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/examples/auth-with-headers/)

\* Implement \[rate limiting](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/)
